state_program_name: Assisted Living Residence (ALR), Comprehensive Personal Care Home (CPCH) and Assisted Living Program (ALP), licensed by the NJ Department of Health under N.J.A.C. 8:36 after a Certificate of Need; Medicaid care services paid through NJ FamilyCare MLTSS managed care

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** organizes and operates its New Jersey assisted living services. The program types covered are an Assisted Living Residence (ALR), a Comprehensive Personal Care Home (CPCH) and an Assisted Living Program (ALP). Delete any that do not apply to **[AGENCY NAME]**. Each is licensed by the NJ Department of Health (DOH) under N.J.A.C. 8:36 after a Certificate of Need. Medicaid care services are paid through NJ FamilyCare MLTSS managed care.

The manual does the following:

- **Meets the licensure requirement.** N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7 requires a manual for organization and operation that is developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually, with each review documented. The manual must be available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times.
- **Gives staff one reference.** It tells staff what to do and who is responsible. Topics include resident rights, admission and discharge, care planning, medications, infection control, reporting of abuse and reportable events, staffing and training, confidentiality, and security.
- **Supports consistent, safe care.** Residents, families, guardians, designated responsible individuals, applicants, referring agencies and surveyors can see how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates and what it can and cannot provide.

The manual covers the policy content the rules require. It does not replace the regulations. If this manual and N.J.A.C. 8:36 ever conflict, the regulation controls, and the manual must be corrected promptly.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**1. Customize it first.** This manual is a template. Before use, replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and every other bracketed item with facts about your organization. These include the organizational chart and lines of authority, the services you can provide, your program type(s), your administrator, and local contacts. Delete sections that do not apply, such as ALP-only, CPCH-only or respite care provisions, only after confirming they do not apply to your license. Do not leave placeholder text in the adopted version.

**2. Adopt it formally.** The governing body of **[AGENCY NAME]** must review and adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the approver and the version in the manual's revision log.

**3. Keep it current.** N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7 requires a review at least annually, and each review must be documented. Resident care policies under N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1 must also be reviewed at the intervals the policies specify, with each review documented. Revise the manual whenever a regulation, a DOH or Medicaid requirement, a contact number, or your own operations change. Keep superseded versions in an archive.

**4. Train staff on it.** Every employee must be trained on the policies relevant to their role at hire and again whenever policies change. Keep signed acknowledgments and training records in personnel files. Training under this manual supplements the orientation and in-service training the regulations require, such as PCA orientation and in-service under N.J.A.C. 8:36-9.1 and dementia training under N.J.A.C. 8:36-19.3, where applicable.

**5. Keep it available.** Keep a complete, current copy at the facility, available to DOH representatives at all times. An ALP also keeps it at each program site and at the provider's main office. Under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(b), adopt a written policy stating how the manual is made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, applicants and referring agencies. Follow that policy.

**6. Use Appendix A to check compliance.** Appendix A maps every official item to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it to prepare for survey, to find the policy behind a regulatory requirement, and to confirm nothing is missing after a revision. If a row in Appendix A shows a gap, fix the gap before relying on the manual.

**7. Flag items needing verification.** Some regulatory text was not available when this manual was prepared. Examples are the full lists in N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a)(1)-(7) and (9)-(11), N.J.A.C. 8:36-18.3(a)(1)-(7), and the section-level text of N.J.A.C. 8:36-21. Before adoption, pull the current official text for these sections and confirm the manual's policies against it. Also confirm whether any pending DOH rule proposals have been adopted.

## Regulatory Framework

### Governing rules

The manual is built on the following authorities, cited exactly as they appear in the rules. The citations are grouped by subject.

**Manual, resident rights and reporting**
- **N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7** — Policy and procedure manual
- **N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1** — Resident care policies and procedures
- **N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a)** — Posting and distribution of statement of resident rights

- **N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11** — Notices
- **N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7** — Record of death (cross-referenced in 8:36-5.7(a)8; the text of 15.7 itself must be confirmed)

The chapter was readopted with technical changes and now expires in 2028. Section text should be checked against the current official code, because DOH may amend it. A 2026 proposal affecting N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3 and 8:36-2.4 (CPCH deemed status) has not been verified as adopted.

### Official policy checklist and application documents

I found no single DOH policy-review checklist or application packet for this license. The state reviews the manual against the following documents, and the manual is organized around them:

1. **N.J.A.C. 8:36 — Standards for Licensure of Assisted Living Residences, Comprehensive Personal Care Homes, and Assisted Living Programs.** The sections that list required written policies and procedures are 2.2, 4.1, 5.7, 5.10, 6.1, 11.7, 14.2, 18.3, 19.3 and 23.4. The core manual list is **N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)(1)-(8) and (b)**, which applies to ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs. The manual may be one document or several.
2. **N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2, Application for licensure (current text).** It governs the admission agreement and the application narratives that are policy or program content. The ALR/CPCH admission agreement goes to the Director of the CN&L Program for review. An ALP submits its resident agreement and its contract with the publicly subsidized housing unit.
3. **Notice of Readoption with Technical Changes, N.J.A.C. 8:36 (NJ DOH).** This is the official DOH PDF giving the chapter's subchapter structure and the revised text of several policy provisions.
4. **AAS-24 Affidavit of Compliance, Assisted Living Residences, Comprehensive Personal Care Homes and Assisted Living Programs** (NJ DOH, Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations). This is a supporting document only. It lists the mandatory standards the administrator attests to, including 6.1(a)1-11, written resident care policies and procedures. The full form was not reviewed, so no items are drawn from it.

**Appendix A** maps every official item in these documents to the specific policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use it as the working checklist for survey readiness. Gaps and cautions noted in preparing this manual:

- The verbatim lists in N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a)(1)-(7) and (9)-(11) and 8:36-18.3(a)(1)-(7) were not retrieved. Confirm them against the official text.
- The text of 8:36-14.2 (written emergency plans, which must be filed with DOH and updated when they change) came from a non-official transcription and should be checked.
- Sections 7.1, 10.x, 11.x, 20.x and 21.x were not fully reviewed for further written-policy requirements, such as respite care, restraints, quality improvement and dining. Add them to Appendix A when confirmed.

### Adoption, currency and training

This manual must be customized (replace all **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders), formally adopted by the governing body of **[AGENCY NAME]**, reviewed at least annually with each review documented, and kept current as rules change. All staff must be trained on it. Compliance is the responsibility of the administrator and the governing body.

citations.title: Policy and procedure manual
citations.requirement: Manual for organization and operation must be developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review is documented. The manual is available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times. It must include: (1) organizational chart showing lines of authority; (2) description of services the facility can provide; (3) security policies; (4) abuse/exploitation reporting to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770, plus the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995 if the resident is 60 or older; (5) confidentiality and release of records; (6) personnel records; (7) employee physicals, immunizations and TB testing; (8) prompt notification of a resident's death. Under (b), a policy must say how manuals are made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, applicants and referring agencies.

citations.title: Resident care policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written resident care policies must be established, implemented and reviewed at intervals the policies specify, with each review documented. They must include control of smoking under N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6 (subsection (a)8). Other required items (a)1-7 and 9-11 were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Posting and distribution of statement of resident rights
citations.requirement: Each provider must post and distribute a statement of resident rights to residents of ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs. Retrieved items: #27 confidential treatment of information; #37 written notice at least 30 days before a facility-requested transfer or discharge, except in an emergency, including the Ombudsman's name, address and phone, and also given to the guardian or, with consent, the family; #40 right to complain without threat or reprisal, with names, addresses and phones of complaint agencies (DOH and the State LTC Ombudsman) given to the resident, guardian and family member and posted conspicuously. The NJ Ombudsman rights summary also lists freedom from chemical and physical restraints and from physical and mental abuse and neglect.

citations.title: Reportable events
citations.requirement: Notify the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034, or (609) 392-2020 after business hours, followed by written confirmation within 72 hours, of: (1) termination of the administrator, with the replacement's name and qualifications; (2) any elopements; (3) suspected resident abuse or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman. The written notice goes to the Division.

citations.title: Admission and retention of residents
citations.requirement: (a) The administrator or designee interviews the resident (and family, guardian or agency if the resident agrees) at or before admission, covering policies, business hours, fees, services, resident rights and admission/discharge criteria, with the interview documented in the record. (b) Emergency-contact information is voluntary, and admission cannot be denied for declining it. (c) If a resident's behavior shows danger to self or others and the facility cannot provide proper care, the attending or on-call physician decides on placement and mental health screening is initiated under N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 10:31. (d) An applicant denied admission after a written application must, on written request, receive a signed written reason within 15 days of receipt of the request. (e) Infirmary transfer requires consent and is generally limited to one week.

citations.title: Involuntary discharge
citations.requirement: Written notice from the administrator to the resident and family, guardian or designee. Discharge only on grounds stated in the policies, of which the resident was informed in advance. Notice at least 30 days ahead, stating the reason and the right to appeal, with a copy in the record. The 30-day notice does not apply to discharge for reasons in 5.1(d). Emergency transfer for life safety is allowed without 30 days' notice, and DOH must be notified.

citations.title: Types of services provided to residents
citations.requirement: (a) Provide or coordinate personal care and services based on assessment by qualified persons, consistent with the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37. (b) Be capable of personal care, nursing, pharmacy, dining, activities, recreation and social work services. (c) Supervise self-administration and have trained, supervised staff administer medications. (d) Be capable of nursing services including nursing-home-level residents. A resident may, but need not, be moved if the record documents one of 8 characteristics (24/7 nursing supervision; bedridden over 14 days; totally dependent in 4 or more ADLs; severe cognitive decline; stage 3/4 or multiple stage 2 pressure sores; needs more than assistance with transfer; danger to self or others; unstable condition). A single stage 2 sore must be retained with a plan of care. (e) The admission agreement must say whether the facility will retain such residents, to what extent and at what added cost. (f) Residents needing specialized long-term care must be transferred. (h)-(l) A new ALR or CPCH licensed on or after 9/1/2001 must reach 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy within 3 years and maintain it. Added beds must be 10% Medicaid-occupied. With fewer than 10 beds, at least one bed is reserved. The Commissioner may waive or reduce the requirement, and must waive it if funding is limited.

citations.title: Minimum personal care assistant staffing
citations.requirement: On the premises at all times: at least one awake personal care assistant and at least one additional employee. With more than one free-standing building with residents, at least one PCA in each building, and both PCAs must then be awake. These levels are a minimum only. Staff must be sufficient in number and training based on an assessment of resident acuity.

citations.title: Qualifications of personal care assistants
citations.requirement: A PCA is a facility employee who completed a DOH-approved nurse aide course (N.J.A.C. 8:39-43) and passed the NJ Nurse Aide Certification Exam, or a DOH-approved PCA course and competency evaluation leading to PCA certification. PCA certification requires the criminal history background check under N.J.A.C. 8:43I. Certification is valid 2 years and renewal requires an updated check. Each PCA and direct caregiver gets orientation before or on employment and ongoing in-service on assisted living concepts. Under (m), a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation triggers DOH review and possible entry on the PCA abuse registry with a disciplinary hearing.

citations.title: Certified medication aides
citations.requirement: A certified medication aide must complete a DOH-approved medication administration course and pass a DOH-approved exam. Renewal is every 2 years with at least 10 hours of continuing education per period (5 hours on fundamentals of medication administration and 5 on drug use relevant to the elderly). A finding of abuse, neglect, misappropriation, negligence or incompetence can lead to the medication aide abuse registry. DOH gives notice with at least 30 days to request a hearing.

citations.title: Storage and control of medications
citations.requirement: The administrator provides a safe storage area for medications that are not self-administered (a locked medication cart is acceptable). Medications are stored per manufacturer or pharmacy directions and kept in original, labeled containers. Generic substitutes are labeled per N.J.A.C. 8:71. Needles and syringes are stored, used and disposed of per N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5.10 et seq., N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, N.J.A.C. 7:26-3A and 29 CFR 1910.1030, with a record of purchase, storage and disposal. Controlled dangerous substances follow N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq. Theft of scheduled or controlled substances is reported to the NJ Dept. of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742 and/or other authorities with jurisdiction.

citations.title: Development of infection control policies and procedures
citations.requirement: (c) Document annual influenza vaccination for each resident per the ACIP recommendations of 8/27/2021, unless contraindicated or refused. Vaccination of accepting residents is completed by November 30 each year. Residents admitted after that date, up to February 1, are vaccinated before or on admission as medically appropriate unless they refuse. (d) Document pneumococcal vaccination for residents 65 and older per ACIP (1/28/2011), or provide or arrange it before or on admission unless refused.

citations.title: General infection control policies and procedures
citations.requirement: Written infection prevention and control policies must be established and implemented. Needles and syringes that residents use in home self-care are disposed of per N.J.S.A. 2C:36-6.1 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7. Other required topics (18.3(a)1-7) were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Staff training program for Alzheimer's disease and dementia
citations.requirement: A facility that advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program must train all licensed and unlicensed staff who give direct care to residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, per N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. Copies of the mandatory training program are available from the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations on written request.

citations.title: Submission and availability of documents
citations.requirement: On request, the facility submits in writing any documents the chapter requires to the Director of the CN&L Program. On DOH request it also submits utilization, demographic, cost, charge and staffing data. The facility reports resident days for the prior calendar year to the CN&L Program by April 15 each year.

citations.title: Transfer of ownership
citations.requirement: Before ownership is transferred, the prospective new owner applies to the CN&L Program. After review DOH sends an approval letter with licensure forms and a fee request. Within 5 working days after the transaction closes, the applicant submits the required follow-up documents. The rule fee is $1,500 (see 8:36-2.2).

citations.title: Application for licensure
citations.requirement: A license application is made to the Commissioner after a Certificate of Need is received. The applicant forwards the ALR/CPCH admission agreement to the CN&L Program for review, to confirm it does not violate the chapter, CON conditions or State/Federal law. The application includes the commitment that at least 20% of residents will have nursing-home-level needs within 36 months of licensure. Fees are nonrefundable: $1,500 + $15 per bed initial and annual, $1,500 biennial inspection, $1,500 transfer of ownership, $375 relocation. Applicants may request a preliminary conference with the CN&L Program.

citations.title: Newly constructed or expanded facilities
citations.requirement: Plans go to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit for approval before construction. The license application includes the Unit's written final release. Before occupying a new or renovated building, the facility submits a local certificate of occupancy to the Unit and further items to the CN&L Program.

citations.title: Surveys
citations.requirement: DOH's Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations surveys once the written application is approved and the building is ready. A license issues after a preliminary conference and submission of local zoning, fire, health and building approvals plus a certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy. No resident may be admitted before written DOH approval or a license, and violators face penalties under N.J.S.A. 26:2H-14 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-1.

citations.title: Surrender of license
citations.requirement: Notify each resident, the resident's physician and guarantors of payment at least 30 days before voluntary surrender of a license, or as directed under an order of revocation, non-renewal or suspension. Return the license to the CN&L Program within 7 working days.

citations.title: Waiver
citations.requirement: A facility seeking a waiver of the chapter applies in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program. 8:36-5.1(l)2 uses this process for waiver of the 10% Medicaid occupancy requirement.

citations.title: Advertisement of assisted living
citations.requirement: Only facilities licensed as ALRs or CPCHs may describe and offer themselves to the public as providing assisted living services.

citations.title: Qualifications of the administrator
citations.requirement: The administrator must be at least 21, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and hold a current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification. A qualified owner may serve. Candidates sit the competency exam within two years of the training course and complete a criminal background check. Renewal requires at least 30 hours of CE on assisted living topics earned within the certificate period, and a background check. The certificate runs 3 years.

citations.title: Actions against an assisted living administrator
citations.requirement: An administrator's certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted for improper practice. Improper practice includes a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property of a resident of an ALR, CPCH or ALP, or of a patient, resident or client of any other DOH-licensed facility or agency.

citations.title: Notices
citations.requirement: Conspicuously post a notice that specified information is available in the facility during business hours to residents and the public. The posted information includes the DOH toll-free hotline, county agency phone numbers and the State LTC Ombudsman number (#6). The other items (#1-5, #7) were not shown in the text retrieved.

citations.title: Health care assessment and health service plan
citations.requirement: (a) Within 30 days before admission, a physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant states in writing that the resident is appropriate for this level of care. At admission, the administrator and resident arrange the physician and dentist to call. (c) If the initial assessment shows health care needs, an RN completes a health care assessment within 14 days of admission, using the DOH instrument or an equivalent. (d) The assessment covers ADLs, cognition, communication/hearing, vision, physical functioning, continence, psychosocial well-being, mood and behavior, and activity patterns. (e) A written health service plan is developed from the assessment.

citations.title: Initial assessments and resident service plans
citations.requirement: Upon admission, each resident receives an initial assessment by a registered professional nurse to determine the resident's needs (text as quoted in a DOH survey citation). Text of 7.1(b)-(f), including the general service plan timeline, was not retrieved from the official code.

citations.title: Nursing services (registered nurse availability)
citations.requirement: Per the fact-checked research: at least one registered professional nurse must be available at all times, and each resident receives an RN assessment and care plan. What 'available' means for coverage and response time must be confirmed with DOH.

citations.title: Supplemental Security Income recipients (CPCH)
citations.requirement: Each CPCH must annually have at least 5% of residents be SSI-eligible, at least half of them former psychiatric patients. The percentage is computed on resident days per calendar year and reported to the CN&L Program by April 15 for the prior year.

citations.title: Assisted living program service provider requirements
citations.requirement: ALP services must be delivered only inside a licensed ALR, CPCH or publicly subsidized housing (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Notices (ALP)
citations.requirement: The ALP provider and each program site post a notice that specified information is available at the site and at the provider's main office. It includes the DOH hotline, county senior-services agency numbers and the State LTC Ombudsman number.

citations.title: Notification requirements (ALP)
citations.requirement: With the resident's consent, notify the family, guardian or designated person promptly of specified events. These include any serious accident, criminal act or incident causing serious harm or injury, or the resident's arrest or detention, in which case the CN&L Program is also notified in writing. The ALR counterpart is 5.15 (text not retrieved).

citations.title: Reportable events (ALP)
citations.requirement: ALPs notify DOH immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034 or (609) 392-2020 after hours, with written confirmation within 72 hours. Events include reportable infections and diseases under N.J.A.C. 8:57 among residents (#4) and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman (#7).

citations.title: Requirements for dining services
citations.requirement: Nutrients and calories for each resident follow the Dietary Reference Intake tables of the Food and Nutrition Board (National Academies), adjusted for age, sex, weight, physical activity and therapeutic needs. Subchapter 10 also sets qualifications for dietitians and designation of a food services coordinator (per the readoption summary).

citations.title: Fire extinguisher specifications
citations.requirement: Fire extinguishers must comply with NFPA 10, Standard for Portable Fire Extinguishers, 2002 edition.

citations.title: Resident environment (pets)
citations.requirement: If pets are allowed, the facility provides safeguards to prevent interference in residents' lives. Guidelines for pet-facilitated therapy are available from DOH.

citations.title: Criminal Background Investigations: Nurse Aides, Personal Care Assistants, and Assisted Living Administrators
citations.requirement: Applicants for certification or recertification as a nurse aide, PCA or assisted living administrator submit to a criminal history record background check. There is a process for a determination of rehabilitation after a disqualifying conviction. Readopted effective 1/17/2024, expiring 1/17/2031.

citations.title: Background checks for nurse aide and personal care assistant certification
citations.requirement: A follow-up federal criminal history check is required at least every two years as a condition of recertification of each certified nurse aide and PCA. The Commissioner may provide an alternative means.

citations.title: State minimum hourly wage
citations.requirement: NJ minimum wage is $15.92/hour effective 1/1/2026. NJDOL publishes the CPI-adjusted 2027 rate around September 30, 2026, which was not checked.

citations.title: Medicaid per diem for assisted living (statutory minimums and Medicaid-volume tiers)
citations.requirement: Sets minimum Medicaid per diems for ALR/CPCH/ALP and tier add-ons by yearly average Medicaid census, measured from paid claims against total licensed beds: $10 at 15% to under 30%, $15 at 30% to under 50%, $30 at 50% to under 70%, $35 at 70% or more. The SFY2026 base is $91.10 (ALR), $81.10 (CPCH) and $79.10 (ALP) per DHS notice of 7/16/2025. SFY2027 rates and CMS approval were not checked.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: An ALR provides apartment-style housing and congregate dining for four or more unrelated adults. Units have at minimum one unfurnished room, a private bathroom, a kitchenette and a lockable entrance door. A CPCH provides room and board, with units of no more than two residents and a lockable door. 'Licensed nurse' means an RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37. Contact details: CN&L Program, PO Box 358, Trenton 08625-0358, (609) 292-6552; Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, PO Box 367, Trenton 08625-0358, (800) 792-9770; DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit, (609) 633-8151.

citations.title: State Long-Term Care Ombudsman notification (as cited in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)4)
citations.requirement: When a resident is 60 or older, alleged or suspected abuse or exploitation must also be reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995. Only the rule's cross-reference was retrieved, not the statute text.

citations.title: Record of death
citations.requirement: 8:36-5.7(a)8 requires a policy on staff responsibility for prompt notification of a resident's death as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a). The text of 15.7 itself was not retrieved.

citations.title: Quality Improvement (quality improvement programs, use of restraints, personal care services)
citations.requirement: Subchapter 21 sets standards for quality improvement programs, the use of restraints and personal care services (DOH readoption summary). Specific section numbers and text (21.1-21.3) must be pulled before citing at section level.

citations.title: Resident activities
citations.requirement: Subchapter 12 (sole section 12.1) establishes standards for provision of resident activities. 5.1(b) also requires capability to provide activities, recreational and social work services. Detailed content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Social Work Services
citations.requirement: Subchapter 13 (13.1-13.2) establishes qualifications of social workers and requirements for social work services (DOH readoption summary). Detailed content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Housekeeping, Sanitation, Safety and Maintenance
citations.requirement: Subchapter 17 (17.1-17.8) sets standards for housekeeping, laundry, pest control, resident environment, waste removal, sanitation, and heating and air conditioning (DOH readoption summary). The DOH Affidavit of Compliance lists a written housekeeping work plan with trained staff. Section-level content was not retrieved.

citations.title: Standards for Respite Care Services
citations.requirement: Subchapter 20 (20.1-20.3) covers purpose and scope, policies and procedures, and staffing for respite care (DOH readoption summary). It applies only if respite is offered. Detailed content was not retrieved.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body, Administrator Responsibilities and Organizational Chart
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; governing body, administrator and all department heads
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed, who is accountable for administration and resident care, and what happens when the administrator changes, so that lines of authority are clear to staff, residents and the Department of Health (DOH).
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] maintains a written policy and procedure manual for the organization and operation of the facility. The manual is developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review is documented. The manual is kept in the facility and is available to DOH representatives at all times. This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a) (policy and procedure manual) and N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)1 (organizational chart delineating lines of authority, responsibility and accountability for administration and resident care services). Policy GOV-05 sets out the annual review and document control process.

The governing body holds final authority and responsibility for the facility. It appoints a qualified administrator who is in charge of day-to-day operation and accountable to the governing body. The administrator must be at least 21 years old, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and hold a current New Jersey nursing home administrator license or a current New Jersey assisted living administrator certification. A qualified owner may serve as administrator. Certification is for 3 years. Renewal requires at least 30 hours of continuing education on assisted living topics earned within the certificate period, plus a background check.

The organizational chart shows the governing body, administrator, nursing and personal care services, dining, activities, social work, maintenance and housekeeping, and the reporting line of each position. Each employee has one clearly identified supervisor. The chart also shows who acts for the administrator when the administrator is off site.

The termination of an administrator is a reportable event under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.10. The facility notifies DOH immediately by phone and confirms in writing within 72 hours, giving the replacement's name and qualifications. An administrator's certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted for improper practice, including a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property of a resident or client of any DOH-licensed facility or agency. [AGENCY NAME] treats any such finding as grounds for immediate review of the person's employment.

definitions.definition: The owner(s) or board that holds legal responsibility for the facility, adopts policy, and appoints and evaluates the administrator.
The person who meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.2 and is responsible for day-to-day operation of the facility.
A 3-year DOH certificate allowing a person to serve as administrator of an ALR, CPCH or ALP.
A written diagram showing lines of authority, responsibility and accountability for administration and resident care.

procedures: The governing body adopts this policy and the organizational chart in writing and records the adoption in its minutes or a signed resolution.

The governing body appoints [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as administrator. Before the start date, the governing body verifies and copies the current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certificate, proof of age 21 or older, the high school diploma or equivalent, and the criminal background check result. The copies go into the administrator's personnel file (STF-05, STF-07).
If an owner serves as administrator, the governing body documents in its minutes that the owner meets every qualification in N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.2.

The administrator prepares the organizational chart showing the governing body, administrator, director of nursing or RN, personal care assistants, dining, activities, social work, maintenance, housekeeping and any ALP staff. The chart shows who reports to whom and who is accountable for resident care.
The administrator posts the chart in the staff area and keeps a current copy in the policy manual. Copies are given to each employee at orientation (STF-03).
The administrator reviews the chart at least annually with the manual review and whenever a position, reporting line or owner changes. Each review is dated and initialed on the chart's revision log.

The administrator names in writing an on-site person in charge for periods when the administrator is absent. That person is named on the chart and on the schedule, and is a person who knows the manual, the emergency plan and the DOH reporting numbers.

The governing body meets at least quarterly, and more often as needed. It reviews the administrator's report, incident and complaint trends, staffing, the quality improvement report (GOV-06) and survey results. Minutes are kept.
The governing body evaluates the administrator in writing at least annually against the duties in this policy.

The administrator tracks the expiration date of the administrator certificate or license. The administrator completes the 30 hours of assisted living continuing education within the certificate period and applies for renewal with a background check, starting no later than 6 months before expiration. The CE certificates are kept in the personnel file (STF-07).

If the administrator is terminated, resigns or is removed, the governing body or the person in charge calls DOH immediately at (609) 633-9034, or (609) 392-2020 after business hours. The caller states the facility name, the date, and the replacement's name and qualifications, or the interim plan.

Within 72 hours of the phone call, the governing body sends written confirmation to the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, PO Box 367, Trenton NJ 08625-0358. A copy of the call log and written notice is kept in the administrative file (REC-02).
A replacement administrator is verified under step 2 before assuming duties. The governing body sends DOH the replacement's qualifications with the written notice.

If a DOH or other State finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation is made against the administrator, the governing body is notified the same day. The governing body then decides on interim leadership, reviews the finding and takes action, including removal where warranted.
The administrator keeps the manual in the administrative office, available to DOH representatives at all times, and documents each annual review (GOV-05).

The administrator keeps the DOH contacts in the manual and at the front desk: CN&L Program (609) 292-6552; Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations (800) 792-9770; Assisted Living Administrator Certification 609-633-9706.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts policy and the organizational chart, appoints and evaluates the administrator, meets at least quarterly, and provides resources for compliance.
Manages daily operation, maintains the chart and manual, keeps certification current, makes DOH notifications and reports to the governing body.
Acts for the administrator when absent, including making immediate DOH phone notifications.
Supervise assigned staff and report resident care concerns up the chain shown on the chart.

documentation: Governing body resolution and meeting minutes
Current organizational chart with revision log
Administrator license or certificate, diploma, background check and CE records
Annual administrator evaluation
Administrator-change call log and 72-hour written notice to DOH
Manual annual review log

policies.title: Description of Services the Facility Is Capable of Providing
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; administrator, nursing, admissions and marketing staff
policies.purpose: To state in writing the services [AGENCY NAME] can provide, so that admissions, the admission agreement, advertising and staff practice all describe the same capability.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)2 (a description of the services the facility is capable of providing).

[AGENCY NAME] is licensed as a [LICENSE TYPE: ASSISTED LIVING RESIDENCE / COMPREHENSIVE PERSONAL CARE HOME / ASSISTED LIVING PROGRAM] by the NJ Department of Health. An assisted living residence provides apartment-style housing and congregate dining for four or more unrelated adults. Units have at minimum one unfurnished room, a private bathroom, a kitchenette and a lockable entrance door. A comprehensive personal care home provides room and board, with units of no more than two residents and a lockable door.

The facility provides or coordinates personal care and services based on assessment by qualified persons, consistent with the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37. The facility is capable of providing: (1) personal care services; (2) nursing services; (3) pharmacy services; (4) dining services; (5) activities; (6) recreation; and (7) social work services. Medication services include supervision of self-administration and administration by trained, supervised staff.

The facility is capable of nursing services, including for nursing-home-level residents. A resident may, but need not, be moved when the record documents one or more of these characteristics: (1) need for 24-hour, 7-day nursing supervision; (2) bedridden for more than 14 days; (3) totally dependent in 4 or more activities of daily living; (4) severe cognitive decline; (5) stage 3 or 4 pressure sores, or multiple stage 2 sores; (6) need for more than assistance with transfer; (7) danger to self or others; or (8) unstable condition. A resident with a single stage 2 pressure sore is retained with a plan of care. Residents who need specialized long-term care must be transferred. The admission agreement states whether the facility will retain such residents, to what extent, and at what added cost. [AGENCY NAME] does not describe or advertise any service it cannot actually provide.

definitions.definition: A facility providing apartment-style housing and congregate dining and assisted living services to four or more unrelated adults.
A facility providing room and board and personal care, with units of no more than two residents and a lockable door.
A registered nurse or practical nurse licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37.
A resident whose record documents one or more of the eight characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d).

procedures: The administrator, with the nurse and department heads, prepares a Statement of Services listing each service in this policy and how it is delivered (staff type, hours, whether provided directly or coordinated with an outside provider).

The Statement of Services states the license type, unit types and capacity, the number of residents per unit (CPCH units hold no more than two), and the unit features: lockable door, bathroom and, for ALR units, kitchenette.

Personal care: the statement lists the assistance available with bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, mobility and transfers, eating and other activities of daily living, delivered by trained personal care assistants under the supervision described in HLT-04.

Nursing: the statement lists nursing services, who the licensed nurse is, how nursing availability is arranged, and what is delegated (HLT-04). Only tasks allowed by the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37 are listed.
Pharmacy and medication: the statement describes the pharmacy arrangement, supervision of self-administration, and administration by trained, supervised staff (HLT-02, HLT-03).
Dining, activities, recreation and social work: the statement describes meals offered, therapeutic diets, the activity calendar and social work services (DL-01, DL-02, HLT-11).

The statement lists the retention limits: for each of the eight 5.1(d) characteristics, whether [AGENCY NAME] will retain the resident, to what extent, and at what added cost. It notes that a single stage 2 pressure sore is retained with a plan of care. It also lists the conditions that require transfer to specialized long-term care (ADM-05).
The administrator confirms the statement matches the Certificate of Need conditions and the admission agreement forwarded to the CN&L Program (GOV-03, RR-03). Any difference is corrected before use.
The governing body approves the Statement of Services. It is filed in the manual and distributed under GOV-05.
Admissions staff give the statement to every applicant, and the admission agreement refers to it (ADM-01, RR-03).
Marketing and advertising are reviewed by the administrator before release to confirm they describe only services listed in the statement and only as the license allows (GOV-03).

The nurse reviews the statement whenever staffing, license type, the pharmacy arrangement or service capability changes, and at least annually with the manual review. Revisions are dated and the older version is kept.

Before an applicant is admitted, the nurse and administrator confirm the facility can meet that person's assessed needs with the listed services. If not, the application is declined with a written explanation (ADM-01).
If a service is temporarily unavailable, the administrator notifies affected residents, the physician and responsible individuals the same day, documents it, and tells DOH where required.

responsibilities.duty: Approves and maintains the Statement of Services, and ensures agreement and advertising match it.
Defines nursing, medication and retention-limit content and reviews it annually.
Give the statement to applicants and screen against it.
Approves the statement and any added services.

documentation: Statement of Services with revision dates
Governing body approval
Comparison to admission agreement and Certificate of Need conditions
Advertising review log
Records of service interruptions and notifications

policies.title: Licensure, Posting, Advertising, Waivers, Surrender of License and Change of Ownership
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; governing body and administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is licensed before it admits anyone, advertises accurately, posts required notices, handles waivers, ownership changes and surrender of license correctly, and pays required fees.
policies.policy:
This policy is part of the manual required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a) (policy and procedure manual for organization and operation of the facility). It is reviewed at least annually and kept available to DOH representatives at all times.

[AGENCY NAME] does not admit any resident before it holds written DOH approval or a license. Violation carries penalties under N.J.S.A. 26:2H-14 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-1. A license application is made to the Commissioner only after a Certificate of Need has been received. The application includes the commitment that at least 20% of residents will have nursing-home-level needs within 36 months of licensure. The facility forwards its admission agreement to the CN&L Program for review. Newly constructed or expanded facilities submit plans to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit for approval before construction, and the license application includes the Unit's written final release. Before occupying a new or renovated building, the facility submits a local certificate of occupancy to the Unit and the further items required to the CN&L Program.

Only facilities licensed as ALRs or CPCHs may describe and offer themselves to the public as providing assisted living services. [AGENCY NAME] conspicuously posts the notice required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11, stating that specified information is available in the facility during business hours to residents and the public. The posted information includes the DOH toll-free hotline, county agency phone numbers and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman number.

Waivers are sought in writing from the Director of the CN&L Program. Before ownership is transferred, the prospective new owner applies to the CN&L Program. Before voluntary surrender of the license, or as directed under an order of revocation, non-renewal or suspension, the facility gives residents, their physicians and guarantors of payment at least 30 days' notice and returns the license to the CN&L Program within 7 working days.

definitions.definition: DOH approval that must be received before a license application may be filed.
DOH Certificate of Need and Licensing Program, PO Box 358, Trenton NJ 08625-0358, (609) 292-6552.
Written permission from DOH, granted on application to the Director of the CN&L Program, to be excused from a requirement of N.J.A.C. 8:36.
Transfer of ownership of the licensed facility to a new owner, requiring a prior application by the prospective owner.

procedures: Before any application, the governing body confirms a Certificate of Need has been received. The administrator may request a preliminary conference with the CN&L Program, (609) 292-6552.

For a new or expanded building, the administrator submits plans to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit, (609) 633-8151, and obtains written approval before construction starts. The Unit's written final release is kept for the license application.

The administrator prepares the license application with the 20% nursing-home-level commitment (ADM-02) and forwards the proposed admission agreement to the CN&L Program for review, to confirm it does not violate N.J.A.C. 8:36, Certificate of Need conditions or State or federal law (RR-03).

The administrator pays the nonrefundable initial fee of $1,500 plus $15 per bed and attaches proof of payment. The administrator calendars the annual renewal fee of $1,500 plus $15 per bed, the biennial inspection fee of $1,500 due in the inspection year with that year's annual fee, the $1,500 transfer of ownership fee and the $375 relocation fee.

Before DOH survey, the administrator collects local zoning, fire, health and building approvals and the certificate of occupancy or certificate of continued occupancy, and attends the preliminary conference.

The facility does not admit, or hold itself ready to admit, a resident until written DOH approval or the license is in hand. The administrator signs a written admission hold on all pending applications until then (ADM-01).
The administrator keeps the license, the Certificate of Need and approvals in the administrative office and makes them available to DOH representatives.

The administrator reviews all advertising, website text, brochures and signs before release. The facility uses the term assisted living only while licensed as an ALR or CPCH. The review is logged and the content is checked against the Statement of Services (GOV-02).

The administrator posts a conspicuous notice at the main entrance stating that the information required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11 is available in the facility during business hours to residents and the public. The posting lists the DOH toll-free hotline 1-800-792-9770, the county agency phone numbers [COUNTY AGENCY PHONE] and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995. The administrator checks the posting monthly.

When a waiver is needed, including a request to reduce or waive the 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy requirement, the administrator writes to the Director of the CN&L Program, PO Box 358, Trenton NJ 08625-0358. The letter identifies the rule, the reason, the alternative and the residents affected. The request and DOH's answer are filed.

For a change of ownership, the prospective owner applies to the CN&L Program before the transfer. After review, DOH sends an approval letter with licensure forms and a fee request. The administrator and prospective owner complete the forms and pay the $1,500 fee. Residents and staff are informed of the planned change in writing in advance.
Within 5 working days after the transaction closes, the new owner submits the follow-up documents required by DOH. The administrator confirms submission and files the receipt.

For a voluntary surrender, or a revocation, non-renewal or suspension order, the administrator notifies in writing every resident, each resident's physician and each guarantor of payment at least 30 days before the effective date, or as the order directs. The notice states the date, the reason and relocation help available (ADM-06).
The administrator returns the license to the CN&L Program within 7 working days, records the date and keeps proof of delivery.
For a relocation of the facility, the administrator pays the $375 fee and follows the plan review and certificate of occupancy steps above before residents move.
The administrator reviews this policy annually and keeps an up-to-date licensure calendar showing renewals, fees and inspection years.

responsibilities.duty: Obtains the Certificate of Need, authorizes applications and fees, and approves ownership and surrender decisions.
Files applications, pays fees, controls advertising, posts notices, and carries out waiver, ownership and surrender steps.
Applies to the CN&L Program before the transfer and submits post-closing documents within 5 working days.

documentation: Certificate of Need and license
Application, proof of fee payment and CN&L correspondence
DCA Plan Review Unit final release and certificate of occupancy
Advertising review log
Notice posting checklist
Waiver requests and DOH responses
Ownership transfer file
Surrender notices and proof of license return

policies.title: Licensure Application Narratives: Design, Neighborhood Integration, Waivers and Nursing-Home-Level Access
policies.applies_to: New ALR or CPCH applicants and any expansion requiring plan review; governing body and administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure the narrative statements in the license application are prepared completely, accurately and consistently with the building plans, and that the facility's actual design and operation match them.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] prepares and submits the following narratives with its license application. This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(e)4 (evaluation of any requested waivers under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7), N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(e)5 (description of how the architectural design will promote privacy, choice, independence, dignity and a home-like environment), N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(e)6 (description of how the physical plant will facilitate care of residents with common long-term care problems such as reduced mobility, incontinence and dementia) and N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(f) (if plans are required under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.3, a description of how the location will promote physical integration or social connection of residents into a neighborhood, center or other area with existing services or amenities).

The narratives are written to describe the building that will actually be built and operated. The application also contains the commitment that at least 20% of residents will have nursing-home-level needs within 36 months of licensure. The facility also accepts the Medicaid-eligible occupancy requirement of at least 10% within three years of licensure unless the Commissioner waives or reduces it. Where residents are served through NJ FamilyCare managed long-term services and supports, the setting is designed and operated consistent with the home and community-based setting qualities in 42 CFR 441.301(c): privacy, choice, independence, dignity and community integration.

definitions.definition: A written description or evaluation submitted with the license application under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(e) and (f).
A written analysis of each licensing requirement the applicant asks DOH to waive, with the reason and the alternative.

definitions.term: DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit
definitions.definition: The Department of Community Affairs unit that approves plans for new or expanded facilities before construction.
A setting that gives residents privacy, their own lockable space, personal furnishings and ordinary choices about daily life.

procedures: The governing body assigns the administrator to lead the application narratives, with the architect and the nurse consultant [NAME] contributing, and sets a completion date at least 30 days before the planned submission.

The team lists every licensing requirement the building or program cannot meet as designed. For each, it writes an evaluation covering the rule, why a waiver is sought, how residents remain safe and protected, and the alternative. The administrator then applies in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7. If none is sought, the narrative says so (2.2(e)4).

For the design narrative (2.2(e)5), the architect and administrator describe unit layout and lockable doors, private bathrooms, kitchenettes where provided, resident control of furnishings, shared spaces, and how the layout supports privacy, choice, independence and dignity. They state the unit size, the number of residents per unit, and for a CPCH that no unit exceeds two residents.

For the physical plant narrative (2.2(e)6), the team describes features addressing reduced mobility (corridor widths, grab bars, accessible bathing, thresholds, handrails), incontinence (bathroom proximity, finishes, laundry capacity) and dementia (wayfinding, lighting, secure outdoor space, monitored exits), and cross-references HLT-06 and SAF-03.

For the location narrative (2.2(f)), required when plans must be submitted under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.3, the administrator documents nearby services and amenities (shops, pharmacy, health providers, houses of worship, parks, public transit) and how residents can reach them. The narrative uses distances and transportation arrangements (DL-04).

The administrator checks every narrative against the plans submitted to the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit so that each feature described appears on the drawings. Differences are corrected before filing.

The nursing-home-level commitment (at least 20% of residents within 36 months) and the 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy plan are reviewed by the governing body and described consistently with ADM-02 and ADM-07.
The governing body reviews and signs the final narratives. The administrator submits them with the application and the Unit's written final release (GOV-03).
The administrator files a complete copy of the narratives, plans and DOH correspondence in the permanent administrative file.

Before opening, the administrator walks the completed building with the narratives in hand and records any feature that differs. A difference is corrected or reported to the CN&L Program before resident admission.
If a later renovation or expansion changes a described feature, the administrator updates the narratives, consults the Plan Review Unit and notifies the CN&L Program.
The administrator reviews the narratives annually in the quality improvement process (GOV-06) and asks residents whether the setting provides privacy, choice and dignity. Findings are documented.

responsibilities.duty: Approves narratives, waiver requests and commitments.
Leads preparation, reconciles narratives with plans, files submissions and verifies the finished building.
Provides plan-accurate design and physical plant information.
Advises on mobility, incontinence and dementia care features.

documentation: Signed narratives for 2.2(e)4, (e)5, (e)6 and (f)
Waiver requests and DOH decisions
Plans and DCA Plan Review Unit final release
Pre-opening walk-through record
Annual setting review notes

policies.title: Policy and Procedure Manual: Annual Review, Availability and Document Control
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; administrator and all staff
policies.purpose: To keep the facility's manual current, reviewed at least yearly, available to DOH at all times, and accessible to residents, families, applicants and referral sources under a written procedure.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a) (manual developed, implemented, reviewed at least annually, each review documented, and available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times), N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(b) (policy and procedure addressing how manuals are made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, prospective applicants and referring agencies) and N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.4 (assisted living programs only: manual developed, implemented and reviewed under 5.7, and available at all ALP sites, the provider main office and to DOH).

The manual includes at least: the organizational chart; the description of services; security policies; abuse and exploitation reporting to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770 and, if the resident is 60 or older, to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995; confidentiality and release of records; personnel records; employee physicals, immunizations and TB testing; and prompt notification of a resident's death. Resident care policies are established, implemented and reviewed at the intervals those policies specify, with each review documented (N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1). The resident care policies include control of smoking.

A complete current copy of the manual is kept in [LOCATION IN FACILITY] and is available to DOH representatives immediately on request, at any hour. Residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, prospective applicants and referring agencies may review the manual under the procedures below.

definitions.definition: The policy and procedure manual(s) for organization and operation of the facility, including resident care policies.
A person a resident has named, in writing, to act or receive information on the resident's behalf.
A documented review by the administrator and governing body of every policy at least once every 12 months.
A hospital, case manager, MLTSS care manager, county agency or other organization that refers or places residents.

procedures: The administrator keeps a master copy of the manual in [LOCATION IN FACILITY]. The location is known to all shifts, and a staff member who can unlock it is on duty or on call at all times, so DOH representatives can see the manual immediately at any hour.

Each policy shows an ID, effective date, revision number and the date of last review. The administrator keeps a master index (HLT-01 for resident care policies) and a revision log showing what changed and why.

Annual review: each year, by [REVIEW MONTH], the administrator reviews every policy with the nurse, department heads and, as appropriate, the governing body. The review checks it against current N.J.A.C. 8:36, other law, DOH notices and actual practice.

The administrator documents each review on the Manual Review Log with the policy ID, reviewer name and title, date, changes made (or no changes) and the governing body approval date. The log is retained and available to DOH.
Resident care policies are reviewed at the interval stated in each policy and at least annually, and each review is documented (N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1). The smoking control policy (SAF-08) is included.

Between annual reviews, the administrator updates a policy within 30 days of a rule change, survey finding, incident trend or change in practice. Superseded versions are marked, dated and archived, not discarded.
Staff are told of new or changed policies in writing and in a staff meeting within 14 days. Each employee signs a read-and-understood acknowledgement placed in the personnel file (STF-03, STF-05).

Resident access: the manual is posted in [LOCATION] for residents to read during business hours, with no request needed. Residents, guardians and designated responsible individuals who ask are given the manual to read the same day, or within 2 business days if a copy must be prepared. A copy of any policy they request is provided. Staff help residents who need assistance reading or understanding it, including interpretation (RR-07).

Prospective applicants and referring agencies: admissions staff tell each applicant at the first contact, and each referring agency on request, that the manual is available for review. It is shown to them on site during business hours, or a copy of the requested policies is provided within 2 business days. The offer is documented in the admission file (ADM-01).
Confidential material is removed before release. Personnel files and other residents' information are never part of the manual released (RR-06).
The administrator keeps a Manual Access Log showing who requested the manual, the date, the format given and staff involved.

ALP sites only: the administrator makes sure a current copy of the manual is kept at every ALP site and the ALP provider main office, with the same review log and DOH availability (N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.4). Versions at all locations are replaced the same day as updates.
The administrator verifies each quarter that every copy is current, complete, legible and in the right place, and records the check.
The quality improvement program (GOV-06) reports on timeliness of reviews, access requests and any survey citations tied to policy.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the manual, performs and documents annual reviews, and controls versions and access.
Approves new and revised policies and the annual review.
Reviews resident care policies and clinical content.
Offer the manual to applicants and referral agencies and log it.
Read assigned policies, sign acknowledgements and follow current policy.

documentation: Manual Review Log
Policy revision log and archived versions
Staff acknowledgement forms
Manual Access Log
Quarterly manual copy check record
ALP site and main office copy checks (if ALP)

policies.title: Quality Improvement and Performance Review
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; governing body, administrator, nurse and all department heads
policies.purpose: To establish an ongoing quality improvement program that measures how well [AGENCY NAME] serves residents, finds problems early, and documents corrective action, consistent with N.J.A.C. 8:36 Subchapter 21.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] operates a written quality improvement (QI) program consistent with N.J.A.C. 8:36 Subchapter 21 (quality improvement programs, use of restraints and personal care services). The program collects and reviews data on resident care and operations, identifies trends, sets corrective actions with owners and due dates, and reports results to the governing body. Section-level requirements within Subchapter 21 will be confirmed against the current rule text and built into the program before opening.

The QI program reviews, at least quarterly: incidents and accidents, reportable events, falls, pressure injuries, medication errors, infections, grievances, elopements and restraint use. It also monitors infection prevention and control practices under the written infection control policies required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-18.3, and progress toward the 20% nursing-home-level and 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy commitments. After each DOH survey, the administrator documents the plan of correction and verifies it was carried out. Information used in QI is confidential and handled under RR-06.

definitions.definition: A planned, ongoing process of measuring performance, analyzing results and acting to improve resident care and safety.
The group that reviews QI data, composed of the administrator, nurse, department heads and, where practical, a resident or family representative.
A measurable item (such as number of falls per 1,000 resident days) tracked over time.
A written plan stating how and when a deficiency or problem will be fixed and how the fix will be checked.

procedures: The governing body adopts this QI program and designates the administrator as QI lead. The administrator names a QI committee including the nurse, dining, activities, maintenance, housekeeping and social work representatives, and invites a resident or family member to participate.
The committee meets at least quarterly. Minutes record attendance, data reviewed, findings, decisions and assigned actions.

The administrator sets the indicators for each year, including: falls and fall injuries; pressure injuries; medication errors and omissions; hospital transfers; infections and outbreaks; elopements; restraint use; grievances and their resolution time; incidents reported to DOH; staffing coverage; and resident and family satisfaction.

Staff collect the data monthly. The nurse compiles clinical indicators from the incident, medication and infection logs (SAF-02, HLT-02, SAF-07). The administrator compiles grievance, staffing and reportable event data (RR-02, STF-01, REC-02).

Infection prevention: the nurse reviews infection surveillance data, hand hygiene and cleaning audits, immunization records and needle and syringe disposal practices against the written infection control policies (SAF-07), and reports results to the committee.

Restraints: the nurse reviews every use of a restraint or restrictive practice and confirms it followed policy (SAF-04). Trends and any unauthorized use are referred to the administrator the same day.

For each indicator outside the target, the committee selects a cause-based action, names an owner and sets a due date no later than 60 days, unless the issue is urgent. The action is entered on the QI Action Plan.
The committee checks completed actions at the next quarterly meeting and records whether the indicator improved. Actions that did not work are redesigned.

Occupancy commitments: the administrator reports each quarter the number and percent of residents with nursing-home-level needs, and the percent of Medicaid-eligible occupancy, with the plan to reach 20% within 36 months of licensure and 10% within three years (ADM-02, ADM-07).

Survey follow-up: within 10 days of receiving a DOH survey report, the administrator writes a plan of correction, assigns owners and dates, and reports to the governing body. The administrator verifies completion and files evidence (REC-02).

Resident input: at least twice a year, the administrator surveys residents and responsible individuals about care, dining, activities, privacy and safety, and reports results, including comments, to the committee. Residents are not penalized for responses.

The administrator reports to the governing body at each quarterly meeting and produces an annual QI report stating indicators, actions taken, results and next year's priorities. The governing body documents its review.
All QI minutes, data and reports are retained and available to DOH. Resident identifying information is limited to what is needed for review (RR-06).
The QI program is itself reviewed annually with the manual review (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the QI program, reviews quarterly and annual reports, and provides resources for corrective action.
Chairs the committee, compiles data, ensures action plans and survey corrections are completed and reports to the governing body.
Supplies and analyzes clinical and infection control data and reviews restraint use.
Collect data for their areas and carry out assigned actions.
Report incidents, near misses and concerns promptly and take part in improvement actions.

documentation: QI program description and indicator list
Quarterly QI committee minutes
QI Action Plan with owners, due dates and results
Monthly indicator data and logs
Resident satisfaction survey results
Survey plans of correction and evidence of completion
Annual QI report with governing body review

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity (NJ FamilyCare / MLTSS)
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all staff, contractors and the governing body involved in resident services, documentation or billing for NJ FamilyCare / MLTSS
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] bills NJ FamilyCare managed care plans (MLTSS) only for services that were actually delivered and documented, reports Medicaid-related data accurately, and prevents, detects and corrects fraud, waste and abuse.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] bills NJ FamilyCare / MLTSS plans only for services actually delivered to an enrolled resident and documented in the resident's service plan and daily service records. Medicaid does not pay room and board, so the resident's cost share is billed only as set out in the plan and the county determination, and never as a charge for a service Medicaid has already covered. The agency does not offer, pay, solicit or accept anything of value to induce or reward referrals of Medicaid-covered residents or services (42 USC 1320a-7b(b)), and does not submit or cause to be submitted any false or inflated claim (31 USC 3729). Medicaid-volume per diem tier add-ons under P.L. 2023, c.80 are measured from yearly paid claims against total licensed beds and are not budgeted or booked as revenue until the Division of Medical Assistance and Health Services (DMAHS) confirms them in writing. The agency also reports Medicaid-eligible occupancy accurately where N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1 requires a Medicaid-eligible occupancy level for new ALRs and CPCHs. The governing body designates a compliance contact and maintains a reporting channel with a written non-retaliation statement. This policy is reviewed at least annually (see GOV-05).

definitions.definition: The person designated in writing by the governing body to oversee this policy, receive reports and coordinate audits. The Administrator serves unless another person is named.
A request for payment that the agency knows, or recklessly disregards, is false, including billing for services not delivered, not documented, not authorized or at the wrong rate.
Any payment, discount, gift or other remuneration offered or accepted to induce or reward referrals or purchases covered by a federal health care program.
Managed Long Term Services and Supports, the NJ FamilyCare program through which managed care organizations pay for Medicaid-covered assisted living care services.

An amount above the minimum Medicaid per diem, based on the yearly average Medicaid census (paid claims against total licensed beds): $10 at 15% to under 30%; $15 at 30% to under 50%; $30 at 50% to under 70%; $35 at 70% or more; none below 15%.
Any payment received from a managed care plan or the State that the agency is not entitled to keep.

procedures: The governing body designates the compliance contact in writing ([COMPLIANCE CONTACT NAME], [PHONE]) and records the designation in the governing body minutes. The contact reports to the governing body at least quarterly.

The Administrator issues a written code of conduct and this policy to every employee and contractor at hire and each year. Each person signs an acknowledgment, which is filed in the personnel record (STF-05).

The agency maintains a reporting channel: a telephone line ([COMPLIANCE REPORTING PHONE]), a locked drop box in the staff area, and a mailing address. Anonymous reports are accepted. The channel and the non-retaliation statement are posted where staff can see them.

Non-retaliation statement: no person is disciplined, threatened or treated differently for a good-faith report of a compliance concern or for cooperating in an inquiry. Any retaliation is itself a violation and is grounds for discipline up to termination.

Before billing, the billing designee confirms each resident's NJ FamilyCare eligibility, managed care plan enrollment and the plan's authorization or service plan, and records the check in the resident's billing file. This is repeated monthly.

Direct care staff document each day's services on the daily service record at the time they are delivered. The RN or Administrator reviews records weekly for gaps. No service is billed that lacks documentation consistent with the service plan.

The billing designee reconciles the month's census (including hospital days, leaves and discharges) against the claims before submission. Days when the resident was not in the residence are not billed unless the plan's rules expressly allow it. The Administrator signs the reconciliation.

Rates: the billing designee applies the current DHS-published per diem for the license type. The SFY2026 base is $91.10 (ALR), $81.10 (CPCH) and $79.10 (ALP) per NJ FamilyCare beneficiary per day. Before each July 1 the Administrator confirms the new State fiscal year rate in writing from DMAHS or the managed care plan, and does not assume that a prior-year rate continues.

Tier add-ons: the compliance contact calculates the yearly average Medicaid census from paid claims against total licensed beds each fiscal year. Add-ons are not included in budgets, forecasts or revenue until DMAHS confirms the amount in writing. The written confirmation is kept in the billing file.

Room and board and cost share: Medicaid does not pay room and board. The agency bills the resident cost share only as shown in the plan and county determination, and follows RR-03, RR-04 and ADM-07. No resident is charged for a service the managed care plan pays for.

Referral arrangements: no employee may pay or accept anything of value for resident referrals. The Administrator submits any marketing, referral-source, discount or gift arrangement to counsel for review before it starts. Gifts from vendors or referral sources are declined or reported to the compliance contact.

Before hiring or contracting, and at least monthly thereafter, the compliance contact checks employees, contractors and vendors against federal and State exclusion and debarment lists. Results are filed. Any listed person is removed from Medicaid-funded work at once.

Where N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1 requires Medicaid-eligible occupancy, the Administrator keeps the monthly occupancy records. Counts and reports to the State are checked against the census by a second person before they are sent (see ADM-02 and REC-02).

The compliance contact audits at least five resident billing files each quarter, or 10% of Medicaid residents if that is more, comparing claims to service plans and daily records. Findings, corrective actions and dates go into the quality improvement review (GOV-06).

Overpayments: when an error is found, the compliance contact stops further billing of the error, quantifies it, informs counsel, notifies the managed care plan or DMAHS in writing, and returns the overpayment promptly. The steps and dates are documented.

Reports of concerns: the compliance contact logs every report on receipt, starts review within five business days, involves counsel as needed, and records findings, corrective action and any discipline. The reporter is told the review is closed, to the extent identity is known and privacy allows.

Government requests: any inquiry, audit or subpoena from a payer or government agency goes at once to the Administrator and compliance contact. Staff cooperate fully, and records are never altered, backdated or destroyed.
Training: all staff are trained at orientation and each year on false claims, kickbacks, accurate documentation and how to report. Sign-in sheets and content are kept (STF-03).
Billing, audit and compliance records are kept as set out in REC-01. The governing body reviews this policy and the audit results at least annually and records the review.

responsibilities.duty: Designate the compliance contact, receive quarterly compliance reports, review this policy annually and ensure resources for compliance.
Implement this policy, sign monthly census and claim reconciliations, confirm rates and tier add-ons in writing, and prevent retaliation.
Receive and log reports, run exclusion checks and quarterly audits, manage overpayment returns and report to the governing body.
Verify eligibility and authorizations, reconcile census to claims, apply correct rates and keep billing files.
Review service documentation against the service plan and flag undocumented or unsupported services.
Document accurately and on time, never bill or document services not delivered, and report concerns without fear of reprisal.

documentation: Governing body designation of compliance contact and quarterly reports
Signed code of conduct and policy acknowledgments
Compliance report log and investigation files
Monthly eligibility checks and census-to-claim reconciliations
Written DMAHS or plan confirmation of rates and tier add-ons
Quarterly audit results and corrective action records
Exclusion and debarment screening results
Overpayment calculations, notices and refunds
Training sign-in sheets

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities (Posting and Distribution)
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all residents, guardians and designated representatives, and all staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident knows and can exercise the rights set out in the Department of Health statement of resident rights, and that the statement and required notices are posted and distributed as the rules require.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a): [AGENCY NAME] posts and distributes the statement of resident rights (items 1-42 of the rule) to all residents of the assisted living residence, comprehensive personal care home or assisted living program. The statement includes the right to confidential treatment of information (item 27) and freedom from chemical and physical restraints and from physical and mental abuse and neglect.
