This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a)37: when the facility requests a resident's transfer or discharge, the resident receives written notice at least 30 days in advance, except in an emergency. That notice includes the name, address and telephone number of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and is also given to the resident's legally appointed guardian, if any, or, with the resident's consent, to the resident's family, 30 days in advance. The agency gives each resident a copy at admission, documents receipt, and conspicuously posts the notice required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11, which states that specified information is available in the facility during business hours and lists the Department's toll-free hotline, county agency telephone numbers and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman number. For residents who receive MLTSS, the agency also applies the home and community-based settings protections of 42 CFR 441.301(c), including privacy, choice and a lockable unit door, and complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101). Rights are never conditioned on payment source. The policy is reviewed at least annually and each review is documented (N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1).

definitions.definition: The Department of Health's written list of resident rights, items 1-42, required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a).
A legally appointed guardian or a person the resident has chosen, in writing, to receive information or act on the resident's behalf.
The State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, 1-877-582-6995, an advocate for residents of long-term care facilities.
Federal protections for Medicaid home and community-based services residents, including privacy, choice and a lockable unit door, under 42 CFR 441.301(c).

procedures: The Administrator keeps the current Department of Health statement of resident rights, unaltered, with all items 1-42. When the Department revises it, the Administrator replaces it within 10 business days.
The Administrator posts the statement in [LOCATIONS, e.g., main lobby and dining room] at a height readable from a wheelchair, with a large-print copy available. The posting log is initialed monthly.

The Administrator posts the N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11 notice beside it. The notice says required information is available in the facility during business hours, and lists the DOH hotline (1-800-792-9770), the county agency telephone numbers ([COUNTY AGENCY PHONE NUMBERS]) and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (1-877-582-6995). The information binder is kept at [LOCATION] and shown on request during business hours.
At or before the admission interview (ADM-01), the admission staff member gives the resident, and the guardian or designated representative if any, a copy of the statement of resident rights.
The staff member reviews the rights in plain language, reads them aloud if the resident cannot read, and uses interpreter, large-print or other accessible formats as needed (RR-07).

The resident or representative signs and dates the rights acknowledgment. A signed copy is placed in the resident record. If the resident declines to sign, staff note the date, the refusal and the witness, and the rights are still delivered.

Item 37: the admission agreement and the rights statement explain that the agency gives 30 days' written notice of a facility-requested transfer or discharge, except in an emergency. The notice includes the Ombudsman's name, address ([OMBUDSMAN MAILING ADDRESS]) and telephone number (1-877-582-6995). It goes to the guardian if one is appointed, or, with the resident's consent, the family. ADM-06 governs the full process.
Item 27: staff protect confidential information under RR-06 and REC-01 and share it only as the resident authorizes or the law permits.

Freedom from restraints and abuse: staff follow SAF-04 (no chemical or physical restraints for convenience or discipline) and SAF-01 (zero tolerance for abuse, neglect and exploitation, with reporting to DOH at 1-800-792-9770 and, for residents 60 or older, to the Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995).
The right to complain without reprisal (item 40) is carried out under RR-02.

For MLTSS residents, the RN and Administrator confirm privacy in personal care and visits, choice in daily routine, and that each resident unit door can be locked by the resident, with keys held by the resident and only authorized staff. Any limit on these protections is documented in the service plan with the reason, less intrusive options tried, the resident's written agreement and a review date (ADM-04).

The agency gives residents a statement of responsibilities (treat others with respect, follow written house rules, pay charges, tell staff of changes in health or contact information). The statement does not reduce any right.
Staff are trained on resident rights at orientation and each year (STF-03). Sign-in sheets are kept.
When the rights statement is revised or a resident's circumstances change, the updated copy is re-issued to residents and representatives and receipt is documented.
No staff member may threaten, discipline or discharge a resident for asserting a right. Violations are reported to the Administrator and corrected immediately.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually, documents the review date and any changes, and keeps the record with the manual (GOV-05, HLT-01).

responsibilities.duty: Maintain the current rights statement and 5.11 notice, ensure posting and distribution, investigate violations and review this policy annually.
Deliver and explain the rights statement at admission, obtain the signed acknowledgment and file it.
Confirm HCBS protections are reflected in service plans and that any limits are documented and reviewed.
Respect resident rights, direct complaints to the Administrator, and never retaliate.

documentation: Current DOH statement of resident rights and posting log
Posted 5.11 notice and information binder
Signed resident rights acknowledgment in each record
Interpreter or alternative format records
HCBS protection modification documentation in service plans, if any
Staff training sign-in sheets
Annual policy review record

policies.title: Grievances, Complaints and Ombudsman Access
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all residents, guardians, family members and staff
policies.purpose: To give every resident a safe, prompt way to raise complaints inside and outside the facility, and to protect the resident from threats, interference, discharge or reprisal for doing so.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a)40 (the right to voice complaints without being threatened or punished). Each resident may complain and present grievances to the administrator and staff, to government agencies, and to anyone else without fear of interference, discharge or reprisal. [AGENCY NAME] provides each resident, the resident's legally appointed guardian if any, and the resident's family member with the names, addresses and telephone numbers of the government agencies to which a resident can complain and ask questions, including the Department of Health (Complaints Program, 1-800-792-9770) and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (1-877-582-6995), and posts the same information in a conspicuous place in the facility, consistent with the N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.11 notice. Alleged or suspected abuse or exploitation is reported to the DOH Complaints Program and, if the resident is 60 or older, also to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)4; N.J.S.A. 52:27G-7.1 et seq.). The agency allows Ombudsman access to residents and records as the law provides, and logs each grievance, investigation, response and outcome.

definitions.definition: Any complaint, oral or written, about care, services, staff, other residents, charges, the environment or resident rights.
Any threat, discipline, change in care, room or services, loss of privilege, or notice of transfer or discharge because a person complained.
The Department of Health's toll-free complaint and incident hotline, 1-800-792-9770.
The State advocate for residents of long-term care facilities, 1-877-582-6995.

procedures: At admission, the admission staff member gives the resident, guardian and, with the resident's consent, family member a written sheet with the names, addresses and telephone numbers of the Department of Health ([DOH MAILING ADDRESS], 1-800-792-9770) and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman ([OMBUDSMAN MAILING ADDRESS], 1-877-582-6995), and documents that it was given.
The Administrator posts the same agency information in a conspicuous place, with the 5.11 notice, in large print, and checks monthly that the posting is intact.

Any staff member who hears a complaint accepts it respectfully, records it on the grievance form the same shift, and gives it to the Administrator or designee by the next business day. Residents may also complain in writing, by telephone or through a representative, and anonymously.
The Administrator or designee acknowledges the grievance with the resident within two business days and records the date, the person complaining, what was alleged and what the resident wants done.

If the complaint alleges abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator starts SAF-01 immediately, protects the resident, reports to the DOH Complaints Program (1-800-792-9770) and, if the resident is 60 or older, to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (1-877-582-6995), and documents the date, time and name of the person reached.

For other grievances, the Administrator assigns a person not involved in the matter to investigate. The investigator interviews the resident, staff and witnesses, reviews records and records findings.

The Administrator gives the resident a written or, if preferred, verbal response with the findings, action taken and how to appeal or contact the agencies above, within seven calendar days. If more time is needed, the resident is told why and given an expected date.

If the resident is not satisfied, the Administrator offers to meet with the resident and representative, review the matter again, and help the resident contact the Department of Health or the Ombudsman. Staff never discourage outside complaints.

Staff do not question, threaten, move, reduce services to, or give transfer or discharge notice to any resident because of a complaint. If reprisal is alleged, the Administrator investigates under SAF-01 and the governing body is told.

Ombudsman access: the Administrator allows the Ombudsman and authorized representatives to meet privately with residents, with the resident's agreement. Requests to see records are logged, and the Administrator consults counsel before releasing them, applying the law and RR-06.
When the Department of Health or another agency visits or calls about a complaint, staff direct the contact to the Administrator, cooperate fully and keep records unaltered (see REC-02).

The Administrator records every grievance on the grievance log: date, resident, summary, investigator, findings, response date, resolution and resident satisfaction. Log entries are kept in the resident record or a confidential file (REC-01).
The Administrator reviews the log monthly for trends and reports it to the quality improvement committee (GOV-06). The policy is reviewed at least annually with the manual (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Receive and resolve grievances, protect against reprisal, report alleged abuse to the correct agencies, and maintain postings and the log.
Investigate objectively, document findings and report to the Administrator.
Provide agency contact information to residents, guardians and family and document that they did.
Accept complaints courteously, record and forward them promptly, and never retaliate.

documentation: Signed record that agency contact information was given
Posted DOH and Ombudsman information and monthly posting check
Grievance forms and grievance log
Investigation notes and written responses
Reports to DOH and Ombudsman, with date, time and person contacted
Ombudsman access and records request log
Quality improvement trend reports

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits, Refunds and Notice of Charge Changes
policies.applies_to: ALR and CPCH admission agreements (submitted to DOH with the license application); ALP uses its program contract (ALP-01); all admission, billing and administrative staff
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident signs a clear admission agreement that states charges, how charges may change, the right to appeal involuntary discharge, the discharge criteria, and whether the agency retains residents with nursing-home-level needs.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(c): [AGENCY NAME] forwards a copy of its assisted living residence or comprehensive personal care home admission agreement, or other document stating the scope of its services, to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program for review when it applies for licensure. The agreement must not violate N.J.A.C. 8:36, the Certificate of Need conditions, or State or federal law. The agreement includes: (2.2(c)1) proposed charges for room, board and all levels of service and care, and for all additional services and care not included in the standard package of rates, in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.2; (2.2(c)2) how and when the resident will be notified of any change in charges, and a statement that each resident has the right to request written justification of any increase in charges; (2.2(c)3) a statement that each resident has the right to appeal an involuntary discharge as specified at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.14(b); and (2.2(c)4) the criteria in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) that will be used to discharge residents, with an explanation of how the discharge process is carried out, including which staff take part and the extent of resident participation. As N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(e) requires, the agreement states whether the facility will retain residents who have the 5.1(d) characteristics, to what extent and at what added cost. Deposit and refund terms are reviewed by counsel before use. Residents are given the agreement in time to review it and ask questions, as part of the admission interview required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13.

definitions.definition: The written contract between the resident (or representative) and [AGENCY NAME] that sets out services, charges, rights and discharge terms.
The room, board and basic services included in the base monthly charge, as listed in the agreement.

Characteristics that allow, but do not require, moving a resident: need for 24-hour nursing supervision; bedridden for more than 14 days; totally dependent in four or more activities of daily living; severe cognitive decline; stage 3 or 4 pressure sores or multiple stage 2 sores; need for more than assistance with transfer; danger to self or others; unstable condition. A single stage 2 sore must be retained with a plan of care.
A transfer or discharge the facility initiates without the resident's agreement (see ADM-06).

procedures: Before submitting the license application, the Administrator and counsel finalize the admission agreement and check it against N.J.A.C. 8:36, the Certificate of Need conditions and State and federal law. The Administrator includes a copy in the application sent to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program (CNandLicensing; CNLapps@doh.nj.gov).

Charges (2.2(c)1): the agreement lists a rate schedule for room, board, each level of service and care, and each additional service not in the standard package, with the price or pricing method for each. The schedule is attached as an exhibit and dated.

Charge changes (2.2(c)2): the agreement states the agency gives at least 30 days' written notice before any increase, delivered by hand or mail to the resident and representative with a receipt record. It states the resident has the right to request written justification of an increase.
When a resident requests justification, the Administrator provides a written explanation of the reason and calculation within 10 business days, and the request and answer are filed.

Discharge appeal (2.2(c)3): the agreement states that the resident may appeal an involuntary discharge as set out at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.14(b), and describes the appeal process in ADM-06, including the written notice with reason and right to appeal.

Discharge criteria (2.2(c)4): the agreement lists the 5.1(d) criteria that the agency will use to discharge residents, and explains that the Administrator decides after consulting the RN, the attending physician and the social worker or designee. The resident and representative are invited to every meeting and can speak, bring a person of their choice and propose alternatives.

Retention under 5.1(e): the agreement states whether the agency retains a resident who has any 5.1(d) characteristic, to what extent, and what additional charge applies, consistent with GOV-02, ADM-02 and ADM-05. Residents needing specialized long-term care are transferred as ADM-05 states.

The agreement states that the agency gives written notice of at least 30 days of a facility-requested transfer or discharge, except in an emergency, as in RR-01, and that the notice includes the Ombudsman's name, address and phone.

The agreement states how MLTSS residents are billed: Medicaid pays covered care services to the plan and does not pay room and board, and the resident cost share is billed per the plan and county determination (GOV-07, ADM-07, RR-04).

Deposits and refunds: the agreement states in plain language any deposit or fee, what it covers, the conditions for refund, and the number of days in which refunds are made ([REFUND PERIOD IN DAYS]). Counsel approves this text before use. A refund of a deposit or prepaid charges is made in writing to the resident or estate, with an accounting of any deduction.

Review step: at the admission interview (ADM-01), the Administrator or designee reads or summarizes the agreement, answers questions, offers a copy to take home, and allows the resident or representative time to consult family, counsel or an advocate before signing.

Signing: the resident or authorized representative signs and dates the agreement. The Administrator signs for the agency. A copy is given to the resident, and the original is placed in the record (REC-01). The agency does not require a signature as a condition of receiving rights or emergency care.
Emergency-contact information is voluntary. The agency does not deny admission if a resident declines to give it, and notes the refusal in the record.

If the agreement is changed in a material way after DOH review, the Administrator sends the revised agreement to the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program and uses it only for new admissions until reviewed. Existing residents receive notice of changes as the agreement states.
The Administrator reviews the agreement and rate schedule at least annually with counsel and documents the review (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Prepare and submit the agreement to DOH, ensure required content, explain it at admission and respond to justification requests.
Review the agreement, deposit and refund terms and any material change before use.
Deliver notices of charge changes, process deposits and refunds, and keep signed agreements.

responsibilities.role: Registered nurse and social worker or designee
responsibilities.duty: Take part in decisions about 5.1(d) criteria and discharge, and support resident participation.

documentation: Admission agreement and rate schedule as submitted to the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program
Signed agreement in each resident record
Notices of charge changes with delivery proof
Written justification requests and responses
Deposit receipts and refund accountings
Annual agreement review record

policies.title: Resident Funds, Personal Needs Allowance and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; residents who ask the agency to hold funds, MLTSS residents with a personal needs allowance, and all staff handling money or property
policies.purpose: To protect residents' money and belongings, make sure the personal needs allowance remains available to the resident, and prevent loss, theft and exploitation.
policies.policy: Residents control their own money and property. [AGENCY NAME] holds resident funds only on the resident's written request or the written request of the resident's legally authorized representative, keeps them separate from agency funds, and gives receipts and a statement at least quarterly. For MLTSS residents, the personal needs allowance is the resident's money and is used only as the resident directs. The DMAHS figures effective 1/1/2026 are room $996.40 per month and personal needs $147.65 per month; the agency verifies the current amounts before billing each year. Medicaid does not pay room and board. The agency keeps an inventory of each resident's personal property at admission and at discharge. Staff may not borrow from, sell to, be a beneficiary of, or hold a power of attorney for a resident, and any suspected misuse is reported under SAF-01 as exploitation. These protections are consistent with the resident's right to confidential treatment of information and freedom from abuse and exploitation (N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a); RR-01). The agency's written personal needs allowance policy follows the current N.J.A.C. 8:36 provisions on resident charges and funds, and counsel confirms the current rule text before this policy is finalized.

definitions.definition: A separate account or ledger, apart from agency operating funds, in which money held for residents is kept, with an individual record for each resident.
The monthly amount a Medicaid-eligible resident keeps for personal use after the room charge is paid ($147.65 per month effective 1/1/2026).
Clothing, furnishings, jewelry, electronics, devices and other items belonging to the resident.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator or designee explains that the resident may keep, manage and spend their own money and may ask the agency to hold funds. The agency does not require the resident to deposit funds as a condition of admission.

To hold funds, the resident or authorized representative signs a written consent form stating the amount, purpose and how the resident can withdraw money. The form is filed in the record, and a copy is given to the resident.

Funds are kept in a separate resident funds account or ledger, never mixed with agency funds. Each resident has an individual ledger showing every deposit and withdrawal with date, amount, purpose and balance.
For every deposit or withdrawal, the staff member issues a numbered receipt. The resident or representative signs, and a second staff member witnesses withdrawals over [WITNESS THRESHOLD AMOUNT].
A resident may withdraw funds on request during business hours, or within one business day of the request, and is never required to explain the purpose.

The Administrator reviews and signs the funds reconciliation monthly, and the resident receives an itemized statement at least quarterly, in a format the resident can understand. Differences are investigated immediately.

MLTSS residents: the billing designee confirms the current room and personal needs figures with DMAHS or the plan each year ($996.40 and $147.65 per month effective 1/1/2026). The agency charges no more than the amounts allowed and gives the resident the remaining personal needs allowance on request or deposits it as the resident directs.

Charges for additional services (hair care, transportation, supplies) may be taken from resident funds only if the resident or representative authorizes them in advance in writing and the service is listed in the admission agreement (RR-03).

At admission, two staff members, with the resident or representative, inventory the resident's personal property on a signed form. Items of value are photographed if the resident agrees. New items are added to the list as the resident brings them.

The agency provides a lockable space in the resident's room and, on request, a locked area for valuables. It explains that it is not liable for items the resident chooses to keep but will investigate any loss.

At discharge, transfer or death, two staff members review the inventory with the resident or representative or, in a death, the person legally entitled to the property. The resident funds balance is paid out within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days of discharge, with a final accounting, and a signed receipt is kept (see HLT-10).

Staff may not borrow from, sell to, accept gifts of value from, or be named beneficiary or agent of a resident. A suspected violation is reported to the Administrator at once and handled under SAF-01 and STF-06.

Loss or theft reports: the staff member who learns of a missing item records it on an incident report, the Administrator investigates within 24 hours, informs the resident and, if theft or exploitation is suspected, reports under SAF-01 and SAF-02.
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually (GOV-05), including the current DMAHS room and personal needs figures.

responsibilities.duty: Oversee funds, sign monthly reconciliations, investigate losses and ensure no staff conflicts of interest.
Maintain the funds account and ledgers, issue receipts and quarterly statements, and verify current Medicaid figures.
Inventory property at admission and discharge with the resident and file signed lists.
Never take, borrow or manage a resident's money or property, and report any loss or suspected exploitation immediately.

documentation: Written consent to hold funds
Individual resident ledgers and numbered receipts
Monthly reconciliations signed by the Administrator
Quarterly resident fund statements
Signed property inventories at admission and discharge
Loss or theft incident reports and investigation notes
Annual confirmation of DMAHS room and personal needs figures

policies.title: Advance Directives and Resident Choice
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all residents and representatives, and all staff
policies.purpose: To make sure residents are asked about advance directives and health care representatives, that valid directives are honored, and that residents make their own choices about their care and providers.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] respects each resident's right to make decisions about their own care, including the right to accept or refuse treatment and to choose among available providers, as part of the rights in N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a) (see RR-01). At admission the agency asks whether the resident has an advance directive or has named a health care representative, and records the answer. The agency honors a valid directive and a valid health care representative's decisions within the limits of the law (45 CFR 164.502(g) governs when a personal representative may receive health information). The agency does not require or prohibit an advance directive as a condition of admission. Staff do not witness, draft or give legal advice about advance directives. A copy is kept in the record and sent with the resident to EMS or the hospital at transfer. The agency's decisions follow the physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant's statement of the resident's appropriateness for this level of care and the health assessment and service plan (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2). Counsel confirms the current New Jersey advance directive statute text before this policy is finalized.

definitions.definition: A written statement, such as a living will or health care proxy, in which a resident states wishes about future medical care or names a person to decide when the resident cannot.
A person the resident has named, or the law identifies, to make health care decisions when the resident cannot.
A medical order signed by the resident's physician or advanced practice nurse, such as a POLST form, that EMS and other providers can follow.

procedures: At the admission interview (ADM-01), the admission staff member asks every resident, in plain language, whether they have an advance directive, a health care proxy or any portable medical order, and records the response on the admission checklist.

If the resident has a document, staff copy it, with the resident's permission, and place the copy in the record (REC-01). The original stays with the resident or representative. The record shows the date received.

If the resident does not have one, the staff member offers written information and suggests the resident discuss it with their physician, attorney or family. Staff do not draft, advise on content, or witness the document.
Admission is neither granted nor denied because a resident has, or does not have, an advance directive.

The Administrator or designee records the name and contact information of any health care representative or guardian. Staff share health information with a representative only to the extent the law, 45 CFR 164.502(g) and RR-06 allow, and confirm the representative's authority by reviewing the document.

The RN reviews the directive and any portable medical order with the attending physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant at the health care assessment (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2), and notes it on the health service plan (ADM-04).

Residents may revise or revoke an advance directive at any time. Staff who learn of a change inform the RN, replace the document in the record, and note the date. Documents are reviewed with the resident at each reassessment and when there is a significant change in condition.

In an emergency, staff call 911 first (SAF-05, HLT-05). Staff follow a valid directive or portable medical order as written, and give EMS a copy. If the directive's validity is unclear, staff begin emergency care and call the physician while EMS responds.

At transfer to a hospital, staff send a copy of the directive and any portable medical order, the health service plan summary and the health care representative's contact information with the resident, and record that they did.

Resident choice: the Administrator and RN support the resident's choice of physician, dentist, pharmacy and other providers, and record choices in the record. For MLTSS residents, the plan's care manager is involved in service planning, and the resident's choice of qualified providers is respected.
If a resident with capacity refuses care, staff explain risks, document the refusal and the explanation, inform the physician, and, if safety is involved, use a managed risk agreement (ADM-04).

Staff are trained on this policy at orientation and each year (STF-03). The Administrator reviews it at least annually, with counsel confirming the New Jersey statute text, and documents the review (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensure the question is asked at every admission, designate a representative contact, and review this policy annually with counsel.
Review directives with the practitioner, reflect them in the health service plan and ensure they go with the resident at transfer.
Ask the question, copy documents and record responses.
Honor valid directives, call 911 in emergencies, never witness or draft directives, and refer questions to the RN.

documentation: Admission checklist showing the advance directive question and the resident's answer
Copies of advance directives, health care proxies and portable medical orders
Record of health care representative or guardian authority
Health service plan notation
Transfer documentation showing the directive was sent
Records of refusals of care and managed risk agreements
Training sign-in sheets and annual policy review

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality, Release of Records and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all staff, contractors, volunteers and students with access to resident information
policies.purpose: To protect the confidentiality of resident information, to let residents and other authorized persons examine resident records, and to ensure records leave the facility only with the resident's consent or as required by law or a third-party payor.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)5 (policies and procedures for maintaining confidentiality of resident records, including examination of records by the resident and other authorized persons and release of records to any individual outside the facility or program, as consented to by the resident or as required by law or third-party payor). Confidential treatment of information is a resident right under N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a), item 27, and [AGENCY NAME] posts and distributes it with the statement of resident rights (see RR-01). Resident information is used and disclosed only as the resident (or authorized representative) consents, as the law requires, or as a third-party payor requires. The facility follows the HIPAA Privacy Rule to the extent it applies, including the notice of privacy practices (45 CFR 164.520), the right of access (45 CFR 164.524) and the administrative requirements (45 CFR 164.530): a designated privacy official, workforce training, safeguards, a complaint process and sanctions. Access to records is limited by job role. Records are kept secure at all times and are available to DOH representatives on request.

definitions.definition: All paper and electronic information about a resident, including the admission agreement, assessments, service plans, medication records, progress notes, incident reports and billing records.

The resident; a court-appointed guardian; an agent under a power of attorney or health care proxy acting within that authority; and any family member, designated responsible individual or other person the resident has approved in writing.
The person designated by the Administrator to oversee this policy and receive privacy complaints. Unless another person is named, this is the Administrator.
Disclosing only the information needed for the stated purpose, except for treatment disclosures and disclosures to the resident.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Privacy Officer in writing ([PRIVACY OFFICER NAME], [PHONE]) and posts that person's name and phone number with the notice of privacy practices.

At admission, the admission staff member gives the resident or representative the notice of privacy practices, explains it, and obtains a signed acknowledgment for the record. If no signature can be obtained, staff document the attempt. The notice is posted in the lobby and given to anyone who asks.

The Administrator maintains a written role-based access list. Care staff see only the records of residents they serve. Business-office staff see billing and admission records. The Administrator, RN and Privacy Officer have full access. Staff must not look at records outside their duties.

Paper records are kept in locked cabinets in [RECORD STORAGE LOCATION], which are locked whenever unattended. Electronic records require unique user IDs and passwords, automatic log-off, and no shared log-ins. Records, MARs and charts are never left in dining rooms, hallways or other public areas.

Every employee, volunteer and contractor signs a confidentiality statement at hire and completes privacy training at orientation and annually (documented under STF-03). Violations lead to discipline up to termination under STF-06.

Residents and authorized persons may examine the resident's record. The request is made to the Administrator, orally or in writing; staff offer a request form but do not require it. The Administrator verifies identity and authority and files any guardianship, power of attorney or proxy document in the record.

The Administrator or RN arranges the review in a private area, with staff present to keep the record intact and to answer questions. Review is arranged promptly. Copies are provided within 30 days of the request, and the Administrator may take one 30-day extension only after giving the resident a written reason and a completion date (45 CFR 164.524).

Copies are provided in the form requested, including electronic form where the record is kept electronically. Any fee is limited to the reasonable cost of copying, postage and preparing a summary the resident agreed to. No fee is charged for the resident to inspect the record.

If any part of a request is denied, the Administrator gives a written denial with the reason and the resident's review and complaint rights, and the denial is filed in the record. Denials are rare and are reviewed with the facility's legal counsel before issuance.

Before releasing records to anyone outside the facility, staff obtain a written authorization signed and dated by the resident or representative. It must name the recipient, describe the information to be released, state the purpose, and give an expiration date. The resident may revoke it in writing at any time.

Records may be released without a new authorization only to (a) DOH representatives and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman during surveys and complaint investigations; (b) the DOH Complaints Program (1-800-792-9770) and, for residents 60 or older, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (1-877-582-6995) when reporting abuse, neglect or exploitation (see SAF-01); (c) treating physicians, hospitals, hospice and home health providers for treatment and transfers (see HLT-05); (d) the NJ FamilyCare MLTSS plan and the State for payment, care management and audit purposes, limited to the minimum necessary; and (e) others as required by law, subpoena or court order, after the Privacy Officer verifies the legal basis.

The Privacy Officer or designee records each release outside the facility in the record's disclosure log: date, recipient, information released, purpose, authorization or legal basis, and the staff member who released it.

Staff answering phone or in-person inquiries do not confirm that a person lives in the facility, or share any information about them, unless the resident has agreed to be listed in the facility directory or has authorized the caller. Staff take a message and pass it to the resident.

Staff do not photograph or record residents or post their information on social media or personal devices without the resident's written consent. Resident names are not posted in public areas unless the resident agrees.

Any suspected improper use or disclosure, including lost records, misdirected faxes or e-mails, and unauthorized access, is reported to the Privacy Officer the same day. The Privacy Officer investigates, documents the facts, mitigates harm, applies sanctions, and makes any notifications the HIPAA breach rules and other law require.

Residents may complain about privacy practices to the Privacy Officer or through the grievance process (RR-02), and to DOH or the Ombudsman. No resident is threatened or retaliated against for complaining.
Record retention and storage follow REC-01. The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually as part of the manual review (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the Privacy Officer, approves the access list, ensures records are available to DOH, approves releases required by law, and reviews this policy annually.
Provides the notice of privacy practices, handles access requests and complaints, investigates breaches, maintains the disclosure log, and oversees training.
Supports record review by residents and representatives and releases clinical information to treating providers during transfers.
Protect resident information, access only what their role requires, sign the confidentiality statement, and report suspected breaches immediately.

documentation: Signed notice-of-privacy-practices acknowledgment in each resident record
Written role-based access list
Signed staff confidentiality statements and privacy training records
Record access/review request forms and denial letters
Signed authorizations for release of information
Disclosure log
Breach investigation and notification files
Annual policy review record

policies.title: Nondiscrimination, Language Access and Interpretation Services
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; all staff, with emphasis on admissions, nursing and front-desk staff
policies.purpose: To ensure that applicants and residents are treated without discrimination, that residents with limited English proficiency, hearing, vision or other communication needs can understand and take part in their care, and that interpretation services are provided and documented.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin (including limited English proficiency), disability, age, sex, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status or source of payment, and complies with Title VI (42 USC 2000d), the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101) and 45 CFR 92 to the extent they apply. Admission decisions rest on the admission criteria and the services the facility is capable of providing (see ADM-01 and GOV-02), never on protected status. The facility provides reasonable accommodations, auxiliary aids and free language assistance so residents can understand the statement of resident rights, the admission agreement and their care, and so they can exercise the rights in N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a). The facility provides interpretation services as the licensing rules require. The Administrator confirms the current requirement at each annual manual review. Nondiscrimination and language-assistance notices are posted conspicuously. Each use of an interpreter is documented. No resident is threatened or retaliated against for complaining about discrimination (N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a), item 40).

definitions.definition: A limited ability to speak, read, write or understand English well enough to take part in care or services without assistance.

A person who is fluent in English and the resident's language, trained in interpreting, and bound by confidentiality. This may be a staff member designated and trained for the role, a contracted interpreter, or a telephone or video interpreting service.
Services and devices that allow effective communication with people with disabilities, such as sign language interpreters, large print, amplified phones, captioning and screen readers.

A change in a rule, policy, practice or service that gives a person with a disability an equal opportunity to use and enjoy the facility, unless it would be a fundamental alteration or an undue burden.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Civil Rights/Language Access Coordinator ([COORDINATOR NAME], [PHONE]) to oversee this policy and receive discrimination complaints.

The Administrator contracts for telephone or video interpretation covering the languages common in the facility's service area, and for sign language interpretation on request. The vendor, access instructions and 24-hour phone number are posted at the nurses' station, the front desk and the med room.

During pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the admission staff member asks every applicant and representative their preferred language for written and spoken communication, and any hearing, vision, speech or cognitive communication needs. The answers are recorded on the screening form and the face sheet.

At admission, the Administrator or designee gives the resident or representative the statement of resident rights, the admission agreement and the notice of privacy practices in the resident's language where available, or reads and explains them through a qualified interpreter. The resident's understanding is confirmed and documented.

Staff use a qualified interpreter for the admission interview, the RN assessment, service plan meetings, consent discussions, medication teaching, change-of-condition conversations, discharge or transfer notices, and grievance meetings.

Staff do not require or pressure a resident to use a family member or friend as interpreter. If the resident chooses to, the choice is documented. A minor is not used as an interpreter except in an emergency where no qualified interpreter is immediately available.
Staff who are bilingual may interpret only after the Administrator confirms and documents their language competence and training in interpreter ethics and confidentiality.

For residents with hearing, vision, speech or cognitive impairments, the RN identifies the auxiliary aids needed during assessment and lists them in the service plan (ADM-04). The Administrator provides them at no charge to the resident.

Requests for reasonable accommodation, whether made orally or in writing, are given to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator responds within [RESPONSE TIMEFRAME, NOT TO EXCEED 10 BUSINESS DAYS] and documents the decision. If an accommodation is denied, the Administrator gives a written reason and offers an alternative.

Each time an interpreter or auxiliary aid is used, the staff member records in the resident record the date, the language or aid, the interpreter's name or ID number, the topic, and whether the interpretation was in person, by phone or by video.

The Administrator posts, in the lobby and other common areas, the notice of nondiscrimination and the language-assistance notice, in English and the languages most commonly spoken locally, together with the resident rights and complaint agency information (DOH 1-800-792-9770; State Long-Term Care Ombudsman 1-877-582-6995).

Key documents (rights, admission agreement summary, grievance procedure, evacuation instructions, menus and the activity calendar) are translated or interpreted for residents who need it. The Administrator keeps a list of the translated documents.

Applicants who are denied admission receive the same written reason, on request, as described in ADM-01. The Administrator reviews each denial to confirm it was based on the admission criteria and the facility's capability and not on protected status.
Any resident, applicant or family member may complain of discrimination or language access problems through RR-02. The Coordinator investigates and responds in writing. No retaliation is permitted.
Staff receive training on this policy at orientation and annually (STF-03), including how to reach the interpreter service and how to treat residents with dignity regardless of background.
The Coordinator reviews interpreter-use logs and complaints at least annually, reports to the QI committee (GOV-06), and updates this policy as part of the annual manual review (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures nondiscrimination, contracts for interpreter services, grants or denies accommodation requests, posts required notices, and confirms current interpretation requirements annually.
Receives complaints, maintains the interpreter vendor list and logs, and reports to the QI committee.
Record language and communication needs and arrange interpretation for admission documents and interviews.
Identify auxiliary aid needs, use qualified interpreters for care communication, and document each use.

documentation: Language and communication needs on the screening form and face sheet
Interpreter-use entries in the resident record
Interpreter vendor contract and instructions
Accommodation request log with decisions
Copies of posted notices and translated documents
Complaint files and QI review notes
Training attendance records

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening, Admission Interview and Denial of Admission
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; Administrator, admission staff and RN
policies.purpose: To admit only applicants whose needs the facility can meet, to give applicants clear information before they decide, and to document the admission interview, the physician's statement of appropriateness, and any denial.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] admits applicants whose assessed needs fall within the services the facility is capable of providing (GOV-02, N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1) and who are not barred by the conditions in ADM-05. Within 30 days before admission, a physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant must state in writing that the applicant is appropriate for this level of care (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(a)). The Administrator or designee interviews the resident at or before admission, and the resident's family, guardian or agency too if the resident agrees. The interview covers policies, business hours, fees, services, resident rights and admission and discharge criteria, and is documented in the record (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(a)). Emergency-contact information is voluntary, and admission is never denied because an applicant declines to give it (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(b)). If an applicant's behavior shows danger to self or others and the facility cannot provide proper care, the attending or on-call physician decides on placement and mental health screening is initiated under N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 10:31 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(c)). An applicant denied admission after submitting a written application receives, on written request, a signed written reason within 15 days of the facility's receipt of the request (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(d)). Decisions are made without discrimination (RR-07). The admission agreement states whether the facility retains nursing-home-level residents, to what extent and at what added cost (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(e); see RR-03 and ADM-02).

definitions.definition: A person who has asked to be admitted, directly or through a representative, hospital, agency or managed care plan.
The facility's signed application or referral packet submitted by or for the applicant. A denial after a written application triggers the 15-day written-reason right on request.
A written statement, dated within 30 days before admission, by a physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant that the applicant is appropriate for this level of care.

The documented meeting at or before admission between the Administrator or designee and the applicant (and family, guardian or agency if the applicant agrees) covering the topics required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(a).

procedures: Admission staff log every inquiry and application on the Pre-Admission Log, recording the date, source of referral, payer source (private pay, NJ FamilyCare MLTSS or other) and the staff member responsible.

Admission staff give each prospective resident a copy of the services description (GOV-02), the fee schedule, the admission agreement, the statement of resident rights and the admission and discharge criteria. They offer a facility tour and tell the applicant and family of the right to see the policy manual (GOV-05).

The Administrator or RN conducts a pre-admission screening, by visit or phone, covering diagnoses, medications, ADL needs, cognition, behaviors, continence, skin condition, mobility and fall history, special diets, treatments, use of tobacco, substance use and any history of wandering or aggression. The screening is recorded on the Pre-Admission Screening Form.

The RN reviews the screening and any hospital, physician or plan records, and compares the applicant's needs with the services the facility provides, current staffing (STF-01) and the conditions the facility cannot serve (ADM-05). The Administrator makes the final admission decision, consulting the RN.

Before admission, the facility must obtain the written appropriateness statement from the physician, advanced practice nurse or physician assistant. The statement must be dated no more than 30 days before the admission date. An older statement is not accepted. The statement is filed in the record. No resident is admitted without it.

For applicants whose behavior shows danger to self or others, the Administrator does not admit them if the facility cannot provide proper care. The attending or on-call physician decides on placement and the Administrator initiates mental health screening under N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 10:31. The Administrator documents the call, the physician's decision and the referral.

The Administrator or designee holds the admission interview at or before admission, with the resident and, if the resident agrees, the family, guardian or referring agency. The interview covers facility policies, business hours, fees and what is and is not included, services, resident rights, and admission and discharge criteria (see ADM-05 and ADM-06). The resident's agreement to include others is documented.

The interviewer documents the interview in the resident record: date, who attended, topics covered, the materials given, and the resident's questions and understanding. Interpretation is arranged where needed (RR-07).

The Administrator reviews the admission agreement with the resident or representative, including the nursing-home-level retention provision and added cost, and obtains signatures (RR-03). The resident may take time to review and may consult family or counsel.

The facility asks for emergency-contact information but tells the applicant that providing it is voluntary. If the applicant declines, staff record 'declined' on the face sheet and proceed with admission.
At admission, the Administrator and the resident arrange which physician and dentist will be called for the resident (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(a)) and record those names and phone numbers on the face sheet.

On the admission date, the RN completes the initial assessment (ADM-03), staff inventory personal belongings (RR-04), give the resident the privacy notice (RR-06), and begin the interim service plan (ADM-04).

If the facility decides not to admit an applicant, the Administrator tells the applicant or representative promptly, in plain language, and notes the reason in the Pre-Admission Log. For an applicant who submitted a written application, the Administrator explains the right to request the reason in writing.

When a denied applicant asks in writing for the reason, the Administrator writes down the date the request was received, prepares a written statement of the specific reason (for example, needs exceed the services the facility is capable of providing under ADM-05), signs it, and sends it so it reaches the applicant within 15 days of the date of receipt. A copy and the proof of delivery are kept in the denial file.

The Administrator keeps a denial file for each denied applicant with the application, screening form, the basis of the decision and any correspondence. The file is kept as REC-01 provides. The Administrator reviews all denials quarterly to confirm they were consistent with the criteria and nondiscriminatory (RR-07), and reports to the QI committee (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Makes admission and denial decisions, conducts or delegates the admission interview, signs written denial reasons within the 15-day deadline, and arranges mental health screening referrals.
Screens clinical needs, confirms that needs fit the facility's capability, and completes the initial assessment on admission.
Maintain the log, give out materials, collect documents and check that the physician's statement is dated within 30 days.
Decides placement for an applicant whose behavior endangers self or others and for whom proper care is not possible.

documentation: Pre-Admission Log
Pre-Admission Screening Form
Physician, APN or PA appropriateness statement dated within 30 days before admission
Documented admission interview in the resident record
Face sheet noting voluntary emergency contact and the resident's chosen physician and dentist
Signed admission agreement
Denial file, including written request, written reason, and proof of delivery within 15 days
Records of mental health screening referral and physician decision, where applicable

policies.title: Nursing-Home-Level Access, Medicaid-Eligible Occupancy and CPCH SSI Commitments
policies.applies_to: ALR and CPCH (Section on SSI commitment applies to CPCH only); Administrator, admission staff, business office and RN
policies.purpose: To keep the facility's license commitments on access for residents with nursing-home-level needs, Medicaid-eligible occupancy, and (for CPCHs) SSI-eligible residents, and to monitor and report them accurately.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(e)7 (statement of the licensed operator's commitment to assuring access to assisted living for individuals with nursing home level of care needs). [AGENCY NAME] commits that, within 36 months after licensure, at least 20 percent of its residents will be individuals with nursing-home-level care needs, computed on the number of resident days per calendar year and including both direct admissions and residents who are maintained after developing nursing-home-level needs. A newly licensed ALR or CPCH licensed on or after 9/1/2001 must reach at least 10 percent Medicaid-eligible occupancy within 3 years of licensure and maintain it. Beds added later must be 10 percent Medicaid-occupied. A facility with fewer than 10 beds reserves at least one bed for a Medicaid-eligible resident (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(h)-(l)). The Commissioner may waive or reduce the Medicaid requirement, and must waive it if funding is limited. A request is made in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7. If the facility is a CPCH, at least 5 percent of residents each year must be SSI-eligible, and at least half of them former psychiatric patients; the percentage is computed on resident days per calendar year and reported to the CN&L Program by April 15 for the prior year (N.J.A.C. 8:36-22.7). The facility monitors all percentages monthly and keeps the supporting records available for survey. These commitments are met through nondiscriminatory admission and retention decisions and without lowering the quality of care.

definitions.definition: A resident who meets the definition in N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3 and whose record documents one or more of the characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d): needs 24-hour nursing supervision; bedridden for more than 14 days; totally dependent in 4 or more ADLs; severe cognitive decline; stage 3 or 4 pressure sores or multiple stage 2 sores; needs more than assistance with transfer; is a danger to self or others; or has an unstable condition.
The total number of days residents occupied beds in the calendar year, counted nightly from the census; the basis for the percentage calculations.
The share of occupied beds held by residents eligible for NJ FamilyCare (Medicaid), measured against the facility's occupancy as the licensing rules specify.
A resident who qualifies for Supplemental Security Income. At least half of the 5 percent must be former psychiatric patients.

The per diem add-on under P.L. 2023, c.80, set by yearly average Medicaid census measured from paid claims against total licensed beds: $10 at 15% to under 30%, $15 at 30% to under 50%, $30 at 50% to under 70%, and $35 at 70% or more.

procedures: The Administrator records the facility's commitments in a Compliance Commitments Register: the 20% nursing-home-level access commitment and the 36-month date counted from the license issue date; the 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy requirement and its 3-year date; the CPCH 5% SSI commitment (if applicable); and the April 15 reporting date.

The business office keeps a daily census listing each resident's payer status (private pay, Medicaid-eligible/NJ FamilyCare MLTSS, SSI) and admission and discharge dates, so resident days can be computed for any period.

The RN determines at admission and at every reassessment (ADM-03) whether the resident has any of the eight nursing-home-level characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d), and documents which one(s) and the date in the record.

The RN keeps a Nursing-Home-Level Roster listing each resident who qualifies, the characteristic(s), the date the status began and ended, and whether the resident was admitted at that level or became so while living in the facility (maintained resident).

Within the first 5 business days of each month, the Administrator and business office compute, for the prior month and year to date, resident days of nursing-home-level residents divided by total resident days, and (for the license commitments) Medicaid-eligible occupancy and, if a CPCH, SSI-eligible resident days and former-psychiatric-patient resident days. Results are entered in the Register.

The Administrator compares results with the targets: 20% nursing-home-level by month 36 after licensure; 10% Medicaid-eligible by year 3 and afterwards; 5% SSI (CPCH). If any measure trends below the glide path to its target, the Administrator documents a corrective plan within 10 business days (for example, outreach to hospitals, MLTSS plans and county agencies; review of admission barriers).

The facility does not refuse or delay an applicant because of NJ FamilyCare, SSI or nursing-home-level status if the applicant meets the admission criteria and the facility can serve the person (ADM-01, ADM-05, RR-07). A resident who becomes Medicaid-eligible while living in the facility is not asked to leave for that reason.

The admission agreement states whether the facility retains nursing-home-level residents, to what extent and at what added cost, as N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(e) requires (RR-03). The Administrator reviews the statement against this policy and the facility's capability (GOV-02) at each annual review. Residents who need specialized long-term care the facility cannot provide are transferred (ADM-05, ADM-06).

For beds added after initial licensure, the Administrator reserves and tracks the added beds so that 10% of them are Medicaid-occupied. If the facility has fewer than 10 beds, the Administrator reserves at least one bed for a Medicaid-eligible resident and records the reservation in the Register.

If the facility will not meet the 10% Medicaid requirement or needs reduction, the Administrator prepares a written waiver request to the Director of the CN&L Program under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7. It documents the reasons and the efforts made, and a copy and DOH's response are kept in the Register. Requests are filed before the compliance date.

If the facility is a CPCH, the Administrator compiles the prior calendar year's SSI-eligible resident days and the portion for former psychiatric patients, and submits the report to the CN&L Program by April 15 [CN&L SUBMISSION METHOD AS DIRECTED BY DOH]. A copy and proof of submission are retained. Preparation begins by March 1.

The Administrator uses the annual average Medicaid census (paid claims against total licensed beds) to understand where the facility sits relative to the per diem tiers and to plan billing and cash flow (ADM-07). Tier results are never a reason to select or reject applicants.
The Administrator presents all percentages, trends and corrective actions to the QI committee at least quarterly (GOV-06) and reports annual figures to the governing body (GOV-01).

Admission and acuity records, the Register, rosters and census are kept in a secure location, available for DOH survey at any time (REC-02, REC-01). The Administrator updates the policy after any change in the commitments or DOH direction.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the Compliance Commitments Register, reviews monthly figures, files waiver requests and the CPCH April 15 report, and reports to the governing body.
Identifies and documents nursing-home-level status at admission and reassessment, and maintains the Nursing-Home-Level Roster.
Maintains the daily census by payer status and computes resident-day percentages monthly.
Reviews annual results and approves corrective plans and waiver requests.

documentation: Compliance Commitments Register with dates and targets
Daily census by payer status
Nursing-Home-Level Roster with RN documentation of characteristics
Monthly percentage worksheets
Corrective action plans
Waiver request (N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7) and DOH response, if any
CPCH SSI report and proof of submission by April 15
QI committee minutes showing review

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; Registered Nurse, Administrator and care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident's needs are identified by a registered nurse at admission, fully assessed within 14 days when needs exist, and reassessed whenever needs change, as the basis for the health service plan.
policies.policy: A registered professional nurse (RN) completes an initial assessment of every resident upon admission to determine the resident's needs (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.1(a)). If the initial assessment shows health care needs, the RN completes a health care assessment within 14 days of admission using the DOH instrument or an equivalent (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(c)). The assessment covers activities of daily living (ADLs), cognition, communication and hearing, vision, physical functioning, continence, psychosocial well-being, mood and behavior, and activity patterns (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(d)). Each resident has an RN assessment and care plan (N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2). At least one RN must be available at all times (N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2). The facility defines what availability means for coverage and response time in HLT-04. The facility reassesses on any change of condition and at the periodic interval required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.1(b)-(f). The Administrator confirms that interval against the current rule text before opening and at each annual review. For residents in NJ FamilyCare MLTSS, the facility coordinates with the managed care plan's care manager on level-of-care and assessment documents.

definitions.definition: The RN's evaluation at admission to identify immediate needs, risks and the care required from day one.
The comprehensive RN assessment completed within 14 days of admission when the initial assessment identifies health care needs, using the DOH instrument or equivalent.

A noticeable decline or improvement in a resident's physical, cognitive, behavioral or psychosocial status, including a fall, new skin problem, weight change, new confusion, infection signs, or hospitalization.
The staff member of the resident's NJ FamilyCare MLTSS plan responsible for care management and the plan of care.

procedures: Before admission, the RN reviews the appropriateness statement (ADM-01), medication list, hospital discharge papers and any MLTSS plan documents, and prepares for the admission assessment.

On the admission date, the RN personally completes the initial assessment and records the date, time and RN signature. The assessment covers current health status, medications, allergies, skin condition, mobility, ADL status and immediate safety risks. If an RN is not on-site at admission, admission is deferred until an RN can complete the initial assessment.

The RN decides at the end of the initial assessment whether the resident has health care needs and records that finding and the reason. If yes, the RN schedules the full health care assessment immediately and enters the due date (admission date plus 14 days) on the assessment tracker.

The RN completes the health care assessment within 14 days using the DOH instrument or an equivalent form approved by the Administrator. It covers: ADLs; cognition; communication and hearing; vision; physical functioning; continence; psychosocial well-being; mood and behavior; and activity patterns.

The RN gets information directly from the resident, observation, the resident's physician orders, and family or representatives (with the resident's consent). Where language or sensory needs exist, interpretation or aids are used and documented (RR-07).

The RN screens for risks and, when found, triggers the related protocols: falls (HLT-07), skin integrity (HLT-08), cognition and wandering (HLT-06, SAF-03), medication self-administration ability (HLT-03), and nutrition and diet (DL-01).

The RN also checks whether the resident has any of the nursing-home-level characteristics listed in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d), records them, and updates the roster (ADM-02). The RN determines if any reason would prevent the facility from meeting the resident's needs and informs the Administrator (ADM-05).
The RN signs and dates the completed assessment, reviews it with the resident or representative, and files it in the record. The RN begins or updates the health service plan from it (ADM-04).

Staff report any change of condition to the RN the same shift. The RN evaluates the resident, notifies the physician and representative as required (HLT-05), and performs a reassessment of the affected areas within [RN REASSESSMENT TIMEFRAME, NOT TO EXCEED 3 BUSINESS DAYS] of the change, or immediately if urgent. The RN updates the service plan.

The RN reassesses every resident at the periodic interval, [REASSESSMENT INTERVAL], which must not exceed the interval required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.1. The tracker lists each resident's next due date; the Administrator reviews the tracker monthly for overdue items.

Reassessment is also required after a hospital stay or return from rehabilitation, after any fall with injury, on a new diagnosis or medication change that affects function, when a resident requests it, and when an incident suggests unmet needs.

For NJ FamilyCare MLTSS residents, the RN or Administrator sends the assessment and service plan to the plan care manager as required and requests the plan's level-of-care determination and plan of care. Staff record each contact with the care manager and keep the plan's documents in the record. Differences between the plan's authorization and the facility's assessment are raised with the care manager promptly (ADM-07).
The Administrator checks RN coverage against HLT-04 and the actual schedule to confirm that an RN is available to perform assessments on admission days and at all times.

The Administrator audits a sample of at least [NUMBER] records each quarter for timeliness and completeness of initial assessments, 14-day assessments and reassessments, and reports to the QI committee (GOV-06). Late assessments are corrected and root causes addressed.

responsibilities.duty: Completes initial, 14-day and periodic assessments and reassessments on change of condition; documents findings; updates the service plan.
Ensures RN coverage and assessment timeliness, approves the assessment instrument, confirms the periodic interval against the rule, and audits records.
Observe residents and report changes in condition to the RN the same shift.
Provides level-of-care determinations and the plan of care, and coordinates with the facility.

documentation: Initial RN assessment signed, dated and timed on the admission date
Health care assessment on the DOH instrument or equivalent, completed within 14 days
Reassessments after change of condition and at the periodic interval
Assessment tracker with due dates
Communications with the MLTSS care manager
Quarterly assessment audit results

policies.title: Health Service Plan / Care Plan and Managed Risk Agreements
policies.applies_to: ALR, CPCH and ALP; Registered Nurse, Administrator, care staff, residents and representatives
policies.purpose: To ensure that each resident has a written health service plan based on the RN assessment, developed with the resident and representative, reflecting the resident's choices, and that managed risk agreements are negotiated and documented when a resident's choice poses a high probability of risk.
policies.policy: A written health service plan is developed from the RN assessment for each resident (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(e)), and each resident has an RN assessment and care plan (N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2). The plan lists the services to be provided, the staff responsible for each and the dates it will be reviewed. The resident and the resident's representative take part in planning, and the resident's preferences and choices are documented. Plans for residents in NJ FamilyCare MLTSS are person-centered and consistent with the plan of care developed by the managed care plan, in line with 42 CFR 441.301(c). Staff follow the plan. When a resident's choice poses a high probability of risk, the facility seeks to negotiate a managed risk agreement with the resident rather than overriding the choice. The Administrator confirms the current licensing requirements for managed risk agreements at each annual manual review. The service plan is reviewed and revised at each reassessment (ADM-03) and on any change of condition.

definitions.definition: The written plan developed from the RN assessment that sets out the resident's needs, goals, services, responsible staff and review dates.
A short plan prepared on the admission date from the initial RN assessment, used until the full health service plan is completed.

A written agreement between the facility and a resident (or representative) that identifies a risk arising from the resident's choice, the possible consequences, the steps the facility and the resident will take to reduce the risk, and how the agreement will be reviewed.
A planning process directed by the resident, with people the resident chooses, that reflects the resident's strengths, preferences and goals.

procedures: On the admission date, the RN prepares an interim plan from the initial assessment listing immediate services, safety precautions, diet, medication assistance and special needs, and gives it to the care staff on each shift.

After the 14-day health care assessment is complete (ADM-03), the RN drafts the full health service plan from it. The plan is finalized by day 14 of admission, or sooner if the assessment is finished sooner.

The RN invites the resident and, with the resident's consent, family, the guardian or other representative, and (for MLTSS) the plan care manager to a service-planning meeting. The meeting is arranged at a time and place convenient to the resident, and interpretation or aids are provided where needed (RR-07).

At the meeting, the RN asks the resident about daily routines, preferences (wake and sleep times, bathing, meals, activities, privacy), goals, and what help the resident wants and does not want. The RN records these choices in the plan.

The health service plan states for each need: the problem or need, the resident's goal, the services and interventions, the frequency, the staff position responsible (RN, medication-trained staff, personal care assistant, dietary, activities, social work, or outside provider such as home health or hospice), and the date for review.

The plan addresses, as applicable, ADL assistance, medication assistance or supervision (HLT-03), falls (HLT-07), skin (HLT-08), cognition and wandering (HLT-06, SAF-03), nutrition and therapeutic diet (DL-01), activities (DL-02), psychosocial needs and social work (HLT-11), hospice or home health coordination (HLT-09) and advance directives (RR-05).

For residents in NJ FamilyCare MLTSS, the RN compares the facility's plan with the plan care manager's plan of care and resolves differences with the care manager before finalizing. The facility does not provide or bill services that conflict with the plan of care (ADM-07).

The resident or representative reviews the plan, may ask for changes, and signs to show participation and agreement. If the resident or representative disagrees or declines to sign, the RN records that and the reason, and the dispute is handled under RR-02. A copy of the plan, or a summary of it, is offered to the resident.

The RN places the plan in the record and reviews it with the staff who will deliver the services. Care staff access a care summary at the point of care. They report to the RN anything that is not working.

When a resident's choice creates a high probability of risk (for example, refusing assistance with transfers, declining a prescribed diet, or leaving the building unaccompanied despite safety concerns), the RN or Administrator first discusses the risk with the resident, explains consequences and alternatives, and checks the resident's decision-making capacity. The discussion is documented.

The RN or Administrator tries to negotiate a managed risk agreement that identifies the choice, the risk, the potential consequences, what the resident agrees to do, what the facility will do to reduce the risk and respect the choice, notification of the physician and representative as the resident agrees, and the date of review. The resident or representative and the facility sign it and it is filed in the record and summarized in the service plan.

A managed risk agreement does not allow the facility to withhold needed care, and it does not apply to conditions the facility cannot serve under ADM-05. If no agreement is reached, or the risk cannot be managed within the facility's capability, the Administrator and RN review the situation, consult the physician, and, if needed, start the process in ADM-05 and ADM-06.

The RN reviews each plan at each reassessment (ADM-03), on change of condition, after hospitalization, and at the dates set in the plan. Managed risk agreements are reviewed at least at each service plan review. Each review is signed and dated.

The Administrator audits a sample of at least [NUMBER] service plans and managed risk agreements each quarter for consistency with the assessment, resident participation, signatures and timely review, and reports to the QI committee (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Develops, updates and reviews the health service plan; leads planning meetings; negotiates managed risk agreements; and briefs staff.
Take part in planning, state preferences and choices, and review and sign the plan and any managed risk agreement.
Ensures plans are completed on time, signs managed risk agreements for the facility, resolves disputes, and audits plans.
Carry out the plan, report problems, and respect resident choices.
Provides the plan of care and works with the facility to align plans.

documentation: Interim plan dated on the admission date
Full health service plan with services, responsible staff and review dates
Record of the service-planning meeting and attendees
Resident or representative signature, or documentation of refusal and reason
Managed risk agreements and review notes
Correspondence with the MLTSS care manager and the plan of care
Quarterly plan audit results

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
policies.applies_to: Assisted Living Residence (ALR), Comprehensive Personal Care Home (CPCH) and Assisted Living Program (ALP) sites operated by [AGENCY NAME]; all residents, the administrator, nursing, social work and care staff
policies.purpose: To state when [AGENCY NAME] will keep a resident whose needs have increased, when it may move a resident, and which conditions it cannot serve. To describe how a retention or discharge decision is made, who takes part, and how the resident takes part.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(c)4 (specification of the N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) criteria used to discharge residents, and an explanation of how the discharge process is implemented, including which staff participate and the extent of resident participation).

1. Retention is the default. [AGENCY NAME] is capable of providing nursing services, including to nursing-home-level residents (see GOV-02), and has committed to serving residents with nursing-home-level needs (see ADM-02). A resident is never discharged only because needs have increased.

2. Criteria.
