[AGENCY NAME] may, but is not required to, move a resident when the resident's record documents one or more of the eight characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d): (1) the resident requires 24-hour, seven-day-a-week nursing supervision; (2) the resident is bedridden for more than 14 days; (3) the resident is totally dependent in four or more activities of daily living; (4) the resident has severe cognitive decline; (5) the resident has stage 3 or 4 pressure sores, or multiple stage 2 pressure sores; (6) the resident needs more than assistance with transfer; (7) the resident is a danger to self or others; (8) the resident's condition is unstable. A characteristic must be documented in the record before it is used as a basis for moving a resident. These are the only criteria [AGENCY NAME] will use under 5.1(d) to discharge a resident for care-need reasons.

3. Mandatory retention. A resident with a single stage 2 pressure sore must be retained, with a plan of care (see HLT-08 and ADM-04). A single stage 2 sore is never grounds for discharge.

4. Mandatory transfer. A resident who needs specialized long-term care must be transferred (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(f)). The administrator decides this with the attending physician and the RN, and documents it.

5. Danger to self or others. If a resident's behavior shows danger to self or others and the facility cannot provide proper care, the attending or on-call physician decides on placement and mental health screening is started under N.J.S.A. 30:4-27.1 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 10:31 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(c)). Staff call 911 first if there is immediate danger.

6. Admission agreement. Each admission agreement states whether [AGENCY NAME] will retain residents with the 5.1(d) characteristics, to what extent, and at what added cost (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(e); see RR-03).

7. Infirmary transfer. A temporary transfer to an infirmary requires the resident's consent and is generally limited to one week (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(e)).

8. How the process is implemented, who takes part, and how the resident takes part. A discharge based on a 5.1(d) criterion is decided case by case by an interdisciplinary review made up of the administrator (decision-maker), the RN, the attending physician or a physician designee, the social worker or designee, and the care staff who know the resident. The resident takes part throughout. The resident is invited to the review and may bring a family member, guardian or other representative. The resident's wishes are recorded, and the facility must respond to them. Where possible, the resident chooses the receiving setting. The resident may ask for reconsideration by the administrator. With the resident's consent, the family, guardian or designated person is included and the MLTSS care manager is told. The notice, appeal and relocation steps in ADM-06 then apply.

definitions.definition: The eight documented conditions in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) on which a resident may, but need not, be moved.
A resident whose care needs meet the nursing-home level, including one with one or more of the 5.1(d) characteristics, whom the facility is able to retain.
The documented meeting of administrator, RN, physician input, social work and care staff, with the resident taking part, that decides whether to retain or move a resident.
Care the facility cannot provide under its license and services description (see GOV-02), which requires transfer under 5.1(f).

procedures: The RN reassesses a resident within [NUMBER] days of any change of condition and at each scheduled reassessment (ADM-03). The RN records whether any of the eight 5.1(d) characteristics is present.
If a 5.1(d) characteristic is present, the RN notifies the administrator the same business day and writes a short summary of the finding in the resident record.

The administrator convenes an interdisciplinary retention review within [NUMBER] business days. Participants are the administrator, RN, social worker or designee, a direct care representative, and the attending physician or a physician designee (by phone or in writing).

The administrator invites the resident to the review. With the resident's consent, the administrator also invites the family, guardian or designated person. The resident may bring any representative. Staff explain the findings in plain language and use an interpreter if needed (RR-07).

The team states whether [AGENCY NAME] can safely meet the resident's needs with services, a revised care plan (ADM-04), added staffing, home health or hospice (HLT-09), or a managed risk agreement. It also states what the added cost would be under the admission agreement.
If the resident can be safely served, the team keeps the resident. The care plan is updated within [NUMBER] days and the added cost, if any, is explained in writing before it begins (RR-03).
If the resident has a single stage 2 pressure sore, the RN writes a plan of care and the resident is retained (HLT-08). The record shows that the sore was not used as a basis for discharge.
If the resident needs specialized long-term care, the administrator documents the basis with the physician and starts a transfer under ADM-06.

If the resident is a danger to self or others and cannot be cared for safely, staff follow the physician-directed placement and mental health screening process in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.13(c) and N.J.A.C. 10:31. The administrator documents each step and notifies the family or guardian with the resident's consent.

If the team recommends moving the resident, the administrator records the specific 5.1(d) characteristic or characteristics relied on, the evidence, the alternatives considered, and the resident's response. The social worker begins relocation planning with the resident and discusses receiving settings.
The administrator may use infirmary transfer only with the resident's consent. Staff record the consent, the start date and the one-week target, and review the stay before the week ends (5.13(e)).

The administrator issues the written notice required by ADM-06. No resident is moved until the notice and the resident's appeal rights have been handled under that policy, except in an emergency as ADM-06 describes.

The administrator reports to the governing body quarterly on retention reviews, transfers and discharges, so that the facility's retention rate for nursing-home-level residents can be checked against its 20% nursing-home-level commitment within 36 months of licensure (GOV-06, ADM-02).
The administrator reviews this policy annually with GOV-05 and revises it when N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1 changes.

responsibilities.duty: Makes the final retention or discharge decision, convenes the review, issues notices, and ensures the criteria are applied consistently and only on documented grounds.
Assesses the resident, documents 5.1(d) characteristics, writes plans of care, and advises on safe retention.
Gives clinical input, decides placement when the resident is a danger to self or others, and certifies need for specialized long-term care.
Supports the resident and family in the review, explains options, and leads relocation planning.
Report changes in condition and give observations to the review.
Reviews retention and discharge data quarterly.

documentation: Reassessment records showing presence or absence of each 5.1(d) characteristic
Interdisciplinary retention review record (date, participants, findings, resident's response, decision)
Updated care plan, plan of care for a stage 2 sore, and any managed risk agreement
Physician orders or placement decision and mental health screening referral where applicable
Infirmary transfer consent and dates
Written discharge notice and proof of delivery (see ADM-06)
Quarterly retention and discharge report to the governing body

policies.title: Involuntary Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
policies.applies_to: All residents of [AGENCY NAME] (ALR, CPCH and ALP); administrator, social work, nursing and business office staff
policies.purpose: To make sure any discharge or transfer requested by [AGENCY NAME] is based on grounds the resident was told about in advance, is made with proper written notice, and protects the resident's right to appeal and to Ombudsman help.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-4.1(a)37, the resident's right to written notice at least 30 days in advance when the facility requests the resident's transfer or discharge, except in an emergency. That notice includes the name, address and telephone number of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman and is also provided to the resident's legally appointed guardian, or, with the resident's consent, to the resident's family, 30 days in advance.

1. Grounds. [AGENCY NAME] discharges a resident involuntarily only on grounds stated in its policies, which are given to the resident, guardian or designee before or at admission (see ADM-01 and RR-03). Those grounds are: needs the facility cannot safely meet or that require specialized long-term care (ADM-05); nonpayment after notice and opportunity to resolve (RR-03); danger to self or others; and closure or loss of license (see item 8). No other reason is used.

2. Written notice. The administrator gives written notice to the resident and to the family, guardian or designee. The notice is given at least 30 days before the discharge date. It states the reason and the right to appeal. A copy is kept in the resident's record (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.14).

3. Ombudsman and guardian. The notice includes the name, address and telephone of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (1-877-582-6995). It is also given to the guardian, if one has been appointed, or to the family if the resident consents.

4. Exceptions. The 30-day notice requirement does not apply to a discharge for a reason in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) (see ADM-05). An emergency transfer to protect life safety may be made without 30 days' notice, and the Department of Health is notified. [AGENCY NAME]'s practice is to give the full 30 days whenever it is safe to do so. When it gives less, the administrator records why and gives as much notice as the circumstances allow.

5. Surrender, revocation or non-renewal of license. If [AGENCY NAME] voluntarily surrenders its license, or is ordered to close through revocation, non-renewal or suspension, the administrator notifies each resident, the resident's physician and guarantors of payment at least 30 days before the surrender, or as the order directs. The license is returned to the CN&L Program within 7 working days (N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.6; see GOV-03).

6. Safe relocation. No resident is discharged to an unsafe or unknown setting. Staff help the resident find a suitable placement and prepare the resident for the move.

definitions.definition: A discharge or transfer requested by the facility rather than by the resident or guardian.
A transfer needed right away to protect the life safety of the resident or others, for which 30 days' notice is not required.
A person the resident has named to receive notices on the resident's behalf.
The State Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, 1-877-582-6995, which advocates for residents and receives notices of discharge.

procedures: When a staff member believes a resident may need to be discharged, he or she tells the administrator the same day. The administrator opens a discharge review file.

The administrator confirms that the reason matches a ground listed in the admission agreement and in this policy, and that the resident was given the ground in advance. If it does not, the discharge does not go forward.

For care-need discharges, the administrator holds the interdisciplinary retention review required by ADM-05, with the resident taking part. For nonpayment, the business office first sends the written reminders and offers a payment plan or benefits referral under RR-03 and ADM-07.

The administrator personally prepares the written notice. It includes the resident's name, the date of notice, the planned discharge date (at least 30 days later), the specific reason, a statement of the resident's right to appeal, and how to ask for an appeal in writing to [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] at [ADDRESS] or [PHONE].
The notice gives the name, address and telephone of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and also the DOH complaint hotline (1-800-792-9770) and [AGENCY NAME]'s grievance policy (RR-02).

The administrator delivers the notice to the resident in person, reads or explains it, and uses an interpreter or accommodation if needed (RR-07). The resident signs to acknowledge receipt, or staff record that the resident declined to sign.

The same day, the administrator sends the notice to the guardian, if any, and, with the resident's consent, to the family or designee. The consent or refusal is documented. A copy is mailed or delivered with proof of delivery.
The administrator sends a copy to the Ombudsman and to the MLTSS care manager or managed care plan if the resident is a NJ FamilyCare member (see ADM-07).
A copy of the notice, proof of delivery and the resident's acknowledgment are placed in the resident record the same day.

If the resident appeals, the administrator meets with the resident (and the representative of choice) within [NUMBER] business days, reviews the evidence, and gives a written decision within [NUMBER] business days. The resident is not discharged on the notice date while the appeal is under review unless an emergency exists.

The social worker or designee starts relocation planning within 3 business days of the notice. This includes identifying suitable settings, helping with applications and referrals, arranging transportation, and giving the receiving provider the transfer summary.

Before the move, the RN prepares a transfer summary with current medications, diagnoses, treatments, care plan, and contact information. The facility returns the resident's funds and property under RR-04 and sends medications as ordered.

For an emergency transfer for life safety, staff call 911 or arrange immediate transport, notify the physician and the family, guardian or designee with the resident's consent, and the administrator notifies the Department of Health as required (see SAF-02 and REC-02). The administrator documents why 30 days' notice was not possible.

If the facility is closing or surrendering its license, the administrator sends written 30-day notices to each resident, each resident's physician and each guarantor of payment, and returns the license to the CN&L Program within 7 working days (see GOV-03).
After the discharge, the administrator completes the discharge note, closes the file, and reports the event in the quarterly report to the governing body (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Confirms grounds, issues and delivers the written notice, hears appeals, notifies the Ombudsman, DOH when required, and oversees safe relocation.
Supports the resident, plans the relocation and coordinates with the receiving provider and care manager.
Prepares the transfer summary and ensures medications and treatment information go with the resident.
Handles billing steps for nonpayment discharges and returns funds and deposits.

documentation: Written 30-day discharge notice, with proof of delivery to resident, guardian or family, and Ombudsman
Resident's signed acknowledgment or note of refusal
Resident's consent or refusal to notify family
Retention review record (ADM-05) or payment notices (RR-03)
Appeal request, meeting notes and written decision
Emergency transfer record and DOH notification
Relocation plan, transfer summary and discharge note
Notices sent to residents, physicians and guarantors for license surrender, plus date the license was returned

policies.title: NJ FamilyCare MLTSS Participation, Per Diem and Room-and-Board Billing
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME] business office, administrator, admissions and social work staff; residents who are, or may become, NJ FamilyCare MLTSS members
policies.purpose: To describe how [AGENCY NAME] takes part in NJ FamilyCare Managed Long-Term Services and Supports (MLTSS), how Medicaid per diem payments and tier add-ons are tracked, and how room and board and personal needs funds are kept separate from Medicaid-paid services.
policies.policy:
1. Participation. [AGENCY NAME] participates in NJ FamilyCare MLTSS and contracts with the managed care plans that pay for assisted living services. It maintains the Medicaid-eligible occupancy required of a newly licensed ALR or CPCH: at least 10% Medicaid-eligible occupancy within three years of licensure, kept thereafter, with added beds also 10% Medicaid-occupied and at least one bed reserved when the facility has fewer than 10 beds (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(h)-(l); see ADM-02). The Commissioner may waive or reduce the requirement. No waiver is assumed.

2. Equal treatment. Residents who are Medicaid-eligible or become so are not treated differently in services, rooms, or staff attention (see RR-07).

3. Per diem. Medicaid pays a per diem for covered assisted living services. The SFY2026 base rates are $91.10 for an ALR, $81.10 for a CPCH and $79.10 for an ALP, per NJ FamilyCare beneficiary per day (DHS notice of 7/16/2025). SFY2027 rates and CMS approval were not checked when this manual was written. The business office confirms the rate in effect for each plan before billing and updates this policy when rates change.

4. Medicaid-volume tier add-ons (ALR and CPCH). Under P.L. 2023, c.80, the per diem rises above the minimum based on the yearly average Medicaid census, measured from paid claims against total licensed beds: $10 at 15% to under 30%; $15 at 30% to under 50%; $30 at 50% to under 70%; $35 at 70% or more; none below 15%. [AGENCY NAME] does not budget for add-ons until they are paid.

5. Room and board. Medicaid does not pay room and board. The resident (or family, guardian or representative payee) is responsible for it, as stated in the admission agreement (RR-03). The facility will verify and use the DMAHS standards in effect: $996.40 per month for room and $147.65 per month for maintenance (personal needs), effective 1/1/2026. The resident keeps the personal needs amount for personal use (see RR-04). The facility never takes it for room and board or services.

6. No extra charges for covered services. [AGENCY NAME] does not bill a Medicaid resident for services covered by the per diem.

7. Eligibility. MLTSS eligibility requires a nursing-home level of care and meeting income and resource limits. [AGENCY NAME] staff do not determine eligibility. They refer families to the county agency or a benefits specialist.

8. Federal home and community-based requirements. Services are delivered consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c) (HCBS settings and person-centered planning). The resident's choices, privacy, and rights are respected, and care plans follow ADM-04.

9. Electronic visit verification (EVV). 42 USC 1396b(l) requires EVV for certain Medicaid personal care services. [AGENCY NAME] will confirm in writing with DMAHS and each managed care plan whether EVV applies to assisted living services at its ALR/CPCH/ALP, and will follow the written answer.

10. Billing integrity. All claims are accurate, supported by the record, and submitted under GOV-07.

definitions.definition: Managed Long-Term Services and Supports, the NJ FamilyCare program that pays for long-term care services for eligible members through managed care plans.
The daily Medicaid payment per beneficiary for covered assisted living services.
An amount added to the minimum per diem by yearly average Medicaid census under P.L. 2023, c.80.
The resident's housing and meals charge, which Medicaid does not pay.
The monthly maintenance amount a Medicaid resident keeps for personal use.
Electronic visit verification of the time and place of certain Medicaid personal care visits.

procedures: The administrator signs and keeps contracts with each NJ FamilyCare managed care plan the facility accepts, and records each plan's contact, authorization and claim procedures in a billing file kept by the business office.

At pre-admission screening (ADM-01), staff ask about payer source and tell applicants whether the facility has a Medicaid bed available. A person is not denied admission solely because the person is on Medicaid, within the facility's Medicaid-eligible occupancy commitments (ADM-02).

If an applicant or resident may qualify for MLTSS, the social worker or admissions coordinator gives the county agency and benefits specialist contacts and offers help gathering documents. Staff do not make eligibility decisions.

The business office records the date a resident applies for Medicaid and the date of eligibility. Staff tell the resident and family in writing what charges apply before and after eligibility, using the admission agreement (RR-03).
For each Medicaid resident, the business office confirms from the plan the authorization, effective dates, and care manager contact. The care manager is invited to care plan meetings (ADM-04).

The business office sets up the resident ledger. Room and board is charged at the amount in the agreement, not more than the resident's allowed contribution under DMAHS rules. Staff verify the current DMAHS room amount and personal needs amount each January and when DMAHS publishes a change.
The resident's personal needs amount is held or paid under RR-04 and never used for room, board or covered services.

The business office submits Medicaid claims for covered services by the plan's deadline, from daily census and attendance records. Another staff member checks each claim against the record before submission.

Each month the business office reports to the administrator: Medicaid residents, paid claims, per diem received, and the Medicaid share of licensed beds. Each quarter this goes to the governing body (GOV-06).

Each year the administrator computes the yearly average Medicaid census using paid claims against total licensed beds, determines the applicable tier, and compares payments received with the tier due. Any discrepancy is raised with the plan or DMAHS in writing.
Each July the administrator checks the DHS rate notice and updates the per diem schedule in this policy. The date and the source reviewed are recorded.

The administrator tracks Medicaid-eligible occupancy against the 10% requirement monthly, starting at licensure, and takes admissions and outreach steps if the facility is behind schedule. Any waiver request to the Commissioner is made in writing and the response is kept.
The administrator confirms in writing with DMAHS and each plan whether EVV applies. The written answer is filed and training is given to staff if EVV applies.

If a Medicaid resident's coverage is denied or ends, the business office tells the administrator within 1 business day. The administrator and social worker meet with the resident and help the resident appeal or reapply. Any discharge follows ADM-06.
The business office reports suspected billing errors, overpayments or improper charges to the compliance officer within 5 business days for review and refund where needed (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Signs plan contracts, monitors Medicaid occupancy and tier status, and approves rate updates.
Bills claims accurately and on time, maintains resident ledgers, reconciles payments, and applies DMAHS room and personal needs amounts.
Refers families to eligibility help and coordinates with care managers.
Reviews billing issues and refunds under GOV-07.
Reviews Medicaid occupancy and revenue reports quarterly.

documentation: Managed care plan contracts and authorizations
Per diem schedule with source and review dates
Resident ledgers showing room and board, personal needs amounts, and Medicaid payments
Claims and remittance records
Monthly Medicaid occupancy report and yearly average census calculation with tier determination
Written EVV confirmation from DMAHS and plans
Waiver request and response, if any

policies.category: Assisted Living Program (ALP) (only if licensed as an ALP)
policies.title: Assisted Living Program Contracts, Manual, Notices and Reporting
policies.applies_to: [AGENCY NAME]'s Assisted Living Program (ALP) provider office and each ALP site, residents served by the ALP, ALP administrator and staff. Applies only if [AGENCY NAME] is licensed as an ALP.
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] operates its Assisted Living Program: where services are delivered, what written contracts are kept, where the policy manual is kept, what notices are posted, and how families and the State are notified of serious events.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.4 (policy and procedure manual for the ALP, developed, implemented and reviewed under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7, available at all ALP sites, the main office and to Department representatives), N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.2 (written contracts detailing all policies, procedures and services of the licensed facility and the licensed program), and N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.2(l)1-2 (the application includes the written contract between the program provider and the publicly subsidized housing unit, and the provider-resident agreement used at each program site, clearly addressing N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.3(d)).

1. Where services are delivered. ALP services are delivered only inside a licensed ALR, a licensed CPCH or publicly subsidized housing (N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.2). ALP services are not delivered anywhere else.

2. Written contracts (23.2). The licensed ALR or CPCH and the licensed program keep written contracts that detail all policies, procedures and services each will provide. Where the site is publicly subsidized housing, [AGENCY NAME] keeps a written contract with the housing unit, and a copy is included with the license application (2.2(l)1).

3. Provider-resident agreement (2.2(l)2). A written agreement between [AGENCY NAME] and each resident is used at each ALP site. The form for each site is submitted with the license application, and it addresses N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.3(d). The agreement is also sent to the CN&L Program for review before use, to confirm that it does not violate the chapter, Certificate of Need conditions, or State or Federal law.

4. Policy and procedure manual (23.4). The ALP manual is developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7, with each review documented (see GOV-05). It includes the organizational chart, the description of services, security policies, abuse and exploitation reporting (DOH Complaints Program 1-800-792-9770, and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman 1-877-582-6995 for residents 60 or older), confidentiality and release of records, personnel records, employee physicals, immunizations and TB testing, and prompt notification of a resident's death. A current copy is kept at every ALP site, at the main office, and is available at all times to representatives of the Department. The manual is made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, applicants and referring agencies as provided in GOV-05.

5. Notices (23.6). The ALP provider and each ALP site post a notice that specified information is available at the site and at the provider's main office. The notice includes the DOH hotline, the telephone numbers of the county senior-services agency, and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman number.

6. Notification of family or guardian (23.8). With the resident's consent, [AGENCY NAME] promptly notifies the family, guardian or designated person of: any serious accident; any criminal act or incident causing serious harm or injury; and the resident's arrest or detention. For an arrest or detention, the CN&L Program is also notified in writing.

7. Reportable events (23.17(b)). The ALP notifies DOH immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034, or (609) 392-2020 after hours, with written confirmation within 72 hours. Reportable events include reportable infections and diseases under N.J.A.C. 8:57 among residents, and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman. The facility also reports abuse and exploitation to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770 (see SAF-01).

definitions.definition: A licensed program that provides assisted living services to residents of publicly subsidized housing, or inside a licensed ALR or CPCH.
Each location where the ALP delivers services.
Housing financed or subsidized with public funds in which the ALP may deliver services under a written contract.
The Department of Health Certificate of Need and Licensing Program.

procedures: Before the application is filed, the ALP administrator lists each planned program site and confirms that each is a licensed ALR, a licensed CPCH or publicly subsidized housing. Documentation of license or subsidy status is kept in the ALP site file.

The ALP administrator and the host ALR/CPCH administrator, or the subsidized housing owner, sign a written contract that details the policies, procedures and services of each party. The contract is reviewed by [AGENCY NAME]'s counsel and attached to the application.

The ALP administrator drafts one provider-resident agreement for each program site, checks it against N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.3(d), and submits it with the application. The administrator sends it to the CN&L Program for review before use and keeps the response.

At admission to the ALP, the administrator or designee reviews the agreement with the resident (and family or guardian if the resident agrees), gives a signed copy to the resident, and files a copy in the record (see ADM-01 and RR-03).

The ALP administrator keeps the policy manual in a labeled binder or secure electronic file at each site and at the main office. A designated staff member at each site confirms weekly that the current copy is present and complete, and records this on the manual check log.
The administrator reviews the manual at least annually, documents the review (date, reviewer, changes), and issues revised pages to all sites within 10 business days (GOV-05).

The manual is made available to residents, guardians, designated individuals, applicants and referring agencies on request, in the ways stated in GOV-05, and DOH representatives may see it at any site and the main office at any time.

The ALP administrator posts the 23.6 notice in a conspicuous location at each site and the main office. It lists the DOH hotline, the county senior-services agency telephone numbers ([PHONE]) and the Ombudsman number 1-877-582-6995. A staff member checks the postings monthly and replaces missing or outdated notices.

When a serious accident, criminal act or incident causing serious harm or injury occurs, the staff member on duty makes sure the resident is safe, calls 911 if needed, and tells the ALP administrator immediately.

The ALP administrator asks the resident for consent to notify the family, guardian or designated person, and if consent is given or a guardian exists, makes the notification promptly and records the time, person and content.
If a resident is arrested or detained, the administrator notifies the family, guardian or designated person with consent, and notifies the CN&L Program in writing, keeping a copy.

The administrator calls DOH immediately at (609) 633-9034 (or (609) 392-2020 after hours) for any reportable event, including reportable infections and diseases under N.J.A.C. 8:57 among residents and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation reported to the Ombudsman. The administrator records the time, the person spoken to, and the details.
Within 72 hours the administrator sends written confirmation to DOH and keeps the copy and proof of sending in the incident file (SAF-02, REC-02).

For suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff also follow SAF-01, including reporting to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770 and to the Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995 for residents 60 or older.
The administrator reviews all ALP incidents and notifications each quarter with the governing body (GOV-06) to check that every required notice and report was made on time.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps contracts and agreements current, maintains the manual at every site and the main office, posts notices, makes DOH and family notifications, and files written confirmations.

responsibilities.role: Host ALR/CPCH administrator or subsidized housing owner
responsibilities.duty: Honors the written contract and cooperates in delivering ALP services and reporting events.
Checks weekly that the manual is present and monthly that the notice is posted, and reports serious events at once.
Reviews contracts, manual review documentation and reportable events.

documentation: Written contracts under N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.2 (ALR/CPCH-program contract and housing contract)
Provider-resident agreement for each site and CN&L review response
Manual with annual review log and manual check log for each site
Copy of the posted 23.6 notice and posting check log
Family, guardian or designee notification records, with the resident's consent
Written notice to CN&L for a resident's arrest or detention
DOH phone report log and 72-hour written confirmations
Quarterly incident and notification review

policies.title: Resident Care Policies and Procedures Index and Review
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] staff who deliver or supervise resident care; administrator, RN and governing body
policies.purpose: To keep written resident care policies established, put into practice, reviewed on a set schedule, and mapped to the State's required list so that nothing required is missing.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a): written resident care policies and procedures are established, implemented, and reviewed at the intervals set in this policy, and each review is documented. The policies include, but are not limited to, the items numbered 1 through 11 in 6.1(a).

1. Review interval. All resident care policies are reviewed at least once a year together with the manual review under GOV-05. They are also reviewed when a regulation changes, after a serious incident or survey finding, or when a change in services requires it. Each review is documented with the date, reviewer, findings, and changes.

2. Smoking control (6.1(a)8). Resident care policies include control of smoking under N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6. This item is met by SAF-08.

3. Other required items. The text of 6.1(a) items 1 through 7 and 9 through 11 was not available when this manual was drafted. Before the manual is adopted, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] will obtain the current official text of N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a) from the NJ Department of Health or the New Jersey Administrative Code, list each item in the Resident Care Policy Index, and map each to the policy that covers it. Any item not covered will be written into a new policy or added to an existing one before the license application or survey. The cross-reference is not complete until this is done.

4. Provisional topical map. Until the verification in item 3 is finished, the index maps resident care subjects as follows: medication management and administration (HLT-02, HLT-03); nursing services and delegation (HLT-04); change of condition and hospital transfer (HLT-05); dementia care (HLT-06); falls (HLT-07); skin integrity (HLT-08); hospice and home health (HLT-09); death of a resident (HLT-10); social work and respite (HLT-11); infection control (SAF-07); smoking (SAF-08); restraints (SAF-04); food and diets (DL-01); activities (DL-02); and assessments and care plans (ADM-03, ADM-04). This map is not a substitute for the official item-by-item mapping.

5. Staff acknowledgment. Staff sign an acknowledgment that they have read the resident care policies that apply to their job at orientation and after each revision.

definitions.definition: The written policies and procedures in the manual that govern direct care, health services, and safety of residents.
The list that shows each item required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a) and the policy that covers it.
A documented check that a policy is current, accurate, and followed in practice.

procedures: The administrator keeps a Resident Care Policy Index in the front of the policy manual (GOV-05). It lists each policy ID, title, owner, effective date, last review date, and next review date.
Before adoption, the administrator obtains the official text of N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a) items 1 through 11 and enters each item verbatim in the index.
For each item, the administrator names the policy ID and section that covers it, and marks any gap. The completed map is dated and signed.
For any gap, the administrator assigns an owner and a due date within 30 days to write or revise the policy. The governing body approves the new policy.
The administrator confirms that smoking control, item 8, is covered by SAF-08 and that SAF-08 cites N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6.
The RN reviews every clinical policy at least once a year, compares it with actual practice using chart audits and staff interviews, and writes a short review summary.
The administrator reviews non-clinical resident care policies, such as dining, activities and housekeeping, at least once a year using resident feedback, incident reports and observation.
Each review is recorded on the Policy Review Log: policy ID, date, reviewer, changes, and approval signature.
The administrator calls an off-cycle review within 30 days of a regulatory change, a survey deficiency, a sentinel event or an incident trend identified under GOV-06.

After any revision, the administrator updates the index and the effective date, removes superseded copies from circulation, and keeps the old version marked 'superseded' in the document control file (GOV-05).
New or revised policies are explained to staff within 14 days. Staff sign the policy acknowledgment form, and the administrator files it in the personnel record (STF-05).
New employees receive and sign the resident care policy acknowledgment at orientation (STF-03).
The administrator reports completed reviews and open gaps to the governing body at least annually and at each quarterly meeting until gaps are closed.
The index and review log are kept in the facility and shown to DOH representatives on request.

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the index, completes the official 6.1(a) mapping, assigns gap closure, and ensures reviews are documented.
Reviews clinical policies against practice and recommends revisions.
Approves policies and receives review and gap reports.
Read and follow the policies relevant to their jobs and sign the acknowledgment.

documentation: Resident Care Policy Index with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1(a) items 1-11 and mapping
Policy Review Log
Review summaries and gap closure records
Staff policy acknowledgment forms
Governing body minutes approving revisions
Document control file with superseded versions

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage, Disposal and Theft Reporting
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN, medication-authorized staff, pharmacy provider and any staff with access to medications or sharps at [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep resident medications, controlled substances, needles and syringes safely stored, counted, and disposed of, and to make sure any theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances is reported to the proper authorities.
policies.policy:
This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-11.7(l): any theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances is reported to the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742, and/or to any other municipal, county, State, or Federal authority having jurisdiction over theft of such substances.

1. Safe storage. The administrator provides a safe storage area for medications that are not self-administered. A locked medication cart is acceptable. The area or cart is kept locked whenever staff are not in attendance. Only staff authorized under HLT-03 hold keys or codes.

2. Storage conditions and containers. Medications are stored according to the manufacturer's or pharmacy's directions (for example, temperature and refrigeration) and are kept in their original, labeled containers. Staff do not transfer, combine, or relabel medications. Generic substitutes are labeled in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:71.

3. Controlled dangerous substances (CDS). CDS are handled in accordance with N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq. and are kept under double lock or in a separately locked compartment, with a count record kept by shift.

4. Needles and syringes. Needles and syringes are stored, used and disposed of in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5.10 et seq., N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, N.J.A.C. 7:26-3A and 29 CFR 1910.1030. The facility keeps a record of purchase, storage and disposal. Used sharps go immediately into approved puncture-resistant containers (see SAF-07).

5. Theft. Any theft or suspected theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances is reported to the Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742 and/or to local police or any other authority with jurisdiction. Retaliation against a staff member who reports is prohibited.

definitions.definition: A drug listed in a schedule under N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq. or federal controlled substance law.
The pharmacy or manufacturer container that carries the resident's name, drug, dose, directions and prescriber or expiration information.
Needles, syringes, lancets and other items that can puncture the skin.
The taking, diversion, or unaccounted loss of a medication, including a loss that cannot be explained by count reconciliation.

procedures: The administrator designates the locked medication storage area(s) and assigns keys or codes only to staff authorized under HLT-03. A key and code log shows who holds each. The administrator changes keys or codes within 24 hours of any staff separation or loss.

On receipt of a medication from the pharmacy or family, a medication-authorized staff member checks the label against the physician order, confirms it is in the original labeled container, and logs it in on the resident's medication record. The RN resolves any discrepancy before the medication is used.

Staff keep medications at the temperature in the label directions. Refrigerated medications are stored in a locked refrigerator or locked box. Staff record refrigerator temperatures daily and report out-of-range readings to the RN the same shift.
When a generic substitute is dispensed, the RN confirms the label follows N.J.A.C. 8:71 and that the resident's record and order match.

Controlled substances are counted by two authorized staff members at each shift change and any time the cart is passed from one person to another. Both sign the count record. A discrepancy is not left unresolved: staff search and recount, then tell the RN and administrator immediately.
The administrator reviews the CDS count record weekly. The RN or consultant pharmacist reconciles CDS stock against orders and administration records monthly and signs the reconciliation.

The administrator reviews and documents on the Sharps Record the purchase, storage location, use and disposal of all needles and syringes. Sharps containers are not filled beyond the fill line and are sealed and removed by a licensed medical waste vendor (SAF-07).

Discontinued, expired, or deceased-resident medications are removed from active stock the same day, locked in a separate area, and disposed of with a witness according to law and pharmacist direction. The record shows drug, strength, quantity, date, method, and both signatures. CDS are disposed of only in a way allowed under N.J.S.A. 24:21-1 et seq. and federal law.
A resident's own medications are released to the resident, family or guardian on discharge only by order and with a signed receipt (RR-06, REC-01).

If any theft or suspected theft of a Scheduled or Controlled Substance is found, the discovering staff member secures the area, does not touch evidence, and tells the administrator or administrator on call immediately.
The administrator interviews staff on duty, checks logs, counts and camera footage if available, and decides within 24 hours whether theft is suspected.

When theft is suspected or confirmed, the administrator reports it by phone to the Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742 and/or to local police or any other municipal, county, State or Federal authority having jurisdiction. The administrator records the date, time, person contacted, report number and information given.

The administrator completes an incident report the same day (SAF-02), notifies the resident's physician and, with consent, the family or guardian if the resident was affected, and submits any DOH report required under REC-02.
The RN checks all residents affected for harm or missed doses and gets physician orders for replacement medication.

After a theft report, the administrator reviews controls (keys, counts, access) and records corrective action. Results go to the governing body (GOV-06). Staff found responsible are disciplined under STF-06, and the administrator reports to licensing boards as the law requires.
The administrator reviews this policy annually with the consultant pharmacist and the RN (HLT-01).

responsibilities.duty: Provides safe storage, controls keys, ensures records of CDS and sharps, and reports theft to the Enforcement Bureau and other authorities.
Oversees medication storage and labeling, reconciles counts, and responds to missing medications and resident safety.
Keep medications locked, count CDS, document, and report discrepancies at once.
Reviews storage, labeling, disposal and CDS reconciliation at least monthly and advises on compliance.

documentation: Key and code access log
Medication receiving and storage records, refrigerator temperature log
CDS count and reconciliation records
Needle and syringe purchase, storage and disposal record
Medication disposal record with witness signatures
Theft report log (date, authority contacted, report number) and incident report
Corrective action record and governing body review

policies.title: Medication Administration, Self-Administration and Staff Authorization
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); all nursing, certified medication aide and direct-care staff
policies.purpose: To ensure that residents who can manage their own medications are supervised in doing so, and that residents who cannot are given medications only by trained, supervised and properly authorized staff, as required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(c).
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] supervises resident self-administration of medications and uses only trained, supervised staff to administer medications to residents who cannot self-administer (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(c)). Only two groups of staff may administer medications: (1) licensed nurses, meaning RNs or PNs licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37, within their scope of practice; and (2) certified medication aides (CMAs) who hold a current certificate and work under supervision. A CMA must have completed a DOH-approved medication administration course and passed a DOH-approved exam, and must renew every 2 years with at least 10 hours of continuing education per period, of which 5 hours cover the fundamentals of medication administration and 5 hours cover drug use relevant to the elderly (N.J.A.C. 8:36-9.2). Personal care assistants and other staff without one of these authorizations do not administer medications. They may only remind or cue a resident as the health service plan allows, and report concerns to the RN. Storage, disposal and theft reporting are covered in HLT-02.

definitions.definition: A resident takes their own medications, with the facility's supervision as set out in the health service plan, after the RN has determined the resident can do so safely.
Staff prepare and give a medication to a resident, and record that they did so.
An unlicensed staff member who has completed a DOH-approved medication administration course, passed a DOH-approved exam, and holds a current certificate.
An RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3).
The DOH registry on which a CMA may be listed after a finding of abuse, neglect, misappropriation, negligence or incompetence.

procedures: Before admission, the RN reviews the resident's medication list and prescriber orders. Within 14 days of admission, the RN's health care assessment (ADM-03) determines whether the resident can self-administer, needs supervision, or needs staff administration.
The RN records the decision in the health service plan (ADM-04), stating which medications the resident self-administers, the supervision required, and which medications staff administer.

For self-administering residents, staff supervise as the plan directs. This may include checking storage, observing or confirming doses, and reporting missed doses or confusion to the RN the same shift. Medications for self-administration are kept in a lockable space in the resident's unit, or at the central medication area if the resident or RN chooses.

The RN re-evaluates self-administration whenever there is a change of condition, a medication error, a hospital stay, or a staff report of difficulty. At a minimum, the re-evaluation occurs at each scheduled reassessment (ADM-03). If the resident can no longer self-administer safely, the RN updates the plan and notifies the resident and designee.
Staff administer medications only on a current written prescriber order and only from a labeled pharmacy container belonging to that resident.

Before each pass the staff member washes hands and checks the medication administration record (MAR) for the right resident, medication, dose, route and time. The staff member observes the resident taking the dose and signs the MAR immediately after administration, not before.

A refused or missed dose is recorded on the MAR with the reason. The nurse or CMA notifies the RN the same shift. The RN notifies the prescriber when the refusal or omission is clinically significant, or when it repeats.
PRN medications are given only with the specific order, the reason, the dose limit and the time interval on the MAR. Staff record the reason given and the resident's response.
A CMA who is unsure about an order, a dose, an unusual resident reaction or a labeling discrepancy stops and contacts the supervising RN before giving the medication.

A medication error or adverse reaction is reported to the RN immediately. The RN assesses the resident, notifies the prescriber and the resident's designee, and the staff member completes an incident report under SAF-02 before the end of the shift. Errors are reviewed in the quality improvement program (GOV-06).

Before a CMA is allowed to administer medications, the Administrator or designee verifies and copies the CMA certificate and records the issue and expiration dates. The Administrator or designee also confirms the CMA's status on the registry (STF-02). Hiring and orientation follow STF-03.

The RN observes each new CMA administering medications and records a competency check before the CMA works unsupervised on a medication pass. The RN repeats the check at least annually and after any error.

The Administrator tracks each CMA's 2-year renewal date and the 10 required CE hours per period (5 on fundamentals of medication administration and 5 on drug use relevant to the elderly). A tracking report is reviewed monthly. A CMA whose certificate has lapsed is removed from medication duty on the expiration date until renewal is verified.
CMA certificates, course and exam proof, and CE records are kept in the personnel file (STF-05).

If DOH issues a notice proposing a registry finding of abuse, neglect, misappropriation, negligence or incompetence against a CMA, the Administrator removes the CMA from medication duty pending the outcome, informs the CMA in writing of the right to request a hearing (DOH gives at least 30 days to request one), and keeps the notice in the personnel file. The facility cooperates with DOH. Any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is also reported under SAF-01.
The RN audits MARs and medication storage at least monthly, and reports findings to the Administrator and the quality improvement committee (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Determines self-administration capability, supervises medication administration, checks CMA competency, responds to errors and audits MARs.
Administers medications only within certification and under RN supervision. Documents each dose, reports refusals, errors and reactions, and keeps certification and CE current.
Verifies CMA certification, tracks renewal and CE, removes unauthorized staff from medication duty and handles DOH registry notices.
Do not administer medications. Cue or remind only as the health service plan allows, and report concerns to the RN.

documentation: Medication administration record (MAR)
Self-administration determination in the health care assessment and health service plan
Medication error and incident reports
CMA certificate, course and exam proof, CE hours and renewal tracking in the personnel file
CMA competency checklists
Monthly MAR and storage audit reports
Any DOH registry or hearing notice

policies.title: Nursing Services, RN Availability and Delegation
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); nursing, direct-care and administrative staff
policies.purpose: To ensure that a registered nurse is available at all times, that every resident receives an RN assessment and care plan, and that nursing tasks are delegated only as permitted by the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37, under RN supervision.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides nursing services under N.J.A.C. 8:36-8.2 and is capable of nursing services, including for residents who have nursing-home-level needs (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d)). At least one registered professional nurse is available at all times, and each resident receives an RN assessment and care plan. Services are consistent with the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(a)). 'Licensed nurse' means an RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3). Because the regulation's meaning of 'available' for coverage and response time must be confirmed with DOH, the Administrator obtains that confirmation in writing (Procedure 2). Until it is confirmed, the facility operates the more protective standard in Procedure 3. Nursing assessment, care planning, evaluation and nursing judgment are never delegated. Only the tasks in Procedure 8 may be delegated, and only to staff who have been trained and found competent and who work under RN supervision.

definitions.definition: A nurse licensed as a registered professional nurse under N.J.A.C. 13:37.
Able to be reached and to respond to the resident's need at all times. The coverage and response-time meaning is to be confirmed with DOH (see Procedure 2).
The RN's transfer of a specific task to a competent staff member, with the RN keeping accountability for assessment, supervision and outcome.
An RN or PN licensed under N.J.A.C. 13:37.

procedures: The Administrator appoints a Director of Nursing or lead RN, [DIRECTOR OF NURSING NAME], who is licensed in New Jersey, and verifies the RN license through the licensing board before hire and at each renewal (STF-02).

Before opening, and again when any regulatory change is announced, the Administrator writes to the DOH Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, PO Box 367, Trenton, NJ 08625-0358 ((800) 792-9770), asking for confirmation of what 'available at all times' requires for RN coverage and response time. The Administrator files the written reply in the policy manual. If no reply is received, the Administrator records the date of each follow-up.

Pending that confirmation, the Director of Nursing publishes a monthly RN schedule that names the RN on duty or on call for every hour of every day. The on-call RN must answer the phone immediately and be able to reach the facility within [RESPONSE TIME STANDARD SET BY THE ADMINISTRATOR AND DIRECTOR OF NURSING]. The on-call roster with phone numbers is posted at the staff station and given to every shift.

If the scheduled RN cannot work, the Director of Nursing or Administrator finds a replacement before the shift starts and records the change. If coverage cannot be arranged, the Administrator is notified immediately, and the gap is recorded as an incident for review under SAF-02 and GOV-06.

The RN performs or supervises the pre-admission nursing review and completes the health care assessment within 14 days of admission when the initial assessment shows health care needs (ADM-03), and develops the written health service plan (ADM-04). Each resident has an RN assessment and care plan on file.
The RN reassesses residents as set out in ADM-03 and whenever there is a change of condition (HLT-05).

The RN is responsible for nursing services including the following: monitoring changes of condition, supervising medication administration (HLT-03), skin and fall interventions (HLT-07, HLT-08), coordination with hospice and home health (HLT-09), and communicating with physicians.

Delegation: the RN may delegate to a trained and competent staff member only routine tasks that the Nurse Practice Act and N.J.A.C. 13:37 permit to be performed by unlicensed persons, for example assistance with bathing, dressing, toileting, grooming, transfers, ambulation, feeding of residents who have no swallowing risk identified by the RN, positioning and turning, and measuring and reporting vital signs. Medication administration is authorized only for licensed nurses and certified medication aides under HLT-03.

The RN does not delegate: assessment, interpretation of findings, development or change of the health service plan, decisions about whether a resident's condition is stable, patient teaching that needs nursing judgment, or any task outside the scope of the staff member's training or certification. When the Administrator or RN is unsure whether a task may be delegated, the RN checks N.J.A.C. 13:37 or the licensing board before delegating.

Before delegating, the RN identifies the task, the resident, the competent person, the instructions to follow, and what must be reported. The RN checks the staff member's training and competency record, and records the delegation in the resident's health service plan or the staff assignment sheet.

The RN observes each delegated task being done, at minimum at first delegation and every [MONTHS SET BY DIRECTOR OF NURSING] months afterward, and records the competency. Delegation is withdrawn immediately if the staff member shows poor performance, and the Director of Nursing documents the reason.

The facility remains capable of providing nursing services to residents with the nursing-home-level characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d). Retention decisions and the admission agreement statement are handled under ADM-02 and ADM-05, and residents who need specialized long-term care are transferred (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(f)).
Direct-care staff must report any change in a resident's condition to the RN immediately, using the on-call roster when the RN is off site.
The Director of Nursing reports monthly to the Administrator on RN coverage, delegation, competency checks and response-time problems, and these reports feed GOV-06.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures RN availability at all times, obtains DOH written confirmation of the meaning of 'available', and approves the RN schedule and on-call roster.
Assesses residents, develops the health service plan, supervises care and delegation, and is reachable for staff and physicians.
Perform only delegated tasks they are trained and competent to perform, and report changes in condition promptly.

documentation: RN licensure verification
Monthly RN schedule and on-call roster
DOH written confirmation (or follow-up record) of 'available' meaning
Health care assessments and health service plans
Delegation records and competency checklists
Coverage-gap incident reports
Monthly Director of Nursing report

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); all nursing and direct-care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure that any change in a resident's condition is recognized, reported to the RN and physician promptly, that emergencies are handled by calling 911 first, and that residents who go to the hospital are accompanied by the information needed for their care.
policies.policy: All staff report any change in a resident's condition to the RN immediately. The physician is notified promptly of an acute change. The resident's family, guardian or designee is notified with the resident's consent, in line with the facility's family notification and incident policies (SAF-02, RR-06). In an emergency, staff call 911 first and then notify the RN, the physician and the designee. An unstable condition is one of the characteristics in N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) that the facility documents when deciding whether a resident should remain in or leave the facility, so every change of condition is reviewed for its effect on retention (ADM-05). At admission the administrator and resident arrange which physician and dentist will be called (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(a)), and that choice is recorded so that staff know whom to call.

definitions.definition: A new or worsening symptom, injury, behavior, function or vital sign that differs from the resident's usual status, including falls, new confusion, refusal of food or fluids, new skin breakdown, chest pain, breathing difficulty and uncontrolled pain.
A sudden or serious change of condition that may need medical evaluation without delay.
A situation in which life or limb may be at risk, such as unresponsiveness, severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, stroke symptoms, heavy bleeding or serious injury.
The family member, guardian, agent or other person the resident has chosen to be notified.

procedures: Any staff member who sees a change of condition stays with the resident, ensures safety, and reports to the RN immediately by phone or in person. In an emergency the staff member calls 911 before calling the RN.

The RN, or the licensed nurse on duty, assesses the resident as soon as possible, checks vital signs and relevant history, and decides whether the situation is an emergency, needs same-day physician contact, or can be monitored with specific instructions.

For an emergency, staff call 911 first, give the facility address [ADDRESS] and the resident's condition, send someone to meet the ambulance, and then continue care within their training until EMS arrives. They do not wait for physician approval to call 911.

For a non-emergency acute change, the RN contacts the resident's physician (or the covering physician) promptly, gives the findings using a standard format (situation, background, assessment, request), and writes down the orders given and who gave them. If the physician is unreachable, the RN follows the on-call arrangement or sends the resident for emergency evaluation if risk is significant.

The RN or Administrator notifies the family, guardian or designee, with the resident's consent, as soon as the resident's immediate needs are being met. If the resident cannot consent, notification follows the advance directive, guardianship or designee information on file (RR-05). Staff record the time, person notified and the response.

Before the resident leaves, staff prepare a transfer packet containing: face sheet with emergency contacts, current medication list and last doses given, allergies, advance directives and code status documents (RR-05), physician name and number, recent vital signs, the reason for transfer, and the resident's insurance and NJ FamilyCare information. Staff ensure the packet leaves with the resident and keep a copy.
Staff send glasses, hearing aids, dentures and a few personal items when possible. They record what leaves the building with the resident (RR-04).

When practical, a staff member who knows the resident goes with the resident or follows to the hospital, or the RN calls the receiving emergency department to give a verbal report. The Administrator or RN keeps in contact with the hospital while the resident is there.
The Administrator keeps current referral and transfer agreements, or documented working arrangements, with at least one local hospital and reviews them at least annually, recording the review date.

The RN completes an incident report under SAF-02 when the change of condition involves an injury, a fall, a medication error, an unexplained injury or another reportable event. The Administrator makes any required report to the State (REC-02). If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, staff follow SAF-01 at once.

On the resident's return, the RN reviews discharge instructions and new orders, reconciles the medication list with the prescriber, and arranges for medications and supplies. The RN reassesses the resident within [HOURS SET BY DIRECTOR OF NURSING] hours of return and updates the health service plan (ADM-03, ADM-04).

The Administrator and RN decide whether the resident's needs after the change are within what the facility can provide. If the change creates a retention question, they review it under ADM-05, and if the facility cannot continue to serve the resident, they follow ADM-06. Residents are not moved without that documented process.
Every change of condition is documented in the resident record with date, time, observation, RN assessment, physician contacted, orders, designee notified and outcome (REC-01).
The Director of Nursing reviews all hospital transfers monthly for patterns, and these are reported to the quality improvement committee (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Recognize and report changes immediately. Call 911 in emergencies. Stay with the resident.
Assess, notify the physician and designee, prepare the transfer packet, document, and reassess on return.
Ensures family notification, keeps referral and transfer arrangements current, makes required reports and decides retention questions with the RN.

documentation: Change-of-condition progress note
Physician notification and orders record
Family or designee notification record
Transfer packet copy and 911 call record
Incident report where applicable
Referral and transfer agreement and annual review record
Post-hospital reassessment and updated health service plan

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); all licensed and unlicensed staff who give direct care to residents with Alzheimer's disease or dementia
policies.purpose: To provide safe, person-centered care for residents with Alzheimer's disease or dementia, and to meet the staff training requirement that applies when a facility advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's or dementia program.
policies.policy: This policy meets N.J.A.C. 8:36-19.3(a): a facility that advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program shall provide training in specialized care of residents who are diagnosed by a physician as having Alzheimer's disease or dementia to all licensed and unlicensed staff who provide direct care to residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. This requirement applies only to a facility that advertises or holds itself out as having such a program. [AGENCY NAME] will not advertise or describe itself as having an Alzheimer's or dementia program (including in brochures, website, signs, admission materials or oral statements) until the training in this policy is in place. If it does so, every direct-care staff member who cares for residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, licensed or unlicensed, is trained before working with those residents unassisted. Whether or not the facility advertises such a program, it cares for residents with cognitive impairment according to the assessment and health service plan. Severe cognitive decline is a characteristic under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) that the facility considers, with documentation, when deciding whether it can keep a resident. A resident who becomes a danger to self or others is handled through the facility's documented retention and discharge process (ADM-05, ADM-06), not by staff decision alone.

definitions.definition: Any marketing, website, brochure, sign, admission material, referral statement or oral claim that the facility has an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program, unit or specialized care.
Licensed and unlicensed staff who provide hands-on care or supervision to residents, including nurses, certified medication aides and personal care assistants.
The mandatory dementia training program required by N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2, a copy of which is available in writing from the DOH Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations.

procedures: At licensure and at every annual review of marketing materials (GOV-03), the Administrator decides in writing whether the facility advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's or dementia program, and records the decision. The review covers the website, brochures, signs, social media, listings and staff scripts.

If the facility will not advertise such a program, the Administrator ensures that no material or staff statement uses language that suggests one, and the facility still provides the person-centered dementia care described in Procedures 8 through 13.

If the facility does advertise or hold itself out as having such a program, the Administrator sends a written request to the DOH Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, PO Box 367, Trenton, NJ 08625-0358, asking for a copy of the mandatory training program under N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. The Administrator keeps the request and the response in the policy file.
The Administrator and Director of Nursing build the facility's training from the DOH program and any state-approved material they receive, and name a trainer qualified in dementia care.

All licensed and unlicensed direct-care staff who care for residents with Alzheimer's or dementia complete the training before working with those residents unassisted. Staff hired later complete it during orientation (STF-03). The facility also schedules refreshers at least [FREQUENCY SET BY THE ADMINISTRATOR].

The trainer records the curriculum, the date, hours, the trainer, and a signed attendance sheet. A staff member who misses a session completes a make-up session before being assigned to dementia residents unassisted.

The Administrator keeps the curriculum, the dates and the attendance in each staff member's personnel file (STF-05) and in a training roster that is reviewed quarterly to find staff who have not yet been trained.

Cognition is assessed at admission and in the RN health care assessment (ADM-03), which covers cognition, communication, mood and behavior. A physician's diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease or dementia is recorded in the resident record.

The health service plan (ADM-04) states for each resident with dementia: communication approaches, routines, triggers and calming measures, wandering or exit-seeking risk, nutrition and hydration needs, toileting plan, and meaningful activities (DL-02).

Staff use non-drug approaches first for distress or behavior. Restraints, locked-in practices and chemical restraint are not used except as SAF-04 allows. Any behavioral medication is ordered by a prescriber and reviewed by the RN on a regular schedule.

Residents at risk of leaving the building are identified in the plan, and staff follow SAF-03 (elopement and missing resident) and SAF-09 (security). Residents' rights, including the right to the least restrictive setting, are respected (RR-01).

The RN reassesses cognition at each reassessment and whenever there is a change in condition. If the resident's cognitive decline is severe, or the resident becomes a danger to self or others, the Administrator and RN document the facts. They review the resident's needs under ADM-05, and if the facility cannot continue to serve the resident, they follow ADM-06. The admission agreement states whether the facility will retain such residents and at what added cost (RR-03).
The Administrator informs families, guardians and designees of the facility's approach to dementia care at admission and involves them in the health service plan.
The quality improvement committee reviews dementia-related incidents, falls, elopement attempts and staff training completion at least quarterly (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Decides and records whether the facility advertises a dementia program, requests the DOH training program, ensures training is complete and keeps records.
Assesses cognition, writes dementia-related care plans, supervises staff practice and reviews retention concerns.
Complete training, follow each resident's plan, use person-centered approaches, and report behavior changes, wandering and safety concerns.

documentation: Written decision on advertising or holding out a dementia program
Written request to and response from the DOH Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations
Training curriculum, dates, hours and signed attendance sheets
Personnel file training entries and quarterly training roster
Cognition findings in the RN assessment and dementia-related items in the health service plan
Retention review documentation where applicable

policies.title: Falls Prevention and Post-Fall Response
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); nursing and direct-care staff, maintenance staff
policies.purpose: To identify residents at risk of falling, reduce that risk through the health service plan, and ensure a consistent, documented response when a fall happens.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assesses each resident's fall risk using the physical functioning and cognition domains of the RN health care assessment (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(d)). The RN places fall-prevention interventions in the written health service plan (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(e)). After every fall, staff assess the resident, notify the physician and family or designee as needed, and document the event. A fall with serious injury triggers incident reporting and family notification under SAF-02 and RR-06. Frequent falls are reviewed as a possible change of condition and a factor in whether the facility can meet the resident's needs (HLT-05, ADM-05). Falls prevention respects the resident's rights; the facility does not use restraints to prevent falls (SAF-04).

definitions.definition: An unplanned descent to the floor or other lower surface, with or without injury, including a fall that staff did not see but that is found or reported.
Conditions that raise the chance of a fall, such as unsteady gait, weakness, cognitive impairment, certain medications, vision problems, urgency or incontinence, and unsafe footwear or surroundings.
A fall-related injury that needs treatment beyond first aid, such as suspected fracture, head injury, laceration needing sutures or any hospital transfer.

procedures: At admission and in the RN health care assessment completed within 14 days of admission when the initial assessment shows health care needs, the RN evaluates physical functioning (mobility, balance, transfers, use of devices) and cognition, and records fall history and fall risk (N.J.A.C. 8:36-7.2(c), (d)).
The RN adds a medication review: the RN notes medicines that may cause dizziness, drowsiness or low blood pressure, and reports concerns to the prescriber.

The RN writes fall-prevention interventions in the health service plan, such as assistive devices, supervised walking or transfers, toileting schedule, non-slip footwear, vision and hearing aids, hydration, lighting, bed or chair height and call-system access. Residents and designees are told of the plan and involved in choosing interventions.
Direct-care staff are informed of each high-risk resident and the interventions at shift report and through the assignment sheet.

Maintenance and housekeeping staff check hallways, stairs, lighting, floors, grab bars, handrails and outdoor walkways at least [FREQUENCY SET BY THE ADMINISTRATOR], clean up spills right away and report hazards. The Administrator ensures hazards are repaired promptly (DL-03).

When a fall occurs, staff do not move the resident until a nurse or trained staff member has checked for pain, deformity, head or neck injury and responsiveness. If a serious injury is suspected, staff call 911 and follow HLT-05.

The RN, or licensed nurse on duty, assesses the resident after the fall, including vital signs, injury check, pain and mental status. When the fall is unwitnessed or the head may have been struck, the RN sets a monitoring schedule and writes it in the record.

The RN notifies the physician of any fall with injury, any head strike, new confusion or other change, and any repeated falls. The RN records the orders. The RN or Administrator notifies the family, guardian or designee with the resident's consent.

Staff complete an incident report under SAF-02 before the end of the shift. If the fall causes serious injury, the Administrator reviews whether a State report is required (REC-02) and files it when it applies.

Within [TIME SET BY THE DIRECTOR OF NURSING] after a fall, the RN reviews what happened (time, place, activity, footwear, toileting, medications, environment), and updates the health service plan with new or changed interventions.

After a fall with injury, or two or more falls within [NUMBER OF DAYS SET BY THE DIRECTOR OF NURSING] days, the RN reassesses the resident under ADM-03, considers whether the resident's needs have changed, and informs the Administrator.

If falls continue despite reasonable interventions, the Administrator and RN document the facts and review whether the facility can meet the resident's needs under ADM-05. Residents are not moved without that process (ADM-06).

The Director of Nursing keeps a monthly falls log with resident, time, location, injury and interventions, and reports trends (such as time of day or location) to the quality improvement committee (GOV-06).
Fall-prevention and post-fall response training is part of orientation and annual in-service for all direct-care staff (STF-03).

responsibilities.duty: Assesses fall risk, writes interventions into the health service plan, assesses after falls, notifies the physician and updates the plan.
Carry out interventions, respond to falls without moving the resident prematurely, report and document.
Identify and correct environmental fall hazards.
Ensures hazards are fixed, files required reports and reviews fall trends.

documentation: Fall risk findings in the RN health care assessment
Fall-prevention interventions in the health service plan
Post-fall assessment note and monitoring record
Incident report and physician and family notification record
Monthly falls log
Quality improvement committee review

policies.title: Skin Integrity and Pressure Injury Management
policies.applies_to: All licensed program types (ALR, CPCH and ALP); nursing and direct-care staff
policies.purpose: To prevent pressure injuries, to find skin changes early, to treat them under RN direction, and to make retention decisions for residents with pressure sores in line with N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] prevents and manages skin breakdown through RN assessment and the health service plan. The RN documents a skin assessment at admission and whenever the resident's condition changes.
