procedures: The HR designee opens a personnel file on the date the offer is accepted, before the first day of work.
Each file contains the employee's full name, address and contact information, and the position and start date.
The file records previous employment (employer names, dates, position held, reason for leaving as reported) and the reference checks made.
The file records educational background, with a copy of the diploma or transcript or a signed statement from the employee when documents are not available, and any training course certificates.

The file contains copies of each credential: license or certification type, number, effective date and expiration date (for example nurse aide, PCA, CMA, RN, LPN). The credential type and date are also entered on the credential tracking log.
Verification of each credential is documented by the person who verified it, with date and source (registry, licensing board or issuing agency printout), and is kept in the file.
The file contains the results and dates of the criminal history background check and registry checks completed under STF-02, and for PCAs the updated check at each 2-year certification renewal.
The file contains the signed job description, acknowledged by the employee, with date. Any change in duties results in an updated job description.
The file contains the pre-employment and subsequent physical examinations, TB results and immunization records required by STF-04, kept in the confidential health section.
The file contains the orientation checklist and records of all in-service education, with dates, topics, presenter and length (STF-03), including dementia training and bloodborne pathogen training.

The file contains the job performance evaluation. A probationary evaluation is done within 90 days of hire, and then at least annually. The employee and supervisor sign each evaluation, and the employee may add a written comment.
The file contains signed acknowledgments of resident rights, confidentiality, abuse reporting duties and the staff conduct policy (STF-06), as well as signed acknowledgment of the Employee Handbook.
The file records any disciplinary action, any substantiated complaint and any corrective action.

The Administrator or designee audits every personnel file at least annually and every new-hire file within 30 days of hire using a personnel file checklist. Missing items are given a due date, and the Administrator is notified in writing of any file not complete within 30 days.

Personnel files are kept in a locked cabinet or in a password-protected electronic system with access limited to the Administrator, HR designee and others the Administrator authorizes. The confidential health section is restricted further.

Personnel files are available in the facility to DOH representatives at all times during surveys or investigations. The HR designee retrieves the requested files promptly and records which files were reviewed.

Files of former employees are kept for at least 7 years after separation, except that bloodborne pathogen exposure and vaccination records are kept as required by STF-04. The Administrator confirms the retention period against current law at the annual manual review.
Contract caregivers have a file with the contract, proof of credentials and verification, background check results, health records required by STF-04 and orientation records.

responsibilities.duty: Owns personnel records, audits files, controls access and presents files to DOH.
Opens and maintains files, enters credentials and expiration dates in the tracking log and follows up on missing items.
Provide accurate information and copies of credentials, and tell the HR designee of changes in name, address or certification status.

documentation: Personnel file checklist
Credential tracking log
Credential verification printouts
Signed job description
Orientation and in-service records
Physical examination, TB and immunization records (confidential section)
Performance evaluations
Background check and registry results

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, volunteers, students and contract staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set clear standards of conduct that protect residents from abuse, neglect, exploitation and boundary violations, and to make sure every staff member understands the personal and professional consequences of violations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] prohibits abuse, neglect and misappropriation of resident property by any staff member. A finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation triggers DOH review. A PCA may be entered on the PCA abuse registry after a disciplinary hearing (N.J.A.C. 8:36-9.1), and an administrator's certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted for improper practice, which includes a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property in any DOH-licensed facility or agency (N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.5). Staff may not borrow money or property from residents, accept gifts from residents or their families, or enter into financial dealings with residents. Staff must keep resident information confidential. All staff are mandatory reporters and must report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately, using the process in SAF-01 and the abuse and exploitation reporting policy required by N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7: DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770 and, for a resident age 60 or older, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995.

definitions.definition: Any willful act or omission that causes physical harm, pain, mental anguish, sexual contact, or unreasonable confinement, including verbal and emotional abuse.
Failure to provide the care, services, supervision or safety a resident needs.
Taking, using or misusing a resident's money, property or resources without consent or by deception, coercion or undue influence.
The limit that separates a caregiver's professional relationship from a personal, financial or romantic relationship with a resident.

procedures: At hire, each employee, volunteer and contract caregiver receives this policy, reviews it with the Administrator or designee and signs an acknowledgment filed in the personnel file (STF-05).
Orientation and annual in-service include examples of abuse, neglect, exploitation and boundary violations, resident rights and reporting duties (STF-03).
Staff treat residents with dignity, address them by their preferred name, knock before entering a resident's apartment or room, protect privacy during personal care and respect resident choices.
Staff do not use physical force, threats, intimidation, ridicule, profanity, or any form of punishment toward residents, and do not restrain or seclude a resident except as allowed by SAF-04.

Staff do not borrow money or property from residents, ask for or accept loans or gifts, tips, bequests or gratuities from residents or families, or serve as a resident's agent, executor, or witness to a will or financial document. Staff report any attempted gift to the Administrator, who documents it. Nominal food or cards shared with the whole staff may be accepted with the Administrator's approval.
Staff do not handle resident funds or valuables except through the process in RR-04, and do not use residents' credit cards, bank accounts, passwords or personal identification.

Staff do not enter into sexual or romantic relationships with residents, do not engage in sexual contact with a resident, and do not use social media or personal contact to maintain private relationships with residents or families.
Staff do not use resident property or take resident belongings, medications or food for their own use.

Staff do not share resident information with anyone who is not authorized, do not discuss residents in public areas and do not post photos or information about residents on social media. Violations of confidentiality are handled under RR-06.

Staff report to work free of alcohol, illegal drugs and any medication that impairs judgment, and report any arrest, charge or conviction to the Administrator within 24 hours or on the next business day.

Any staff member who sees or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation protects the resident immediately and reports to the Administrator or the person in charge at once. If the suspected perpetrator is the Administrator, or if staff are not satisfied the report is being acted on, staff may report directly to the DOH Complaints Program at 1-800-792-9770 and, for residents 60 or older, to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman at 1-877-582-6995. No staff member needs permission to report.

The Administrator or designee follows SAF-01 and, under N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.10, notifies the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by phone at (609) 633-9034 (or (609) 392-2020 after business hours), with written confirmation within 72 hours, when suspected abuse or exploitation is reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman.

The employee suspected of misconduct is removed from resident contact immediately pending investigation. Retaliation against anyone who reports in good faith is prohibited, and retaliation is itself grounds for termination.

The Administrator investigates promptly, documents findings and takes corrective action, up to termination. For PCAs and CMAs, the Administrator cooperates with the DOH review and any registry action under N.J.A.C. 8:36-9.1 and 9.2.

A staff member who violates this policy is subject to discipline, up to and including termination, and may be reported to the appropriate licensing board, registry and law enforcement. Disciplinary action is documented in the personnel file.
The Administrator reviews staff conduct complaints and trends quarterly in quality improvement meetings (GOV-06) and reviews this policy at least annually (GOV-05).

responsibilities.duty: Enforces this policy, investigates reports, removes suspected staff from duty, reports to DOH and the Ombudsman, and imposes discipline.
Follow the conduct standards, keep boundaries, protect confidentiality and report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.
Obtains signed acknowledgments and files discipline and investigation records.

documentation: Signed staff conduct acknowledgment
Orientation and in-service records
Gift/attempted gift log
Abuse, neglect and exploitation investigation reports
Disciplinary records in the personnel file
DOH and Ombudsman notification records

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications, Certification Renewal and Continuity
policies.applies_to: The Administrator and any person designated to act in the Administrator's absence
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is always led by an administrator who meets New Jersey qualifications, keeps the certificate current, and that DOH is told immediately if the Administrator leaves.
policies.policy: The Administrator of [AGENCY NAME] must be at least 21 years old, hold a high school diploma or equivalent, and hold a current New Jersey nursing home administrator license or a current New Jersey assisted living administrator certification (N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.2). A qualified owner may serve as administrator. A candidate sits the competency exam within two years of the training course and completes a criminal background check. The assisted living administrator certificate runs 3 years. Renewal requires at least 30 hours of continuing education on assisted living topics earned within the certificate period, plus a background check. An administrator's certificate may be revoked, suspended or restricted for improper practice, including a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property of a resident in an ALR, CPCH or ALP, or of a patient, resident or client of any other DOH-licensed facility or agency (N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.5). [AGENCY NAME] will report the termination of the administrator to the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by telephone, with the replacement's name and qualifications, and confirm in writing within 72 hours (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.10).

definitions.definition: The individual who holds a current NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification and is responsible for the day-to-day operation of the facility.
Education on assisted living topics earned within the certificate period, at least 30 hours for renewal.
A qualified employee named by the Administrator in writing to be in charge when the Administrator is not on site.
Conduct that can result in revocation, suspension or restriction of an administrator's certificate under N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.5.

procedures: Before hiring or appointing an administrator, the governing body verifies age and high school diploma or equivalent, and obtains a copy of the NJ nursing home administrator license or NJ assisted living administrator certification.

The governing body verifies the license or certificate directly with the DOH Certified Assisted Living Administrators office (609-633-9706) and keeps the dated verification in the personnel file (STF-05).

For a candidate who has taken the training course but not yet certified, the governing body confirms in writing that the competency exam will be taken within two years of the course and that the candidate has completed the criminal background check (STF-02). [AGENCY NAME] does not treat the candidate as a qualified administrator until the certification is issued.
If the owner will serve as administrator, the owner is held to every qualification in this policy and the personnel file is kept in the same manner as for any administrator.
The Administrator signs a job description that sets out duties under GOV-01, including day-to-day operations, compliance, staffing, resident protection and cooperation with DOH.
The credential tracking log shows the certificate number, issue date, expiration date and CE hours earned. The governing body reviews it each quarter.

The Administrator earns at least 30 hours of continuing education on assisted living topics within each 3-year certificate period and keeps certificates of attendance in the personnel file. The Administrator should plan to complete a minimum of 10 hours per year so that the requirement is not left to the end.

Renewal is started at least 180 days before the certificate expires. The Administrator submits the renewal, proof of CE and background check, and gives the governing body a copy of the filing and the renewed certificate.

The governing body names a qualified designee in writing, who is available to be in charge when the Administrator is absent, and posts the designee's name and phone number for staff. The governing body reviews the designation at least annually (see GOV-01).

If the Administrator is found to have committed abuse, neglect or misappropriation, or is subject to any DOH action against the certificate, the governing body removes the Administrator from resident-related duties pending review, appoints an interim, and cooperates with DOH under N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.5.

When the administrator's employment ends for any reason, the governing body or owner telephones the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately at (609) 633-9034, or at (609) 392-2020 after business hours.

Within 72 hours the governing body sends written confirmation to the Division stating the date and reason for termination and the replacement's name and qualifications (certificate or license number and expiration date). A copy is filed in the administrative records and the notice is logged on the required-reports log (REC-02).

The replacement administrator must meet all qualifications of N.J.A.C. 8:36-3.2. If a replacement has not been identified, the governing body names the person who will lead the facility on an interim basis, informs DOH of that person's qualifications and makes sure resident care and safety are not interrupted.
The outgoing administrator hands over keys, passwords, the policy manual, current incident files, survey results and plans of correction to the incoming administrator, who signs a handoff checklist.

The governing body updates the organizational chart, the posted information, and any notices that identify the Administrator, and notifies the NJ FamilyCare managed care organizations, residents and families of the change as appropriate (GOV-01, GOV-03).
The governing body reviews the Administrator's performance and compliance at least annually, including survey results, quality improvement outcomes, and CE and certificate status (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints a qualified administrator, verifies credentials, names a designee, and makes the immediate DOH report and 72-hour written confirmation when an administrator is terminated.
Maintains certification and CE, notifies the governing body of any action against the certificate, and keeps the facility in compliance.
Keeps the credential log and files verification, CE and renewal records.

documentation: Administrator license or certificate copy and DOH verification
Background check result
CE certificates and tracking log
Renewal filing and renewed certificate
Written designee appointment
DOH telephone report log and 72-hour written confirmation of administrator termination
Handoff checklist
Updated organizational chart

policies.title: Resident Records, Confidentiality and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, store or release resident records, in paper or electronic form
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, accurate and confidential record for each resident, make it available to authorized persons and to DOH, keep it for the required period, and document a resident's death as required.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for every resident that follows the health record requirements of N.J.A.C. 8:36 Subchapter 15, which cover the health record, its availability, confidentiality, retention, the resident register, individual records and the record of death. The manual must include policies on the confidentiality and release of records, and on staff responsibility for prompt notification of a resident's death as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a) (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7(a)). Each resident record contains the admission interview, the physician statement, the RN assessment, the health service plan, notices and incident reports, along with the other items listed below. Records are kept confidential and are released only as RR-06 allows. Records are available to DOH representatives on request. [AGENCY NAME] keeps records for at least ten (10) years after a resident's discharge or death, or for any longer period required by DOH, a payer, or other law. Because the retention period and section number must be confirmed against the code, the Administrator verifies them against the current text of N.J.A.C. 8:36 Subchapter 15 at each annual manual review (GOV-05) and amends this policy if the code states a different period. Records are protected under HIPAA documentation and security standards (45 CFR 164.530(j) and 164.316).

definitions.definition: The complete paper or electronic collection of information about a resident, from pre-admission through discharge or death.
A chronological list of admissions, discharges, transfers and deaths kept by the facility.
The person designated by the Administrator to control storage, access, release and retention of records.
Documentation of a resident's death and of the notifications made, kept in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7 and N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e.

procedures: The Administrator designates a record custodian and an alternate in writing, and lists them on the organizational chart or in the records plan.
On the day of admission, the custodian opens a record for the resident and enters the resident in the resident register with the date of admission.

Each record contains, at a minimum: the admission interview (ADM-01), the physician statement and orders, the RN assessment (ADM-03) and later reassessments, the health service plan (ADM-04) with any managed risk agreement, the admission agreement and disclosures (RR-03), advance directive information (RR-05), medication records (HLT-02, HLT-03), progress and change of condition notes (HLT-05), notices to the resident or representative, incident reports (SAF-02), discharge or transfer notices (ADM-06) and, where applicable, the death record.

Each entry is legible, dated, timed and signed or electronically authenticated by the author with name and title. Entries are never erased or altered. A correction is made by drawing a single line through the error, writing the correction and initialing and dating it. Late entries are labeled as late.

Active records are kept in a locked cabinet or room, or in an electronic system with unique user IDs, role-based access, automatic log-off, and an audit log. Only staff who need the information to do their jobs may access a record.

Staff keep records out of public view, do not leave charts unattended or open in common areas, do not discuss residents in public areas and do not photograph records or resident information on personal devices.
Records are available in the facility for review by DOH representatives at all times. The custodian retrieves the requested records promptly and logs the date and the records provided.

A resident or authorized representative may request to see or receive a copy of the resident's record. The custodian processes the request under RR-06, with the Administrator's approval, within the time allowed by law and notes the request in the record.

Records are released to third parties only with the resident's or representative's written authorization or as required or allowed by law, as described in RR-06. Each release is logged with date, recipient, what was released and staff name.

Electronic records are backed up at least daily to a secure location, backups are tested at least quarterly, and a written downtime procedure is available so resident information is accessible when systems are down. This meets the security safeguards in 45 CFR 164.316.

When a resident dies, the staff member on duty follows HLT-10: notifies the physician, the resident's representative and others as required, makes the prompt notification of death that N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a) require, and records the date, time and persons notified in the resident record. The custodian enters the death in the resident register.

When a resident is discharged, transferred or dies, the custodian completes the record within 14 days, makes sure all entries and signatures are in place, and moves the record to inactive storage. The discharge date is entered in the register.

Inactive records are stored in a secure, fire-resistant and moisture-protected location, indexed by resident name and discharge date, for at least ten (10) years after discharge or death, or longer where required by law, DOH or a payer, including NJ FamilyCare MLTSS managed care organizations. The Administrator confirms the period against the code at each annual review.
HIPAA policies, procedures and required documentation are kept for six years from the date created or last in effect, as required by 45 CFR 164.530(j) and 164.316.

Records destroyed after the retention period are shredded or permanently deleted. The custodian keeps a destruction log with resident identifiers, date of destruction and method, and the Administrator approves each destruction before it happens.

If [AGENCY NAME] closes or changes ownership, the Administrator and owner arrange for continued custody and access to all records in line with GOV-03 and notify residents and former residents how to obtain their records.
Staff who access or disclose records improperly are subject to discipline, and the Administrator handles any breach under RR-06.
The record custodian audits a sample of open and closed records each quarter for completeness, timeliness and confidentiality, and reports findings to the quality improvement committee (GOV-06).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the record custodian, approves release and destruction, ensures DOH access and verifies retention periods annually.
Opens, maintains, secures, releases, stores and destroys records according to this policy and logs all releases.

policies.title: Required Reports and Submissions to the State
policies.applies_to: All [AGENCY NAME] license types: Assisted Living Residence (ALR), Comprehensive Personal Care Home (CPCH) and Assisted Living Program (ALP). The CPCH SSI reporting provisions apply to CPCH only.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] sends every report, notice and document that the New Jersey Department of Health (DOH) requires, on time, to the correct office, with a record of what was sent and when.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets all State reporting and submission duties under N.J.A.C. 8:36. The Administrator is responsible for this policy and keeps a written State Reporting Calendar and a Submission Log. (1) Annual resident-day report: by April 15 of each year the facility reports resident days for the prior calendar year to the Certificate of Need and Licensing (CN&L) Program (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.4). (2) Documents on request: when asked, the facility submits in writing any document N.J.A.C. 8:36 requires to the Director of the CN&L Program, and submits utilization, demographic, cost, charge and staffing data when DOH requests it (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.4). (3) Reportable events: the facility telephones the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately, at (609) 633-9034 or (609) 392-2020 after business hours, and sends written confirmation to the Division within 72 hours. This applies to termination of the administrator (with the replacement's name and qualifications), any elopement, and suspected resident abuse or exploitation reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.10). (4) Emergency plans: the facility files its emergency plan with DOH and notifies DOH of changes to it. (5) Change of ownership: the prospective new owner applies to the CN&L Program before ownership is transferred. The follow-up documents are due within 5 working days after the transaction closes, and the rule fee is $1,500 (N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.3). (6) New or expanded buildings: plans are approved by the Department of Community Affairs (DCA) Health Care Plan Review Unit before construction. Before occupancy the facility submits the local certificate of occupancy to the Unit and the further required items to the CN&L Program (N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.3). (7) CPCH only: the facility computes the SSI-eligible percentage on resident days per calendar year and reports it to the CN&L Program by April 15 for the prior year. Each CPCH must have at least 5% of residents SSI-eligible each year, and at least half of those residents must be former psychiatric patients (N.J.A.C. 8:36-22.7). No report is late, incomplete or estimated without the Administrator's sign-off. A missed or doubtful deadline is escalated to the Governing Body (GOV-01) and handled as a quality issue (GOV-06).

definitions.definition: The DOH Certificate of Need and Licensing Program, which handles licence applications, renewals, changes of ownership and annual data reports.
The DOH Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations, which receives reportable-event calls and written confirmations and conducts surveys and complaint investigations.

An event that must be telephoned immediately to the Division and confirmed in writing within 72 hours: administrator termination, any elopement, and suspected abuse or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman.
The total number of days of care provided to residents in a calendar year, counted from the facility's daily census records.
A CPCH resident who is eligible for Supplemental Security Income. At least half of the required SSI-eligible residents must be former psychiatric patients.
The DCA unit that approves construction plans before building and receives the local certificate of occupancy before a new or renovated building is occupied.
Business hours are the Division's regular working hours. At any other time, staff use the after-hours number, (609) 392-2020.

procedures: Annual calendar: by January 15 each year the Administrator updates the State Reporting Calendar. It lists the April 15 resident-day report, the April 15 CPCH SSI report (CPCH only), licence renewal and biennial inspection fee dates, the annual emergency plan review, and the Administrator's certificate renewal date (see STF-07). The calendar gives each item an owner and a due date set 14 days before the deadline.

Resident-day data: the Business Office Manager keeps a daily census log. It records residents by payer (private pay, NJ FamilyCare MLTSS and, for CPCH, SSI-eligible status). It reconciles the log with billing records each month and the Administrator initials the reconciliation.

Annual resident-day report: by March 15 the Business Office Manager totals resident days for the prior calendar year. The Administrator reviews the figures against the census and billing records and signs the report.

Submission of the resident-day report: the Administrator submits the signed report to the CN&L Program in writing by April 15 and saves a copy of the report, proof of delivery and date in the Submission Log.

CPCH SSI report (CPCH only): by March 15 the Business Office Manager computes the SSI-eligible percentage on resident days for the calendar year and the number of SSI-eligible former psychiatric patients. The Administrator checks that the facility meets the 5% minimum and the half-former-psychiatric-patient requirement. Any shortfall is reported to the Governing Body and addressed under ADM-02. The report goes to the CN&L Program by April 15.

Requests for documents or data: any staff member who receives a DOH request for documents, utilization, demographic, cost, charge or staffing data gives it to the Administrator the same business day. The Administrator logs the request, due date and assigned preparer.

Preparing a response: the preparer collects only what was requested, from source records such as the census, billing and payroll or schedules. The Administrator checks accuracy and signs the cover letter.

Sending a response: the Administrator submits the response in writing to the Director of the CN&L Program, or to the DOH office that made the request, by the date given. The Administrator records the submission date and method in the Submission Log and keeps a complete copy.

Reportable-event call: when an administrator termination, an elopement, or suspected abuse or exploitation reported to the State LTC Ombudsman occurs, the Administrator, or the senior manager on duty if the Administrator is unavailable, telephones the Division immediately. The number is (609) 633-9034 during business hours and (609) 392-2020 after hours. The caller records the date, time, person spoken to and what was reported.

Written confirmation: within 72 hours of the event the Administrator sends written confirmation to the Division. It includes the facts known, residents involved (by initials or record number as appropriate), actions taken, and for an administrator termination the replacement's name and qualifications.

Linked reports: elopements are handled under SAF-03 and abuse or exploitation under SAF-01 and RR-02. Other incident reporting is handled under SAF-02. Making the State report does not replace those policies' steps for resident safety, family or physician notification, and investigation.

Administrator change: if the Administrator is terminated, the Governing Body makes sure the replacement meets the qualifications in STF-07 and that the Division report includes the replacement's name and qualifications. A replacement is in place so there is no gap in leadership.

Emergency plan filing: after each annual review, and whenever the plan changes, the Administrator files the current emergency plan with DOH and notifies DOH of the change (see SAF-05). The Administrator records the filing date in the Submission Log.

Change of ownership: before any transfer of ownership is closed, the prospective new owner applies to the CN&L Program. When DOH sends its approval letter with licensure forms and fee request, the Governing Body completes the forms and pays the fee ($1,500 rule fee). The owners do not close until DOH approval is received (see GOV-03).

After closing a transfer: within 5 working days after the transaction closes, the new owner submits the required follow-up documents to the CN&L Program. The Administrator or designee keeps proof of delivery in the Submission Log.

New construction or expansion: before construction the owner obtains approval of plans from the DCA Health Care Plan Review Unit and keeps the Unit's written final release for the licence application. Before anyone occupies a new or renovated building, the Administrator submits the local certificate of occupancy to the Unit and the further required items to the CN&L Program (see GOV-04).

Monthly check: on the first business day of each month the Administrator reviews the State Reporting Calendar and Submission Log, confirms no item is overdue, and notes any open item in the monthly management report to the Governing Body.

Late or missed items: if a report or submission is late or incomplete, the Administrator submits it as soon as possible, tells the Governing Body, and opens a corrective action in the QI program (GOV-06) to find and fix the cause.
Annual review: the Administrator reviews this policy each year with the Policy and Procedure Manual review (GOV-05) and updates telephone numbers, addresses and requirements if DOH changes them.

responsibilities.duty: Makes sure resources and staff are available to meet State reporting duties, reviews monthly reports of overdue items, and approves ownership, construction and Administrator-change submissions.

Owns this policy. Keeps the State Reporting Calendar and Submission Log, signs and submits all reports, makes or oversees reportable-event calls and written confirmations, and files emergency plan updates.
Keeps the daily census and payer log, prepares resident-day and (CPCH) SSI figures, and reconciles them with billing each month.

Submission Log: item, date due, date sent, method, sender and location of the copy.
Annual resident-day report signed by the Administrator, with proof of delivery to the CN&L Program.

documents.title: AAS-24 Affidavit of Compliance, Assisted Living Residences, Comprehensive Personal Care Homes and Assisted Living Programs
documents.issuer: NJ Department of Health, Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations
documents.version: Undated. I saw only a search excerpt and could not fetch the full form.

required_items.text: A policy and procedure manual(s) for the organization and operation of the facility or program shall be developed, implemented, and reviewed at least annually. Each review of the manual(s) shall be documented, and the manual(s) shall be available in the facility or program to representatives of the Department at all times. The manual(s) shall include at least the following:
An organizational chart delineating the lines of authority, responsibility, and accountability for the administration and resident care services of the facility or program;
A description of the services which the assisted living residence, comprehensive personal care home or assisted living program is capable of providing;
Policies and procedures for maintaining security;

Policies and procedures for reporting all alleged and/or suspected cases of resident abuse or exploitation to the Complaints Program of the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations at 1-800-792-9770. If the resident is 60 years of age or older, the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman shall also be notified, in compliance with N.J.S.A. 52:27G-7.1 et seq., at 1-877-582-6995;

Policies and procedures for maintaining confidentiality of resident records, including policies and procedures for examination of resident records by the resident and other authorized persons and for release of resident records to any individual outside the facility or program, as consented to by the resident or as required by law or third-party payor;

Policies and procedures for the maintenance of personnel records for each employee, including at least his or her name, previous employment, educational background, credentials, license number with effective date and date of expiration (if applicable), certification (if applicable), verification of credentials, records of physical examinations, job description, records of orientation and inservice education, and evaluation of job performance;

Policies and procedures, including content and frequency, for physical examinations and immunizations and tuberculin testing upon employment and subsequently for employees and individuals providing direct resident care services in the facility through contractual arrangements or written agreement; and

Policies and procedures delineating the responsibilities of the facility's staff in making prompt notification regarding the death of a resident as required by N.J.S.A. 26:2H-5e and N.J.A.C. 8:36-15.7(a).

The facility shall have a policy and procedure that addresses how policy and procedure manuals will be made available to residents, guardians, designated responsible individuals, prospective applicants, and referring agencies.

A policy and procedure manual(s) for the organization and operation of the assisted living program shall be developed, implemented and reviewed in accordance with the provisions of N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.7. The manual(s) shall be available in all assisted living program sites, the assisted living program provider main office, and to representatives of the Department. (Assisted living programs only.)

Written resident care policies and procedures shall be established, implemented, and reviewed at intervals specified in the policies and procedures. Each review of the policies and procedures shall be documented. Policies and procedures shall include, but not be limited to, the following: 1.-11. [I could not retrieve the full text of items 1-7 and 9-11; see notes. The readoption notice confirms only item 8, below.]
The control of smoking in the facility, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:3D-55 et seq. and N.J.A.C. 8:6;

A copy of the assisted living residence or comprehensive personal care home admission agreement or other document stating the scope of a facility's services shall be forwarded to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program for review when application for licensure is made. [Does not apply to a CCRC's continuing care agreement.] The admission agreement shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
Proposed charges for room, board and all levels of service and care and for all additional services and care not included in the standard package of rates in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.2;

Specification of how and when the resident will be notified of any change in charges, and a statement that each resident has the right to request written justification of any increase in charges in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.2;
A statement that each resident has the right to appeal an involuntary discharge as specified at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.14(b); and

Specification of the criteria identified at N.J.A.C. 8:36-5.1(d) which will be used to discharge residents and an explanation of how the discharge process will be implemented, including which facility staff will participate and the extent of resident participation.
An evaluation of any requested waivers to licensing requirements that are sought in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.7;
A description of how the architectural design will promote the essential values of assisted living, including privacy, choice, independence, dignity and a home-like environment;
A description of how the physical plant will facilitate the care of residents with common long-term care problems, such as reduced mobility, incontinence and dementia; and

A statement of the proposed licensed operator's commitment to assuring access to assisted living for individuals with nursing home level of care needs, as defined in N.J.A.C. 8:36-1.3. This statement shall indicate that within 36 months after licensure, at least 20 percent of the facility's residents shall be individuals with nursing home-level of care needs. This percentage shall be computed based on the number of resident days per calendar year and may include direct admissions as well as maintained residents with nursing home-level of care needs.

If an applicant is required to submit plans under N.J.A.C. 8:36-2.3, the applicant shall submit a description of how the location of the proposed facility will promote the physical integration or social connection of the residents into a neighborhood, center or other area with existing services or amenities.

For assisted living programs, the application shall include a copy of the written agreement or contract between the program provider and residents that will be used at each program site, including clearly addressing N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.3(d). [Also 2.2(l)1: a copy of the written contract between the program provider and the publicly subsidized housing unit in accordance with N.J.A.C. 8:36-23.2(c).]

Each assisted living provider shall post and distribute a statement of resident rights for all residents of assisted living residences, comprehensive personal care homes, and assisted living programs. [Items 1-42 are the rights listed in the rule. Two items are quoted below.]

The right to receive written notice at least 30 days in advance when the facility requests the resident's transfer or discharge, except in an emergency. This written notice shall include the name, address, and telephone number of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and shall also be provided to the resident's legally appointed guardian, if applicable, or, with the resident's consent, to the resident's family, 30 days in advance;

The right to voice complaints without being threatened or punished. Each resident is entitled to complain and present his or her grievances to the administrator and staff, to government agencies, and to anyone else without fear of interference, discharge, or reprisal. The facility shall provide each resident and his or her legally appointed guardian, if applicable, and the resident's family member with the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the government agencies to which a resident can complain and ask questions, including the Department and the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman. These names, addresses, and telephone numbers shall also be posted in a conspicuous place in the facility;

The facility shall notify the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations immediately by telephone at (609) 633-9034 or (609) 392-2020 if after business hours, followed within 72 hours by written confirmation, of the following: [items 1-3; item 3 is any suspected cases of resident abuse or exploitation which have been reported to the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman]. (Assisted living programs: see 23.17(b).)

Any theft of Scheduled or Controlled Substances shall be reported to the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety, Enforcement Bureau of Professional Boards at (973) 648-4742, and/or to any other municipal, county, State, or Federal authority having jurisdiction over theft of such substances.

The facility shall develop written emergency plans, policies, and procedures which shall include plans and procedures to be followed in case of medical emergencies, power failures, fire, and natural disasters. The emergency plans shall be filed with the Department and the Department shall be notified when the plans are changed. Procedures for emergencies shall specify persons to be notified, process of notification and verification of notification, locations of emergency equipment and alarm signals, evacuation routes, procedures for evacuating residents, procedures for reentry and recovery, frequency of fire drills, tasks and responsibilities assigned to all personnel, and shall specify medications and records to be taken from the facility upon evacuation and to be returned following the emergency. [Paraphrased from a third-party transcription (alfboss.com). Subsection letters were not captured. Verify against the official text.]

Written policies and procedures shall be established and implemented regarding infection prevention and control, including, but not limited to, policies and procedures for the following: 1.-7. [not retrieved; see notes]
Needles and syringes used by residents as part of home self-care shall be disposed of in accordance with N.J.S.A. 2C:36-6.1 and N.J.A.C. 8:43E-7, and amendments thereto.

A facility that advertises or holds itself out as having an Alzheimer's disease or dementia program shall provide training in specialized care of residents who are diagnosed by a physician as having Alzheimer's disease or dementia to all licensed and unlicensed staff who provide direct care to residents with Alzheimer's or dementia, in accordance with N.J.S.A. 26:2M-7.2. (Applies only to facilities that advertise such a program.)

The assisted living residence and/or the comprehensive personal care home shall establish and maintain written contracts detailing all policies, procedures, and services to be provided by the licensed facility and the licensed program. (Assisted living programs only.)

official.notes: I found no single NJ DOH policy-review checklist or application packet for this license. The required content comes from the N.J.A.C. 8:36 sections listed above. Reviewers should treat § 5.7(a)(1)-(8) and (b) as the core manual list. It applies to ALRs, CPCHs and ALPs, and the manual may be one document or several. The manual must be developed, implemented and reviewed at least annually. Each review must be documented, and the manual must be available at the facility or program for Department representatives at all times. An ALP must also keep it at every program site and at the provider's main office (§ 23.4). The Department states the manual should be available to residents, guardians and referring agencies under a written policy (§ 5.7(b)). With the license application, the ALR or CPCH admission agreement goes to the Director of the Certificate of Need and Licensing Program for review (§ 2.2(c)). An ALP submits its resident agreement and its contract with the publicly subsidized housing unit (§ 2.2(l)). Written emergency plans must be filed with the Department, and the Department must be told when they change (§ 14.2, per a secondary source). A preliminary conference with the CN&L Program is optional (§ 2.2(n)). Survey by the Division of Health Facility Survey and Field Operations follows application approval and precedes licensure and admission of residents (§ 2.4). The Department publishes an Affidavit of Compliance (AAS-24) that cites the chapter's mandatory standards, including § 6.1(a)(1)-(11). Gaps and cautions: (1) I could not retrieve the verbatim lists in § 6.1(a)(1)-(7) and (9)-(11) or § 18.3(a)(1)-(7). Pull them from the Cornell LII pages for N.J.A.C. 8:36-6.1 and 8:36-18.3 before using them. (2) The § 14.2 text is from a non-official transcription and should be checked against the official text. (3) I did not review §§ 7.1, 10.x, 11.x, 20.x or 21.x for further written-policy requirements, such as respite care policies, restraint policy, quality improvement and dining. A complete checklist should add them. (4) Excluded as non-policy content: fees, track-record evaluation, physical plant and bed-count description (§ 2.2(e)1-3), plan review, certificate of occupancy, and local approvals. (5) The 2026 proposed rule changes to §§ 1.3 and 2.4 (CPCH deemed status) have not been verified as adopted.
